french: Les paroles de la Reine-sorcière sont pleines de bon sens. Un toast pour Seridia !
russian: Слышала? Прямо из уст Королевы-ведьмы. Выпьем же, Серидия.
bulgarian: From the Witch Queen's lips to your ear! Cheers to that, Seridia.

english: Oh, you two! Cheers.
french: Merci à vous deux... Santé !
russian: Ох, девочки! Выпьем.
bulgarian: Oh, you two! Cheers.

english: I think it often, but it bears saying out loud...
french: J'y pense souvent, mais il faut parfois dire les choses à haute voix...
russian: Я часто об этом думаю, но стоит высказать вслух...
bulgarian: I think it often, but it bears saying out loud...

english: I... have not...
french: Non... Jamais...
russian: Я... не думала...
bulgarian: I... have not...

english: Nor I...
french: Moi non plus...
russian: Я тоже...
bulgarian: Nor I...

english: Yeah... Probably not a good idea.
french: Ouais... Ce n'est sûrement pas une bonne idée.
russian: Ну да... Наверное, не самая лучшая идея.
bulgarian: Yeah... Probably not a good idea.

english: Ever thought about putting fish in the fountain?
french: Tu as déjà songé à mettre des poissons dans la fontaine ?
russian: Вы не думали запустить в наш фонтан рыбу?
bulgarian: Ever thought about putting fish in the fountain?

english: Awww thank you! The cream I used is from Hayden's farm.
french: Oh, merci ! La crème que j'ai ajoutée vient de la ferme d'Hayden.
russian: О, спасибо! Сливки я брала с фермы Хейдена.
bulgarian: Awww thank you! The cream I used is from Hayden's farm.

english: I'll be sure to pass along your compliment to the girls, Adeline!
french: Je féliciterai mes protégées de ta part, Adeline !
russian: Я передам твой комплимент коровам, Аделина!
bulgarian: I'll be sure to pass along your compliment to the girls, Adeline!

english: Today's soup is delicious, Reina!
french: La soupe du jour est excellente, Reina !
russian: Отличный сегодня суп, Рейна!
bulgarian: Today's soup is delicious, Reina!

english: Biodiversity, he said.
french: La « biodiversité », il me semble.
russian: «Биоразнообразие».
bulgarian: Biodiversity, he said.

english: He sure knows his stuff! You too, Terithia. I'm comfortable saying I know a good deal about farm animals, but most fish look the same to me.
french: Il sait de quoi il parle ! Toi aussi, Terithia. Je peux me vanter d'en connaître un rayon sur les animaux de la ferme, mais pour moi, tous les poissons se ressemblent.
russian: Да, он у нас эрудит! Да и ты тоже, Теризия. Я не постесняюсь сказать, что про своих животных на ферме знаю немало. А вот рыбы для меня все на одно лицо.
bulgarian: He sure knows his stuff! You too, Terithia. I'm comfortable saying I know a good deal about farm animals, but most fish look the same to me.

english: You're quite knowledgeable too, Hayden. But I'll have you both know, I'm the resident expert on what animals are cutest.
french: Tu t'y connais toi aussi, Hayden. En revanche, sachez qu'ici, je suis la seule experte capable de juger quels animaux sont les plus mignons.
russian: Ты тоже весьма образованный, Хейден. Но я вам заявляю, что по самым милым зверушкам авторитет здесь я.
bulgarian: You're quite knowledgeable too, Hayden. But I'll have you both know, I'm the resident expert on what animals are cutest.

english: Luc used a fancy word the other day, to describe all the different fish around Mistria.
french: Luc a utilisé un drôle de mot savant l'autre jour, pour décrire toutes les sortes de poissons de Mistria.
russian: Люк недавно сказал умное словечко, когда говорил про разных рыб, которые водятся у нас в Мистрии.
bulgarian: Luc used a fancy word the other day, to describe all the different fish around Mistria.

english: We've got a happy equilibrium going on at the Inn. And Olric is working out great as a part-timer!
french: L'auberge tourne très bien. Et Olric s'en tire très bien à mi-temps !
russian: Мы в трактире отлично справляемся вместе. А из Ольрика вышел хороший подмастерье.
bulgarian: We've got a happy equilibrium going on at the Inn. And Olric is working out great as a part-timer!

english: Maybe I should have a chat with him! We always get stretched a bit thin at the end of the week, when Nora turns her attention to the Saturday Market.
french: Je devrais peut-être lui parler ! On est souvent à court de main-d'œuvre le week-end, quand Nora s'occupe du marché du samedi.
russian: Может, мне тоже с ним потолковать? Нора в конце недели готовится к Субботнему базару, и у нас часто не хватает рук.
bulgarian: Maybe I should have a chat with him! We always get stretched a bit thin at the end of the week, when Nora turns her attention to the Saturday Market.

english: How are things looking? Do you have everything you need?
french: Comment vont les affaires ? Vous avez tout ce qu'il te faut ?
russian: Как ваша работа? У вас есть всё, что нужно?
bulgarian: How are things looking? Do you have everything you need?

english: Hemlock's been sourcing new wines through Balor lately, but I think that's their little side project.
french: Hemlock se fournit en nouveaux crus auprès de Balor, mais je crois que c'est leur chasse gardée.
russian: Хемлок недавно стал заказывать вина через Балора, но это их небольшое стороннее дельце.
bulgarian: Hemlock's been sourcing new wines through Balor lately, but I think that's their little side project.

english: Wine, you say? Maybe I should start my own side project!
french: Du vin ? Je devrais faire ça, moi aussi !
russian: Ах, у них там вина? Может, мне тоже пора организовать стороннее дельце!
bulgarian: Wine, you say? Maybe I should start my own side project!

english: Is there anything the Inn or General Store need? Just say the word!
french: Il vous manque quelque chose à l'auberge ou au magasin général ? Vous n'avez qu'à le dire.
russian: В трактире и в универмаге всего хватает? Скажите, если что не так.
bulgarian: Is there anything the Inn or General Store need? Just say the word!

english: Oh Adeline, you do more than enough! The best thing you could do is come and enjoy yourself.
french: Adeline, tu en fais déjà bien assez ! Tout ce que je te demande, c'est que tu viennes te détendre.
russian: Ох, Аделина, ты и так достаточно помогаешь! Лучше просто приходи и проведи вечер с нами.
bulgarian: Oh Adeline, you do more than enough! The best thing you could do is come and enjoy yourself.

english: And remember, no clipboards allowed!
french: Et n'oublie pas que les blocs-notes sont interdits !
russian: С документами не пустим, так и знай!
bulgarian: And remember, no clipboards allowed!

english: Friday nights have been so busy at the Inn lately! I've got a few proposals of how I could help-
french: Il y a beaucoup de monde à l'auberge le vendredi soir, ces derniers temps ! J'ai quelques idées pour aider...
russian: По пятницам в тратире так много народу! У меня есть предложение: я могла бы...
bulgarian: Friday nights have been so busy at the Inn lately! I've got a few proposals of how I could help-

english: Oh, it's been good! And busy as ever, with Reina in the kitchen and Balor turning his room into a makeshift office.
french: Oui, très bien ! Entre Reina qui cuisine et Balor qui a transformé sa chambre en bureau de fortune, on ne chôme pas.
russian: Да всё отлично! Кругом кипит работа: Рейна хозяйничает на кухне, а Балор решил превратить свой номер в офис.
bulgarian: Oh, it's been good! And busy as ever, with Reina in the kitchen and Balor turning his room into a makeshift office.

english: The General Store's been bustling, too. Mistria's come a long way since the earthquake!
french: Les affaires marchent aussi du tonnerre au magasin général. Il y a un monde entre la Mistria après le tremblement de terre et la Mistria d'aujourd'hui !
russian: И универмаг стал такой оживлённый! После землетрясения Мистрия прошла большой путь!
bulgarian: The General Store's been bustling, too. Mistria's come a long way since the earthquake!

english: How are things going at the Inn, Josephine?
french: Tout se passe bien à l'auberge, Joséphine ?
russian: Джозефина, как дела в трактире?
bulgarian: How are things going at the Inn, Josephine?

english: Of course! Not saying that I couldn't do it, but that's my nephew's name on the dotted line, so I'll pass it on to him!
french: Oui, promis ! Je pourrais encore m'en charger, mais c'est le nom de mon neveu qui est inscrit, alors je vais la lui transmettre !
russian: Нет уж! Конечно, я бы и сам справился, но лучше пускай племянник старается, нарабатывает репутацию.
bulgarian: Of course! Not saying that I couldn't do it, but that's my nephew's name on the dotted line, so I'll pass it on to him!

english: Besides, between you and me, I think he's a bit quicker than I was at his age. You're lucky to have him!
french: Et puis, entre nous, je crois qu'il est un peu plus rapide que je ne l'étais à son âge. Tu as de la chance de l'avoir !
russian: К тому же, между нами, у него работа идёт чуть быстрее, чем у меня в его годы. Вам с ним повезло!
bulgarian: Besides, between you and me, I think he's a bit quicker than I was at his age. You're lucky to have him!

english: So you'll pass this work order on to Ryis? You won't try to fill it yourself?
french: Tu me promets de transmettre cette commande à Ryis ? Et de ne pas t'en occuper toi-même ?
russian: Так что, Ланден, отдашь заказ Ризу? Сам не хочешь попробовать?
bulgarian: So you'll pass this work order on to Ryis? You won't try to fill it yourself?

english: They look okay... Lady Adeline, when do we do the real royal stuff? Like in my stories?
french: Ça va... Dame Adeline, quand est-ce qu'on va faire des trucs de princesse ? Comme dans les contes ?
russian: Вроде всё хорошо... Но, леди Аделина, когда будут настоящие королевские дела? Как у меня в книгах?
bulgarian: They look okay... Lady Adeline, when do we do the real royal stuff? Like in my stories?

english: This is the real royal stuff, Maple. A good leader works hard!
french: Mais c'est le travail d'une princesse, Maple. Régner, ce n'est pas de tout repos !
russian: Это и есть королевские дела, Мэйпл. Хорошие правители много работают!
bulgarian: This is the real royal stuff, Maple. A good leader works hard!

english: Sure, but what about our political machinations against neighboring fiefdoms?
french: Oui, mais les complots contre les royaumes voisins ?
russian: Да, но когда же будут политические интриги против окружающих феодалов?
bulgarian: Sure, but what about our political machinations against neighboring fiefdoms?

english: Are you done reviewing my books, Maple? How do they look to you?
french: As-tu fini d'éplucher mes livres de comptes, Maple ? Qu'en penses-tu ?
russian: Ну что, проверила счета, Мэйпл? Там всё в порядке?
bulgarian: Are you done reviewing my books, Maple? How do they look to you?

english: Um... Maple... I don't have anything like that...
french: Euh... Maple... je n'ai rien de ce genre...
russian: Эээ... Мэйпл... у меня нет никакого агентства...
bulgarian: Um... Maple... I don't have anything like that...

english: Right... that's what we want them to think!
french: Je vois... C'est ce qu'on doit leur faire croire !
russian: Ах да, конечно... Вслух про него не говорим!
bulgarian: Right... that's what we want them to think!

english: I think the best way to check up on townsfolk would be to use your royal spy network!
french: Le meilleur moyen de savoir comment vont les habitants, ce serait d'utiliser votre réseau d'espions royaux !
russian: По-моему, узнавать, как у всех дела, лучше всего с помощью королевского шпионского агентства!
bulgarian: I think the best way to check up on townsfolk would be to use your royal spy network!

english: We're getting by just fine.
french: Non, on s'en sort bien comme ça.
russian: Мы и сами отлично справляемся.
bulgarian: We're getting by just fine.

english: Olric said I should remind you that you're not taking away resources from anyone else.
french: Olric m'a dit de te rappeler que ça ne serait pas au détriment d'autres personnes.
russian: Ольрик просил тебе напомнить, чтобы ты не брал материалы, предназначенные другим.
bulgarian: Olric said I should remind you that you're not taking away resources from anyone else.

english: He also said I should ask you twice if I want an honest answer.
french: Il m'a aussi dit de te reposer la question si je voulais une vraie réponse.
russian: А ещё он сказал, что тебя надо спрашивать дважды, чтобы получить честный ответ.
bulgarian: He also said I should ask you twice if I want an honest answer.

english: Fine... I could always use some more ore.
french: Bon, d'accord... À vrai dire, j'aurais besoin de plus de minerais.
russian: Ладно... Ещё немного руды нам всегда пригодится.
bulgarian: Fine... I could always use some more ore.

english: Also, don't listen to Olric.
french: Mais surtout, n'écoutez pas Olric.
russian: А вообще-то, поменьше слушай Ольрика.
bulgarian: Also, don't listen to Olric.

english: Does the forge need any extra resources from the town, March?
french: Veux-tu que la ville alloue plus de ressources à la forge, March ?
russian: Скажи, Март, от кузницы будут какие-нибудь заказы из города?
bulgarian: Does the forge need any extra resources from the town, March?

english: Ah... my old friends, "nails".
french: Ah, mes vieux copains... les clous.
russian: А, снова старые друзья, гвозди...
bulgarian: Ah... my old friends, "nails".

english: I'll get started right away.
french: Je m'y mets tout de suite.
russian: Возьмусь за работу немедленно.
bulgarian: I'll get started right away.

english: Here's a list of projects we're starting the new year with!
french: Voici la liste des projets pour bien démarrer l'année !
russian: Я приготовила список задач на грядущий год.
bulgarian: Here's a list of projects we're starting the new year with!

english: You two okay with all the orders I'm sending your way?
french: Vous vous en sortez avec toutes les commandes que je vous envoie ?
russian: Вы справляетесь с заказами, которые я вам присылаю?
bulgarian: You two okay with all the orders I'm sending your way?

english: If anyone can handle it, it's March!
french: March est sur le pont !
russian: Уж кому это по силам — так точно Марту!
bulgarian: If anyone can handle it, it's March!

english: And I can handle it.
french: Comme toujours.
russian: Мне всё по силам.
bulgarian: And I can handle it.

english: Hi March, Olric! I'm doing a business check-in around town.
french: Bonjour March et Olric ! Je fais le tour des commerces de la ville.
russian: Привет, Март! Привет, Ольрик! Я проверяю, как идут дела в наших городских предприятиях.
bulgarian: Hi March, Olric! I'm doing a business check-in around town.

english: The town's doing great! It seems like everyone's got what they need.
french: La ville va bien ! Je crois que tout le monde a ce dont il a besoin.
russian: В городе всё отлично! Кажется, у всех есть всё, что нужно.
bulgarian: The town's doing great! It seems like everyone's got what they need.

english: Hah! I'm happy to hear it, but I was asking how you were doing.
french: Ha ! Je suis ravie de l'apprendre, mais je voulais savoir comment tu allais, toi.
russian: Приятно слышать! Но я спрашивала, как дела у тебя.
bulgarian: Hah! I'm happy to hear it, but I was asking how you were doing.

english: Oh! I'm doing great too, thank you for asking!
french: Oh ! Je vais bien aussi, merci !
russian: А! У меня тоже всё хорошо, спасибо, что спросила.
bulgarian: Oh! I'm doing great too, thank you for asking!

english: How are you doing, Adeline?
french: Comment ça va, Adeline ?
russian: Аделина, как дела?
bulgarian: How are you doing, Adeline?

english: These new forms can be confusing, but they're designed to get you an extra deduction!
french: Ces nouveaux formulaires sont un peu déroutants, mais ils te permettront de déduire plus encore !
russian: Новая форма выглядит довольно запутанно, но она позволяет получить дополнительный вычет.
bulgarian: These new forms can be confusing, but they're designed to get you an extra deduction!

english: That explains it! What a nice surprise!
french: Ah, je vois ! C'est une excellente surprise !
russian: Ах, вот оно что! Приятный сюрприз!
bulgarian: That explains it! What a nice surprise!

english: See, Nora? You just put the merchant's fee over here.
french: Tu vois, Nora ? C'est là que tu indiques la commission du marchand.
russian: Смотри, Нора, торговый сбор вписываем в эту графу.
bulgarian: See, Nora? You just put the merchant's fee over here.

english: We had a bit of scarcity after the earthquake, but ever since Balor started sourcing food from both Hayden and [Ari]'s farms...
french: On a eu quelques soucis de réapprovisionnement après le tremblement de terre, mais depuis que Balor se fournit chez Hayden et [Ari]...
russian: После землетрясения у нас был небольшой дефицит. Но с тех пор, как Балору стали поставлять продукты Хейден и [Ari]...
bulgarian: We had a bit of scarcity after the earthquake, but ever since Balor started sourcing food from both Hayden and [Ari]'s farms...

english: We've been well-stocked!
french: On ne manque de rien !
russian: У нас всегда есть хороший запас!
bulgarian: We've been well-stocked!

english: You know, I don't think I've seen an empty shelf in here for many seasons now.
french: Je crois que je n'ai pas vu une seule étagère vide ici depuis plusieurs saisons.
russian: Знаешь, по-моему, я не видела пустых полок уже много сезонов.
bulgarian: You know, I don't think I've seen an empty shelf in here for many seasons now.

english: Oh, not at all!
french: Oh, pas du tout !
russian: Ой, вовсе нет!
bulgarian: Oh, not at all!

english: Actually, I'm just here because we ran out of potatoes.
french: Je viens faire des courses. Nous sommes à court de pommes de terre.
russian: Просто у нас закончилась картошка.
bulgarian: Actually, I'm just here because we ran out of potatoes.

english: Adeline! Did you need me to look at the ledgers again?
french: Adeline ! Tu veux que je regarde les livres de comptes ?
russian: Аделина! Ты хочешь, чтобы я снова проверила бухгалтерию?
bulgarian: Adeline! Did you need me to look at the ledgers again?

english: Oh, it's my pleasure. No one likes a mystery number!
french: Oh, je t'en prie. Les écarts de compta, c'est toujours pénible !
russian: Обращайся! Неучтённые цифры никто не любит.
bulgarian: Oh, it's my pleasure. No one likes a mystery number!

english: Well, Balor maybe.
french: Sauf pour Balor, peut-être...
russian: Хотя, может, Балор любит.
bulgarian: Well, Balor maybe.

english: Thanks for your assistance, Nora. My books just weren't adding up.
french: Merci pour ton aide, Nora. Ma comptabilité ne tombait pas juste.
russian: Спасибо за помощь, Нора. Без тебя у меня никак не сходилось.
bulgarian: Thanks for your assistance, Nora. My books just weren't adding up.

english: Oh, no... That's sauce from Holt's lunch.
french: Non, pas du tout... C'est une tâche de sauce que Holt a faite en mangeant.
russian: Ой, нет... Это соус с обеда Хольта.
bulgarian: Oh, no... That's sauce from Holt's lunch.

english: Nora, what's the meaning of this red blot here? Do we need to check it over again?
french: Nora, c'est quoi cette tache rouge ici ? Il faut tout revérifier ?
russian: Нора, подскажи, что тут помечено красным кружком? Этот пункт надо перепроверить?
bulgarian: Nora, what's the meaning of this red blot here? Do we need to check it over again?

english: It is! We're actually in great shape.
french: Complètement ! Il marche très bien.
russian: Ещё как! Вообще говоря, там дела идут отлично.
bulgarian: It is! We're actually in great shape.

english: Though we'll need to start costing out some fresh pennants for next year.
french: En revanche, il va falloir envisager de remplacer les toiles des étals pour l'année prochaine.
russian: Но на следующий год надо закупиться новыми флажками.
bulgarian: Though we'll need to start costing out some fresh pennants for next year.

english: Is the Saturday Market budget holding up, Nora?
french: Est-ce que le marché du samedi est à l'équilibre, Nora ?
russian: Нора, Субботний базар укладывается в бюджет?
bulgarian: Is the Saturday Market budget holding up, Nora?

english: I know we can, Nora! We'll get Mistria back on its feet! We'll make it even better!
french: J'en suis sûre, Nora ! Mistria va se relever ! Et même plus !
russian: Уверена, что получится, Нора! Мистрия быстро встанет на ноги. Станет даже лучше, чем раньше!
bulgarian: I know we can, Nora! We'll get Mistria back on its feet! We'll make it even better!

english: You really think we can make the Saturday Market a reality again, Adeline?
french: Tu crois que tu pourras faire revivre le marché du samedi, Adeline ?
russian: Ты правда думаешь, что у нас получится восстановить Субботний базар, Аделина?
bulgarian: You really think we can make the Saturday Market a reality again, Adeline?

english: Not at all! You were very thorough.
french: Pas du tout ! Tu as été très consciencieuse.
russian: Вовсе нет! Ты очень подробно всё расписала.
bulgarian: Not at all! You were very thorough.

english: I'm actually here for groceries.
french: Je viens juste faire des courses.
russian: Я просто зашла за покупками.
bulgarian: I'm actually here for groceries.

english: Oh, Adeline! Did I forget something at the last business check-in?
french: Adeline ! J'ai oublié quelque chose lors de notre dernier point sur la situation économique ?
russian: О, Аделина! Я что-то забыла во время прошлой проверки?
bulgarian: Oh, Adeline! Did I forget something at the last business check-in?

english: Of course! And just say the word! If you don't run into me, you can leave a note in my office any time.
french: Je t'en prie ! Je suis là pour ça ! Et si je ne suis pas là, tu peux toujours laisser un message sur mon bureau.
russian: Говори, конечно, не стесняйся! А если не найдёшь меня, можешь в любое время зайти в мой офис и оставить записку.
bulgarian: Of course! And just say the word! If you don't run into me, you can leave a note in my office any time.

english: The forge is doing super well right now, but if something comes up I'll let you know. Thanks for checking in, Adeline!
french: Tout se passe bien à la forge pour le moment, mais en cas de souci, je viendrai te voir. Merci, Adeline !
russian: В кузнице сейчас всё отлично, но если что-то будет нужно — я сразу скажу. Спасибо, что присматриваешь, Аделина!
bulgarian: The forge is doing super well right now, but if something comes up I'll let you know. Thanks for checking in, Adeline!

english: A pinch of... tesserae...
french: Une pincée de... tesserae...
russian: Взять щепотку... тессер...
bulgarian: A pinch of... tesserae...

english: Actually, let's take it from the top.
french: En fait, on va reprendre du début.
russian: Ладно, давай лучше пойдём с первой строки.
bulgarian: Actually, let's take it from the top.

english: Think of it like the quick math you do for recipes, Reina! Accounting's not so different. Try filling out the next line!
french: Vois ça comme le calcul mental que tu fais en cuisinant, Reina ! La comptabilité, c'est pareil. Vas-y, essaie de remplir la ligne suivante !
russian: Думай об этом, как о подборе ингредиентов для рецепта, Рейна. Бухгалтерия слегка похожа на готовку. Попробуй заполнить следующую строчку!
bulgarian: Think of it like the quick math you do for recipes, Reina! Accounting's not so different. Try filling out the next line!

english: Eyes on the prize, Reina! We're almost done with these invoices!
french: Concentre-toi, Reina ! On en a presque fini avec ces factures !
russian: Держи эту мысль в уме, Рейна! Мы почти закончили с квитанциями.
bulgarian: Eyes on the prize, Reina! We're almost done with these invoices!

english: Ughhh, I wish I was at the Beach.
french: Argh, j'aimerais tellement être à la plage.
russian: Эх, сейчас бы на пляж!
bulgarian: Ughhh, I wish I was at the Beach.

english: What do you mean "maybe"...?
french: Comment ça, « peut-être » ?
russian: Что значит «может быть»?
bulgarian: What do you mean "maybe"...?

english: Before I get carried away with work, maybe we should schedule lunch...
french: Avant de se mettre au travail, on devrait peut-être aller déjeuner...
russian: Пока я не ушла с головой в работу, может быть, стоит подумать об обеде...
bulgarian: Before I get carried away with work, maybe we should schedule lunch...

english: We're getting through the repair projects around town faster than expected thanks to [Ari]'s help! Are you doing okay?
french: Les travaux de réhabilitation vont plus vite que prévu grâce à [Ari] ! Tout va bien de ton côté ?
russian:
[Ari] очень

помогают

помогаетпомогаетпомогает нам с ремонтом города, так что мы опережаем график! У тебя всё в порядке?
bulgarian: We're getting through the repair projects around town faster than expected thanks to [Ari]'s help! Are you doing okay?

english: Not a problem, I can keep up. It's exciting, honestly.
french: Aucun souci, j'arrive à suivre. Je trouve ça même amusant.
russian: Да, я успеваю, без проблем. Честно, так даже интереснее.
bulgarian: Not a problem, I can keep up. It's exciting, honestly.

english: Don't let me interrupt, I'm just here to do a quick check-in.
french: Faites comme si je n'étais pas là. Je viens voir comment ça avance.
russian: Не отвлекайся, у меня просто небольшая проверка.
bulgarian: Don't let me interrupt, I'm just here to do a quick check-in.

english: I'll see what I can do!
french: Je vais voir ce que je peux faire !
russian: Понимаю! Посмотрю, что можно сделать!
bulgarian: I'll see what I can do!

english: Uncle Landen says we could use more lumber! Never know when the jobs come in, y'know?
french: Oncle Landen dit qu'il nous faut plus de bois ! On ne sait jamais quand une nouvelle commande peut arriver.
russian: Дядя Ланден говорит, нам бы не помешало ещё древесины. Никогда не знаешь, когда пойдут заказы.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen says we could use more lumber! Never know when the jobs come in, y'know?

english: Everyone came together to make it happen. Especially you, [Ari]! You really went the extra mile.
french: Tout le monde s'est mobilisé pour sa restauration. Surtout toi, [Ari] ! Tu t'es donné<she>e</she><he></he><they>·e</they> à fond.
russian: К этой работе приложили руку мы все. Особенно ты, [Ari]! Твой вклад трудно переоценить.
bulgarian: Everyone came together to make it happen. Especially you, [Ari]! You really went the extra mile.

english: I'm doing regular check-ins for wear on some of the timber components, but beyond that? It's all upkeep from here. The Mill's looking good, Adeline.
french: Je vérifie régulièrement l'état de certains éléments en bois. En dehors de ça, c'est l'entretien de routine. Le moulin est en parfait état, Adeline.
russian: Иногда я проверяю, не пора ли заменить истёршиеся деревянные детали. А в остальном только мелкий ремонт. Мельница работает отлично, Аделина!
bulgarian: I'm doing regular check-ins for wear on some of the timber components, but beyond that? It's all upkeep from here. The Mill's looking good, Adeline.

english: Why not make them orders instead?
french: Pourquoi vous ne rédigez pas plutôt des ordres ?
russian: Почему бы не сделать из них приказы?
bulgarian: Why not make them orders instead?

english: I have found that ruling with an iron first is quite effective if you want to get things done.
french: Je sais d'expérience que gouverner d'une main de fer permet d'atteindre ses objectifs.
russian: Я заметила, что править железной рукой весьма эффективно, если хочешь, чтобы дела делались как следует.
bulgarian: I have found that ruling with an iron first is quite effective if you want to get things done.

english: Um... I'm not sure that's my style, Seridia.
french: Euh... Ce n'est pas tout à fait dans ma nature, Seridia.
russian: Эм... Я думаю, это не мой стиль, Серидия.
bulgarian: Um... I'm not sure that's my style, Seridia.

english: What about building community? Sharing responsibilities?
french: Que faites-vous des liens qui soudent une communauté ? Et des responsabilités à partager ?
russian: А как же строить сообщество? Разделять ответственность?
bulgarian: What about building community? Sharing responsibilities?

english: Building community? Sharing? With your subjects?
french: Des liens ? Partager ? Ce sont vos sujets !
russian: Общаться и делиться? Со своими подданными?
bulgarian: Building community? Sharing? With your subjects?

english: It is worse than I thought...
french: C'est pire que ce que je pensais...
russian: Всё ещё хуже, чем я думала...
bulgarian: It is worse than I thought...

english: Fear not, Adeline. I shall take you under my wing and teach you the true ways of ruling.
french: N'ayez crainte, Adeline. Je vais vous prendre sous mon aile pour vous apprendre les secrets d'une gouvernance efficace.
russian: Не бойся, Аделина. Я возьму тебя под своё крыло и научу тебя, как подобает царствовать.
bulgarian: Fear not, Adeline. I shall take you under my wing and teach you the true ways of ruling.

english: Tell me, Adeline. I have seen you draft these... requests.
french: Dites-moi, Adeline. Je vous ai observée en train de rédiger ces... requêtes.
russian: Расскажи, Аделина: я видела, как ты выписываешь эти... прошения.
bulgarian: Tell me, Adeline. I have seen you draft these... requests.

english: Though I still question your approach to ruling.
french: Mais je ne peux m'empêcher de me poser des questions quant à votre manière de régner.
russian: Хотя я всё ещё не разделяю твой подход к правлению.
bulgarian: Though I still question your approach to ruling.

english: And your motivations, as well.
french: Ainsi que sur vos motivations.
russian: Как и твои мотивы.
bulgarian: And your motivations, as well.

english: My motivations?
french: Mes motivations ?
russian: Мои мотивы?
bulgarian: My motivations?

english: Well...
french: Eh bien...
russian: Ну...
bulgarian: Well...

english: I really just want everyone in Mistria to be safe and happy.
french: Je veux simplement que tous les habitants de Mistria se sentent en sécurité et soient heureux.
russian: Я всего лишь хочу, чтобы все в Мистрии были довольны и в безопасности.
bulgarian: I really just want everyone in Mistria to be safe and happy.

english: Ah, yes. It is only natural to protect and provide for one's flock if you wish to extract value from them.
french: Ah, je vois. Il est tout à fait naturel de protéger ses ouailles et de leur fournir tout ce dont elles ont besoin pour mieux les exploiter.
russian: Ах, да. Если хочешь извлечь из своего стада выгоду, то защищать и заботиться о нём естественно.
bulgarian: Ah, yes. It is only natural to protect and provide for one's flock if you wish to extract value from them.

english: It seems I nearly mistook your shrewdness for beneficence.
french: J'ai failli prendre votre machiavélisme pour de la bonté.
russian: Я чуть было не приняла твою прагматичность за благонравие.
bulgarian: It seems I nearly mistook your shrewdness for beneficence.

english: The citizens of Mistria... It appears that they respect and admire you as they should.
french: Les citoyens de Mistria... semblent vous respecter et vous admirer, comme il se doit.
russian: Обитатели Мистрии... Кажется, питают к тебе должное уважение и восхищение.
bulgarian: The citizens of Mistria... It appears that they respect and admire you as they should.

english: Oh, let's have a look!
french: Oh, regardons ça tout de suite !
russian: О, давай посмотрим!
bulgarian: Oh, let's have a look!

english: "Bring me 200 stone or perish".
french: « Qu'on m'apporte 200 pierres, sans quoi le malheur s'abattra sur vous. »
russian: «Принесите 200 камня или погибнете».
bulgarian: "Bring me 200 stone or perish".

english: Well... it gets the job done.
french: Eh bien... ça a le mérite d'être direct.
russian: Что ж... Очень ясно доносит мысль.
bulgarian: Well... it gets the job done.

english: Adeline, I have tried my hand at writing one of your board requests.
french: Adeline, j'ai essayé de rédiger moi-même une de ces requêtes pour le panneau.
russian: Аделина, я попробовала сама написать прошение на твоей доске.
bulgarian: Adeline, I have tried my hand at writing one of your board requests.

english: Oh, you think I can do it? I hear some fish can be feisty, but I'm very persuasive!
french: Oh, tu ferais ça pour moi ? Il paraît que certains poissons sont retors, mais je peux me montrer très persuasive !
russian: Ой, думаешь, у меня получится? Слышала, рыба бывает упрямая, но я могу говорить очень убедительно!
bulgarian: Oh, you think I can do it? I hear some fish can be feisty, but I'm very persuasive!

english: I'd be happy to give you fishing lessons any time, Adeline!
french: Je serais ravie de te donner des leçons de pêche quand tu veux, Adeline !
russian: Я готова научить тебя рыбалке, когда захочешь, Аделина!
bulgarian: I'd be happy to give you fishing lessons any time, Adeline!

english: It's always good in Mistria! There must be something in the water.
french: Comme toujours, à Mistria ! Il doit y avoir quelque chose dans l'eau.
russian: В Мистрии — всегда отлично! В здешних водах явно что-то есть.
bulgarian: It's always good in Mistria! There must be something in the water.

english: Like fish.
french: Oui, des poissons...
russian: Рыба, например.
bulgarian: Like fish.

english: How's fishing these days, Terithia?
french: La pêche est bonne en ce moment, Terithia ?
russian: Как дела на рыбалке, Теризия?
bulgarian: How's fishing these days, Terithia?

english: Oh my gosh! I'll schedule it right away!
french: Mince ! Il faut que je prenne rendez-vous, alors !
russian: Ой, точно! Внесу в график сейчас же, чтобы не забыть!
bulgarian: Oh my gosh! I'll schedule it right away!

english: I'd say it's nearing time for your annual checkup, Adeline.
french: Ta visite médicale annuelle approche, Adeline.
russian: Аделина, тебе скоро пора проводить диспансеризацию.
bulgarian: I'd say it's nearing time for your annual checkup, Adeline.

english: Actually, I just like the taste.
french: Non, je trouve ça bon, c'est tout.
russian: Вообще мне просто вкус нравится.
bulgarian: Actually, I just like the taste.

english: You like =Pan Fried Salmon=? Ah, because of its numerous and well-documented health benefits!
french: Tu aimes le =saumon poêlé= ? J'imagine qu'il a plein de qualités nutritionnelles.
russian: Ты любишь =обжаренный лосось=? Наверное, за его неоднократно научно подтверждённую пользу для здоровья.
bulgarian: You like =Pan Fried Salmon=? Ah, because of its numerous and well-documented health benefits!

english: Is that... you?
french: Est-ce que... c'est vous ?
russian: Это же... про тебя?
bulgarian: Is that... you?

english: Oh! Do you think that is true? Surely not.
french: Oh ! Vous croyez ? Je ne pense pas.
russian: Ой! Вы правда так думаете? Не может быть.
bulgarian: Oh! Do you think that is true? Surely not.

english: But if it were... I am awake now. Would the name be changed?
french: Mais si c'était le cas, alors... me voilà réveillé. Faudrait-il changer le nom de cet établissement ?
russian: А если так... Я ведь уже проснулся. Придётся менять название?
bulgarian: But if it were... I am awake now. Would the name be changed?

english: That would be a pity. The Awake Dragon Inn does not have the same ring to it.
french: Ce serait dommage. L'auberge du Dragon éveillé, ça ne sonne pas pareil.
russian: Было бы очень жаль. «Неспящий дракон» — это уже не так звучно.
bulgarian: That would be a pity. The Awake Dragon Inn does not have the same ring to it.

english: Caldarus, we've been wondering... the name of this establishment is the Sleeping Dragon Inn.
french: Caldarus, on se demandait... Cet établissement s'appelle l'auberge du Dragon qui dort.
russian: Кальдарус, мы тут поразмышляли... Это заведение называется «Спящий дракон».
bulgarian: Caldarus, we've been wondering... the name of this establishment is the Sleeping Dragon Inn.

english: My cooking ends up being the same dour hue, more often than not.
french: Tout ce que je cuisine finit par avoir la même apparence terne.
russian: Когда я готовлю, еда чаще всего получается одинакового хмурого цвета.
bulgarian: My cooking ends up being the same dour hue, more often than not.

english: It... does?
french: Vraiment...?
russian: Каким образом?..
bulgarian: It... does?

english: Do elaborate, Caldarus.
french: Dites-nous en plus, Caldarus.
russian: Кальдарус, поясни, пожалуйста.
bulgarian: Do elaborate, Caldarus.

english: Hm, how could one describe it...
french: Hum, comment dire...?
russian: Хм, как бы это описать...
bulgarian: Hm, how could one describe it...

english: Do mortals have a word for the color of burnt food?
french: Les mortels ont-ils un mot pour décrire la couleur de la nourriture qui a brûlé ?
russian: У смертных есть слово для цвета сгоревшей еды?
bulgarian: Do mortals have a word for the color of burnt food?

english: Perhaps I could invent it. It would please me to leave my mark on history.
french: Sinon, je peux peut-être l'inventer. J'aimerais bien laisser une trace dans l'histoire.
russian: Возможно, мне стоит его изобрести. Мне было бы приятно оставить свой след в истории.
bulgarian: Perhaps I could invent it. It would please me to leave my mark on history.

english: The dishes here are delicious, and so colorful!
french: La nourriture servie ici est délicieuse et pleine de couleurs !
russian: Здесь такие вкусные и яркие блюда!
bulgarian: The dishes here are delicious, and so colorful!

english: Mine as well! Here, don't be shy!
french: Et dans la mienne aussi, ne faites pas votre timide !
russian: И с моей! Бери, не стесняйся!
bulgarian: Mine as well! Here, don't be shy!

english: Oh, then please partake of my food as well.
french: Oh, alors je vous offre volontiers de la mienne également.
russian: О, тогда и вы отведайте из моей.
bulgarian: Oh, then please partake of my food as well.

english: This brings back memories... the priestesses of my temple often shared in communal meals.
french: Cela me rappelle des souvenirs... Les prêtresses de mon temple partageaient souvent la nourriture entre elles, lors des repas communs.
russian: Я сразу вспоминаю... как жрицы в моём храме часто устраивали совместные трапезы.
bulgarian: This brings back memories... the priestesses of my temple often shared in communal meals.

english: I like the sound of that. Let's raise a glass to old friends, Caldarus.
french: Voilà qui devait être très convivial. Levons notre verre aux amis disparus, Caldarus !
russian: Звучит отлично. Поднимем бокал за старых друзей, Кальдарус!
bulgarian: I like the sound of that. Let's raise a glass to old friends, Caldarus.

english: Cheers!
french: Santé !
russian: Выпьем!
bulgarian: Cheers!

english: Cheers!
french: Santé !
russian: Выпьем!
bulgarian: Cheers!

english: And here is to new friends as well.
french: Et aux nouveaux amis, également.
russian: А заодно выпьем и за новых.
bulgarian: And here is to new friends as well.

english: I've never seen someone so excited about food. Feel free to take anything off of my plate, Caldarus.
french: Je n'ai jamais vu quelqu'un si intéressé par la nourriture. N'hésitez pas à vous servir dans mon assiette, Caldarus.
russian: Никогда не видел, чтобы кто-то так радовался еде. Можешь брать из моей тарелки, Кальдарус.
bulgarian: I've never seen someone so excited about food. Feel free to take anything off of my plate, Caldarus.

english: Do you have any wisdom to share?
french: Êtes-vous disposé à partager avec moi votre savoir ?
russian: Можешь поделиться своей мудростью?
bulgarian: Do you have any wisdom to share?

english: A good merchant always makes the first offer. That anchors a negotiation.
french: Un bon marchand fait toujours la première offre. Cela pose la base des négociations.
russian: Хороший торговец всегда даёт первое предложение. Это задаёт рамки.
bulgarian: A good merchant always makes the first offer. That anchors a negotiation.

english: I've seen this happen many times in high society, as well. Setting the terms of a conversation is a subtle but powerful tool.
french: J'ai moi-même assisté à de telles situations, dans la haute société. Imposer les bases d'une conversation est une technique subtile, mais redoutable.
russian: Я много раз сталкивалась с этим в высшем обществе. Установить правила диалога — незаметный, но эффективный приём.
bulgarian: I've seen this happen many times in high society, as well. Setting the terms of a conversation is a subtle but powerful tool.

english: I see. Then, for practice, I will negotiate for this piece of fiber in your store, Balor. I offer you... two diamonds!
french: Je vois. Alors, pour m'entraîner, je veux négocier pour la fibre en vente dans votre boutique, Balor. Je vous en offre... deux diamants.
russian: Понятно. Тогда в качестве тренировки давай поторгуемся за кусок волокна из твоего фургона. Балор, я предлагаю тебе... два алмаза!
bulgarian: I see. Then, for practice, I will negotiate for this piece of fiber in your store, Balor. I offer you... two diamonds!

english: Oh!
french: Oh !
russian: Ох!
bulgarian: Oh!

english: Maybe we should start from the basics...
french: On devrait peut-être tout reprendre depuis le début.
russian: Видимо, лучше начинать с основ...
bulgarian: Maybe we should start from the basics...

english: Balor, I have decided that I must learn the art of negotiation, and I can think of no one better to teach me.
french: Balor, j'ai décidé que je devais apprendre l'art de la négociation, et je ne vois personne de mieux placé que vous pour cela.
russian: Балор, я решил обучиться искусству торга и подумал, что лучше тебя учителя не найти.
bulgarian: Balor, I have decided that I must learn the art of negotiation, and I can think of no one better to teach me.

english: Yes. When I was recovering in the Deep Woods, Balor was kind enough to fill my anonymous orders with no questions asked.
french: Oui. Lors de ma convalescence à Boissombre, Balor avait la gentillesse de répondre à mes requêtes anonymes sans poser la moindre question.
russian: Да. Когда я восстанавливался в Глубокой чаще, Балор любезно исполнял мои анонимные заказы без всяких вопросов.
bulgarian: Yes. When I was recovering in the Deep Woods, Balor was kind enough to fill my anonymous orders with no questions asked.

english: He earned himself a loyal customer.
french: Je suis devenu un de ses clients fidèles.
russian: Он заслужил себе верного клиента.
bulgarian: He earned himself a loyal customer.

english: I can't help but give a hand to a poor soul in need! Especially not one that pays so well!
french: Je ne peux pas m'empêcher de venir en aide à une pauvre âme en détresse ! Surtout quand elle paie si bien.
russian: Я просто не могу отказать клиенту в беде! Особенно, когда он так щедро платит!
bulgarian: I can't help but give a hand to a poor soul in need! Especially not one that pays so well!

english: Doing some shopping, Caldarus?
french: Vous faites quelques emplettes, Caldarus ?
russian: Решил закупиться, Кальдарус?
bulgarian: Doing some shopping, Caldarus?

english: What would you have done?
french: Qu'auriez-vous fait ?
russian: Что бы ты делал тогда?
bulgarian: What would you have done?

english: Well... I suppose I would have starved.
french: Eh bien... Je suppose que je serais mort de faim.
russian: Что ж... Полагаю, я бы умер от голода.
bulgarian: Well... I suppose I would have starved.

english: Oh! But [Ari] was there!
french: Oh ! Mais [Ari] était là !
russian:
Ой! Но там же

были

былабылбыло [Ari]!
bulgarian: Oh! But [Ari] was there!

english: That is true, but Elsie...
french: Certes, Elsie, toutefois...
russian: Элси, это верно, но...
bulgarian: That is true, but Elsie...

english: Despite what you may have heard, dragons do not eat people.
french: Malgré ce que vous avez pu entendre, les dragons ne dévorent pas les gens.
russian: Что бы тебе ни рассказывали, драконы не питаются людьми...
bulgarian: Despite what you may have heard, dragons do not eat people.

english: Caldarus, if I hadn't been filling your mystery orders and leaving your care packages...
french: Caldarus, si je n'avais pas répondu à vos requêtes et apporté vos commandes...
russian: Кальдарус, если бы я не выполнял твои загадочные заказы и не оставлял тебе посылки...
bulgarian: Caldarus, if I hadn't been filling your mystery orders and leaving your care packages...

english: Perfection as always, Josephine. My compliments to the chef!
french: Tout est parfait, comme d'habitude, Joséphine. Mes compliments à la cuisinière !
russian: Изумительно, как всегда, Джозефина. Мои похвалы шефу!
bulgarian: Perfection as always, Josephine. My compliments to the chef!

english: I reckon there's no better breakfast in Mistria! What do you think, Caldarus?
french: Je crois qu'il n'y a pas de meilleur petit-déjeuner dans tout Mistria ! Qu'est-ce que vous en pensez, Caldarus ?
russian: Думаю, в Мистрии лучше завтрака не найти! Как думаешь, Кальдарус?
bulgarian: I reckon there's no better breakfast in Mistria! What do you think, Caldarus?

english: I'd say he's too busy eating to voice his thoughts on the matter.
french: Je dirais qu'il est trop occupé à manger pour nous donner son opinion sur le sujet.
russian: Мне кажется, он слишком занят едой, чтобы озвучить своё мнение.
bulgarian: I'd say he's too busy eating to voice his thoughts on the matter.

english: If I had to summarize...
french: Si je devais résumer...
russian: Я выскажусь кратко...
bulgarian: If I had to summarize...

english: May I have seconds?
french: Je peux en avoir encore ?
russian: Можно добавки?
bulgarian: May I have seconds?

english: How are you all liking your breakfast?
french: Alors tout le monde, le petit-déjeuner vous plaît ?
russian: Как вам ваш завтрак?
bulgarian: How are you all liking your breakfast?

english: Any preparation of egg suits me... but my favorite is perhaps a fluffy quiche.
french: En ce qui me concerne, j'aime les œufs préparés de n'importe quelle façon... mais si je dois choisir un plat, je dirais une quiche bien soufflée.
russian: Меня устраивает любой вариант... Но мой любимый — это, пожалуй, пышный киш.
bulgarian: Any preparation of egg suits me... but my favorite is perhaps a fluffy quiche.

english: Fried over easy, on top of some of your famous curry!
french: Sans hésiter, ses œufs au plat, à cheval sur votre fameux curry !
russian: Омлет
bulgarian: Fried over easy, on top of some of your famous curry!

english: I prefer them hard-boiled and diced into a salad.
french: J'aime les œufs durs découpés et mélangés à une salade.
russian: Мне нравится вкрутую и порубить в салат.
bulgarian: I prefer them hard-boiled and diced into a salad.

english: I like an egg any which way... but my favorite's gotta be when it's whipped up into a $Mayonnaise$!
french: J'aime toutes les préparations à base d'œufs... mais je crois que ma préférée reste la $mayonnaise$ !
russian: Мне нравятся яйца в любом виде... Но лучше всего, если из них взбить хороший $майонез$!
bulgarian: I like an egg any which way... but my favorite's gotta be when it's whipped up into a $Mayonnaise$!

english: But... don't you want that to accompany something?
french: Mais... sans rien d'autre pour accompagner ça ?
russian: Но... ты же им, наверное, что-нибудь поливаешь?
bulgarian: But... don't you want that to accompany something?

english: If you want to get all fancy about it!
french: Là on tape dans la cuisine de luxe !
russian: Ну это если хочется изысков!
bulgarian: If you want to get all fancy about it!

english: I'm writing up next week's brunch menu. Tell me... how do you folks like your eggs?
french: Je suis en train de préparer le menu pour le brunch de la semaine prochaine. Dites-moi un peu... comment aimez-vous les œufs ?
russian: Я составляю меню для бранча на следующую неделю. Скажите... В каком виде вы любите яйца?
bulgarian: I'm writing up next week's brunch menu. Tell me... how do you folks like your eggs?

english: I see your tail and the unique structure of your legs, but you otherwise don't seem so different from the rest of us.
french: À part votre queue et la morphologie unique de vos jambes, vous ne semblez pas si différent de nous autres.
russian: Я заметила твой хвост и необычное строение ног, но в остальном ты не сильно отличаешься от нас.
bulgarian: I see your tail and the unique structure of your legs, but you otherwise don't seem so different from the rest of us.

english: Your appetite's the same as the rest of us, that's for sure!
french: En tout cas, vous avez le même appétit que nous, c'est indéniable !
russian: Аппетит у тебя точно не хуже!
bulgarian: Your appetite's the same as the rest of us, that's for sure!

english: Who can resist a good meal?
french: Qui peut résister à un bon repas ?
russian: Кто станет отказываться от вкусной еды?
bulgarian: Who can resist a good meal?

english: Especially with friends!
french: Surtout entre copains !
russian: Тем более с друзьями!
bulgarian: Especially with friends!

english: I suspect you and the others are correct on all points, Valen.
french: Je crois que vous et les autres avez raison sur tous ces points, Valen.
russian: Полагаю, и ты, Вален, и остальные совершенно правы.
bulgarian: I suspect you and the others are correct on all points, Valen.

english: A good meal, with good company... it makes the heart warm, no matter who we are.
french: Un bon repas en bonne compagnie... cela réchauffe le cœur de n'importe qui.
russian: Хорошая еда в хорошей компании... Согревает нам сердце, кем бы мы ни были.
bulgarian: A good meal, with good company... it makes the heart warm, no matter who we are.

english: As a doctor, I cannot help but be curious about your physiology, Caldarus.
french: En tant que docteure, je ne peux m'empêcher de me poser des questions sur votre physiologie, Caldarus.
russian: Как медик я не могу не интересоваться твоей физиологией, Кальдарус.
bulgarian: As a doctor, I cannot help but be curious about your physiology, Caldarus.

english: Oh, like... top shelf country fresh organically grown heirloom seeds?
french: Oh, comme... « graines bio et locales de nos campagnes » ?
russian: Например... «свежие отборные фермерские семена, выращенные по семейной традиции»?
bulgarian: Oh, like... top shelf country fresh organically grown heirloom seeds?

english: Wow, you're a natural!
french: Waouh, tu as ça dans le sang !
russian: Ух, да у тебя талант!
bulgarian: Wow, you're a natural!

english: Haha, I'm my mother's daughter!
french: Ha ha, je tiens ça de ma mère !
russian: Ха-ха, это всё от мамы!
bulgarian: Haha, I'm my mother's daughter!

english: Instead of calling them seeds from your garden, how about calling them something more memorable?
french: Au lieu de dire que ce sont des graines de ton jardin, il faudrait un nom plus accrocheur, tu ne crois pas ?
russian: Может, лучше назвать их не просто «семена из сада Селин», а придумать что-нибудь более запоминающееся?
bulgarian: Instead of calling them seeds from your garden, how about calling them something more memorable?

english: Only if it's not a bother!
french: Merci, c'est gentil !
russian: Только если тебе не сложно!
bulgarian: Only if it's not a bother!

english: Special plant food formula from the Capital? I know a chemist, I can ask around.
french: Tu veux que je rapporte un engrais spécial pour plantes de la capitale ? Je connais un chimiste, je vais voir avec lui.
russian: Особый столичный рецепт удобрений, говоришь? У меня есть знакомый специалист, могу поспрашивать.
bulgarian: Special plant food formula from the Capital? I know a chemist, I can ask around.

english: That's probably it! We're so lucky that they grow wild in Mistria.
french: Sûrement ! On a tellement de chances qu'elles poussent bien à Mistria.
russian: Наверняка! Нам повезло, что в Мистрии они повсюду растут!
bulgarian: That's probably it! We're so lucky that they grow wild in Mistria.

english: There's a real demand for Fog Orchids in the Capital. Apparently they don't grow easily around there... something about the soil?
french: Les orchidées nébuleuses font fureur dans la capitale. Apparemment, elles ne poussent pas facilement là-bas... C'est peut-être la terre qui ne leur convient pas ?!
russian: В столице большой спрос на туманные орхидеи. Оказывается, там их трудно выращивать... Наверное, дело в почве?
bulgarian: There's a real demand for Fog Orchids in the Capital. Apparently they don't grow easily around there... something about the soil?

english: Oh, thank you! It's a big job, but I love doing it!
french: Oh, merci ! Ça demande beaucoup de travail, mais j'adore ça !
russian: Спасибо большое! Работы там много, но она мне нравится!
bulgarian: Oh, thank you! It's a big job, but I love doing it!

english: I was admiring the manor grounds the other day. A garden of that size is no easy thing to maintain... you have skill.
french: J'admirais les jardins du manoir l'autre jour. Ça ne doit pas être facile d'entretenir une telle surface... Tu es vraiment douée.
russian: Я недавно гулял вокруг особняка. За садом таких размеров, должно быть, непросто ухаживать... Ты отлично справляешься.
bulgarian: I was admiring the manor grounds the other day. A garden of that size is no easy thing to maintain... you have skill.

english: They're absolutely of use! Thank you!
french: Oui, et plutôt deux fois qu'une ! Merci !
russian: Ещё как пригодятся! Спасибо!
bulgarian: They're absolutely of use! Thank you!

english: Here are those pressed cuttings from that botanist in the Capital, Celine. I hope they're of some use to you.
french: Voici les fleurs séchées que tu avais commandées à ce botaniste de la capitale, Céline. J'espère qu'elles te seront utiles.
russian: Селин, я привёз твои черенки от того столичного ботаника. Надеюсь, они тебе пригодятся.
bulgarian: Here are those pressed cuttings from that botanist in the Capital, Celine. I hope they're of some use to you.

english: Not so fast, Hemlock. That hand doesn't beat my triple.
french: Pas si vite, Hemlock. Cette main ne bat pas mon brelan.
russian: Придержи коней, Хемлок. Моя тройка сильнее твоей руки.
bulgarian: Not so fast, Hemlock. That hand doesn't beat my triple.

english: But my hand does, right Balor?
french: Mais la mienne, oui. Pas vrai, Balor ?
russian: Но не сильнее моей, да, Балор?
bulgarian: But my hand does, right Balor?

english: What did Hemlock just say? Read them and cry, children!
french: C'était quoi, les paroles d'Hemlock ? Vous allez pleurer, la jeunesse !
russian: Что там Хемлок сказал? Не надо плакать, дети!
bulgarian: What did Hemlock just say? Read them and cry, children!

english: This is riveting, [Ari]!
french: C'est fascinant, [Ari] !
russian: [Ari], это такая захватывающая игра!
bulgarian: This is riveting, [Ari]!

english: Read 'em and weep, kiddos.
french: Vous allez pleurer, les jeunes.
russian: Я открываюсь — только не плачьте, ребята!
bulgarian: Read 'em and weep, kiddos.

english: You're definitely not. But you look shady.
french: Peut-être, mais tu es quand même louche.
russian: На самом деле нет. Но вид у тебя сомнительный.
bulgarian: You're definitely not. But you look shady.

english: It's your face, honestly.
french: C'est ta tête.
russian: Честно, дело в лице.
bulgarian: It's your face, honestly.

english: Definitely your face.
french: Oui, ta tête.
russian: Да, определённо, в лице.
bulgarian: Definitely your face.

english: You wound me! I'm not as shady as all that.
french: Je me suis senti blessé ! Je ne suis pas si louche que ça.
russian: Ты меня обижаешь! Разве я мутный?
bulgarian: You wound me! I'm not as shady as all that.

english: I drew up defensive plans, and Maple made the necessary arrangements.
french: J'ai élaboré les plans de défense et Maple a pris les dispositions nécessaires.
russian: Я подготовил план обороны, а Мэйпл договорилась с нужными людьми.
bulgarian: I drew up defensive plans, and Maple made the necessary arrangements.

english: To say I'm grateful to the Dragonguard would be an understatement, so allow me to thank you with some samples from the shipment.
french: Je ne saurais comme remercier la Garde des dragons, alors voici une partie de la cargaison pour vous.
russian: Не могу выразить, как я благодарен Драконьей страже! Позвольте мне отблагодарить вас образцами товара.
bulgarian: To say I'm grateful to the Dragonguard would be an understatement, so allow me to thank you with some samples from the shipment.

english: Yaaaay!
french: Youhou !
russian: Урааа!
bulgarian: Yaaaay!

english: The Dragonguard is here to protect your chocolate shipment, Balor.
french: La Garde des dragons est ici pour protéger la cargaison de chocolat, Balor.
russian: Балор! Драконья стража пришла охранять твою партию шоколада.
bulgarian: The Dragonguard is here to protect your chocolate shipment, Balor.

english: Well of course! I must know how to tax my citizens in a manner that brings money into the royal treasury, without enraging the people.
french: Évidemment ! Il faut savoir comment faire payer des impôts au peuple de manière à remplir le trésor royal, sans les mettre en rogne pour autant.
russian: Разумеется! Мне необходимо понимать, как обогащать казну за счёт налогов, не вызывая протестов населения.
bulgarian: Well of course! I must know how to tax my citizens in a manner that brings money into the royal treasury, without enraging the people.

english: I don't want to do taxes anymore...
french: J'en ai un peu marre des impôts...
russian: Надоело заниматься налогами...
bulgarian: I don't want to do taxes anymore...

english: That's what Mom said the other day!
french: Maman a dit pareil l'autre jour !
russian: Мама вчера тоже так говорила!
bulgarian: That's what Mom said the other day!

english: Maple, I have to say... you have a surprising grasp of a kingdom's economics.
french: Maple, franchement... tu comprends étonnamment bien comment l'économie d'un royaume fonctionne.
russian: Мэйпл, должен заметить, у тебя неожиданно широкие познания об устройстве экономики королевства.
bulgarian: Maple, I have to say... you have a surprising grasp of a kingdom's economics.

english: You forget who you're asking. I'll reach out to my contacts.
french: Tu as oublié à qui tu t'adresses ? Je vais en parler à mes contacts.
russian: Ты знаешь, к кому обращаться. Я свяжусь со своими контактами.
bulgarian: You forget who you're asking. I'll reach out to my contacts.

english: I'm looking for a collection, Balor. It's four volumes, covering Caldosian architecture. Red slipcase, gold trim. Any chance you can procure it?
french: Balor, je cherche une collection en quatre tomes sur l'architecture caldosienne. La couverture est rouge et la tranche, dorée. Tu pourrais me trouver ça ?
russian: Балор, я ищу одно коллекционное издание. Четырёхтомник о кальдосийской архитектуре. В красном футляре, с золотой окантовкой. Может, у тебя получится раздобыть?
bulgarian: I'm looking for a collection, Balor. It's four volumes, covering Caldosian architecture. Red slipcase, gold trim. Any chance you can procure it?

english: Hah! There's always a twist with you, Eiland.
french: Ha ! Je te reconnais bien là, Eiland.
russian: Ха! С тобой всегда всё не так просто, Эйланд.
bulgarian: Hah! There's always a twist with you, Eiland.

english: I'll reach out to my source and see if I can't track that information down for you.
french: Je vais contacter ma source et voir si j'arrive à obtenir ces informations pour toi.
russian: Я свяжусь с моим поставщиком и попрошу разыскать эту информацию.
bulgarian: I'll reach out to my source and see if I can't track that information down for you.

english: Your latest inventory intrigues me, Balor. I might be inclined to make a purchase if you can also illuminate its origins.
french: Tes dernières trouvailles m'intriguent, Balor. Je t'achèterai peut-être quelque chose si tu peux m'éclairer sur leur origine.
russian: Одно из твоих новых поступлений меня заинтриговало, Балор. Я готов рассмотреть покупку, если будет возможность прояснить его происхождение.
bulgarian: Your latest inventory intrigues me, Balor. I might be inclined to make a purchase if you can also illuminate its origins.

english: A great question! I've got several records that seem to conflict, so I'm waiting for some kind of definitive primary source to turn up before I come to any conclusions!
french: Excellente question ! J'ai plusieurs documents qui semblent se contredire, donc j'attends de trouver une source fiable avant de tirer mes propres conclusions.
russian: Великолепный вопрос! В разных записях фигурируют противоречивые сведения. Поэтому я не делаю поспешных выводов и жду, когда найдётся достоверный первоисточник.
bulgarian: A great question! I've got several records that seem to conflict, so I'm waiting for some kind of definitive primary source to turn up before I come to any conclusions!

english: So all that translates to... "no"?
french: Pour résumer... tu ne sais pas, c'est ça ?
russian: В общем, это значит... «не знаю»?
bulgarian: So all that translates to... "no"?

english: Yes.
french: Voilà.
russian: Да.
bulgarian: Yes.

english: Do you know how old the Manor House is, Eiland?
french: Tu sais de quand date le manoir, Eiland ?
russian: Эйланд, ты знаешь, сколько лет этому особняку?
bulgarian: Do you know how old the Manor House is, Eiland?

english: Oh, but this is wonderful! I can get a start on translating it right away!
french: Oh, mais c'est merveilleux ! Je vais pouvoir commencer à la traduire dès maintenant !
russian: О, это же замечательно! Я могу сейчас же приступить к расшифровке!
bulgarian: Oh, but this is wonderful! I can get a start on translating it right away!

english: The stone tablet you asked me to inquire after is actually broken into three pieces. Sorry to say that this is the only section I've been able to track down.
french: La tablette de pierre que tu m'as demandé de chercher est en trois morceaux. Malheureusement, c'est le seul morceau que j'ai pu retrouver.
russian: Скрижаль, которую ты просил разыскать, оказалась разделена на три части. Прости, но мне удалось добыть только эту.
bulgarian: The stone tablet you asked me to inquire after is actually broken into three pieces. Sorry to say that this is the only section I've been able to track down.

english: Well, the workload is about the same, but its nature changes.
french: La charge de travail reste la même, c'est juste sa nature qui change.
russian: На самом деле, работы не меньше, просто она другая.
bulgarian: Well, the workload is about the same, but its nature changes.

english: Less time at the dig site, more time researching.
french: Je consacre moins de temps aux fouilles et plus à mes recherches.
russian: Я меньше времени провожу на раскопках и больше — в кабинете.
bulgarian: Less time at the dig site, more time researching.

english: I suppose your work winds down in the winter, Eiland. It can't be easy to excavate anything in this snowy weather.
french: J'imagine que tu as moins de travail en hiver, Eiland. Ça ne doit pas être facile de faire des fouilles avec cette neige.
russian: Я думаю, зимой ты отдыхаешь от работы, Эйланд? Под таким снегом трудновато что-то раскопать.
bulgarian: I suppose your work winds down in the winter, Eiland. It can't be easy to excavate anything in this snowy weather.

english: I may be spending more time indoors, but that means more time for planning the spring excavations!
french: Je passe plus de temps à l'intérieur, mais cela me permet de bien préparer les fouilles de printemps !
russian: Мне приходится больше времени проводить в доме. Но это значит — больше времени на планирование весенних раскопок.
bulgarian: I may be spending more time indoors, but that means more time for planning the spring excavations!

english: Not even the winter season stops you from pursuing your passions, eh Eiland?
french: Même l'hiver ne t'empêche pas de vivre tes passions, hein Eiland ?
russian: Ты не бросаешь свои увлечения даже в зимний сезон, Эйланд?
bulgarian: Not even the winter season stops you from pursuing your passions, eh Eiland?

english: I dig up old stuff occasionally! Let's see... is my great granddad's old boot noteworthy? We did have the same shoe size!
french: Ça m'arrive de temps en temps ! Voyons... est-ce qu'une botte de l'époque de mon arrière-grand-père a un intérêt historique ? Il faisait la même pointure que moi !
russian: Иногда я выкапываю какие-то старые штуки. Дай подумать... сапог моего прапрадедушки — историческая ценность? У меня, оказывается, тот же размер!
bulgarian: I dig up old stuff occasionally! Let's see... is my great granddad's old boot noteworthy? We did have the same shoe size!

english: Why would you know that? Did you... did you put on the boot, Hayden?
french: Comment tu le sais ? Tu l'as essayée, Hayden ?
russian: Откуда ты знаешь? Ты что... ты же не надевал этот сапог, Хейден?
bulgarian: Why would you know that? Did you... did you put on the boot, Hayden?

english: Haha... I kinda dared him to...
french: Ha ha... Je l'ai mis au défi de le faire...
russian: Ха-ха... Это я с ним поспорил...
bulgarian: Haha... I kinda dared him to...

english: Have you ever dug up any artifacts on your land, Hayden? Anything of historical importance?
french: As-tu déjà déterré des artéfacts sur ton exploitation, Hayden ? Quelque chose d'important d'un point de vue historique ?
russian: Хейден, у тебя на участке когда-нибудь встречались артефакты? Какие-нибудь исторические ценности?
bulgarian: Have you ever dug up any artifacts on your land, Hayden? Anything of historical importance?

english: Oh, you are a gem Balor. I'll be reading these for weeks!
french: Oh, tu es une perle, Balor. J'ai de la lecture pour quelques semaines !
russian: О, Балор, ты мой спаситель! Мне их на несколько недель хватит.
bulgarian: Oh, you are a gem Balor. I'll be reading these for weeks!

english: I've got some books from the Capital for you, Elsie. The Kept Man series, right?
french: J'ai rapporté des livres de la capitale, Elsie. Vous vouliez la série « Le Gigolo », c'est ça ?
russian: Элси, я привёз тебе книг из столицы. Серия «Любовник на содержании», правильно?
bulgarian: I've got some books from the Capital for you, Elsie. The Kept Man series, right?

english: Balor my boy, when you get to my age, you learn some rules. And one of them is:
french: Balor, mon garçon, quand tu auras mon âge, tu sauras qu'il y a des règles. L'une d'elles est...
russian: Балор, мальчик мой, когда дорастёшь до моих лет, у тебя появятся принципы. Вот один из них:
bulgarian: Balor my boy, when you get to my age, you learn some rules. And one of them is:

english: No business in the Bathhouse!
french: On ne parle pas travail aux bains !
russian: В купальне дела не обсуждаем!
bulgarian: No business in the Bathhouse!

english: I've got a line on a rarity in the Capital, Errol. Will you let me know if the Museum's interested?
french: J'ai déniché une rareté à la capitale, Errol. Vous me direz si ça peut intéresser le musée.
russian: Эррол, у меня в столице есть выход на одну антикварную штучку. Если музею это интересно, дашь мне знать?
bulgarian: I've got a line on a rarity in the Capital, Errol. Will you let me know if the Museum's interested?

english: Answer me this, Errol. What's a museum without a gift shop?
french: J'ai une question, Errol. Qu'est-ce qu'un musée sans magasin de souvenirs ?
russian: Скажи-ка мне, Эррол, ну что такое музей без сувенирной лавки?
bulgarian: Answer me this, Errol. What's a museum without a gift shop?

english: A museum?
french: Un musée ?!
russian: Нормальный музей?
bulgarian: A museum?

english: I've got a business proposal for you and Eiland, but first...
french: J'ai une proposition pour Eiland et vous, mais tout d'abord...
russian: У меня для вас с Эйландом деловое предложение, но сперва...
bulgarian: I've got a business proposal for you and Eiland, but first...

english: I hear Hemlock's been prepping a new cocktail.
french: Il paraît qu'Hemlock a inventé un nouveau cocktail.
russian: Я слышал, Хемлок готовит новый коктейль.
bulgarian: I hear Hemlock's been prepping a new cocktail.

english: Think I'll end my shift at the Museum early, not much use manning the desk when the whole town is at the Inn tonight!
french: Je partirai du musée plus tôt aujourd'hui. Ça ne rime à rien d'être à l'accueil, alors que tout le monde se retrouve à l'auberge ce soir !
russian: Думаю сегодня пораньше уйти со смены в музее. Нет смысла стоять за стойкой, когда весь город в трактире!
bulgarian: Think I'll end my shift at the Museum early, not much use manning the desk when the whole town is at the Inn tonight!

english: However, I have to know. How do you get your pumpkins so big?
french: Ceci dit, j'aimerais bien savoir comment tu fais pour obtenir des citrouilles de cette taille.
russian: И всё же я должен знать. Как тебе удаётся выращивать такие огромные тыквы?
bulgarian: However, I have to know. How do you get your pumpkins so big?

english: Well, Hayden's always had a green thumb, ever since we were kids.
french: Tout petit déjà, Hayden avait la main verte.
russian: Ну, я знаю Хейдена с детства, и у него всегда был талант к садоводству.
bulgarian: Well, Hayden's always had a green thumb, ever since we were kids.

english: Sure, but judging by the size of those gourds, I'd say Hayden's got a whole green arm!
french: À en juger par la taille de ces courges, il n'y a pas que sa main qui est verte !
russian: С такими здоровенными тыквами, я бы сказала, просто талантище!
bulgarian: Sure, but judging by the size of those gourds, I'd say Hayden's got a whole green arm!

english: And they're so brilliantly orange! Surely you have an explanation for that! Explain yourself, sir!
french: Et elles sont d'un orange éclatant ! Tu as forcément un secret. Je veux tout savoir.
russian: И такой яркий рыжий цвет! Этому должно быть какое-то объяснение. Объяснитесь, сэр!
bulgarian: And they're so brilliantly orange! Surely you have an explanation for that! Explain yourself, sir!

english: Now now! I'm just glad you appreciate them! Come by the farm any time and take a gander!
french: Je suis content qu'elles vous plaisent. Passez à la ferme quand vous voulez. Je vous montrerai !
russian: Ну-ну! Я рад, что вам всем нравятся мои тыквы. Можете заходить на ферму поглазеть, когда хотите.
bulgarian: Now now! I'm just glad you appreciate them! Come by the farm any time and take a gander!

english: Hayden, I'm but a humble merchant, so farming is well outside my wheelhouse.
french: Hayden, je ne suis qu'un modeste marchand. L'agriculture, ça me dépasse.
russian: Хейден, я простой торговец и в фермерских делах не разбираюсь.
bulgarian: Hayden, I'm but a humble merchant, so farming is well outside my wheelhouse.

english: You could travel the breadth and width of Aldaria and not see a cow as fine as this, Balor.
french: Tu auras beau parcourir Aldaria de long en large, jamais tu ne croiseras de vache aussi belle, Balor.
russian: Ты, Балор, можешь объехать всю Альдарию вдоль и поперёк и не найдёшь такой коровы, как эта!
bulgarian: You could travel the breadth and width of Aldaria and not see a cow as fine as this, Balor.

english: When you said you had something rare and precious to show me, I wasn't expecting a cow...
french: Quand tu m'as dit que tu avais quelque chose de rare et de précieux à me montrer, je ne m'attendais pas à une vache...
russian: Когда ты говорил, что у тебя есть одна редкая и ценная штучка, я подумал не о корове...
bulgarian: When you said you had something rare and precious to show me, I wasn't expecting a cow...

english: Oh, don't you worry! Cooking is a breeze when Henrietta is my sous chef!
french: Oh, pas du tout ! Ça va tout seul avec Henrietta comme second de cuisine !
russian: Не переживай! Любое блюдо готовится легко, когда помогает Генриетта!
bulgarian: Oh, don't you worry! Cooking is a breeze when Henrietta is my sous chef!

english: This is a great spread, Hayden! I hope it didn't take too long to put it all together.
french: C'est un véritable festin, Hayden ! J'espère que ça ne t'a pas pris trop de temps à tout préparer.
russian: Отличная намазка, Хейден! Надеюсь, ты не очень долго её готовил.
bulgarian: This is a great spread, Hayden! I hope it didn't take too long to put it all together.

english: You want me to breed racing horses so you can start a betting pool? That'll take years!
french: Tu veux que j'élève des chevaux de course pour que tu puisses te lancer dans les paris ? Ça prendra des années !
russian: Ты правда хочешь, чтобы я разводил скаковых лошадей для твоего букмекерского бизнеса? Это работа на много лет!
bulgarian: You want me to breed racing horses so you can start a betting pool? That'll take years!

english: How about Olric and I have a footrace, and folks can bet on that! Saves us all some trouble.
french: Organise une course à pied avec Olric et moi et les gens parieront ! Ça nous évitera les complications.
russian: Может, лучше мы с Ольриком пробежимся на спор, а ребята пускай на нас ставят? Так всем будет проще!
bulgarian: How about Olric and I have a footrace, and folks can bet on that! Saves us all some trouble.

english: Come on, Hayden. I need a rancher in on this little scheme. I'll take care of the overhead, too.
french: Hayden, j'ai besoin d'un éleveur pour le coup. Je prendrai en charge tous les frais.
russian: Подумай, Хейден. Накладные расходы я возьму на себя, но в таком деле нужен хороший скотовод.
bulgarian: Come on, Hayden. I need a rancher in on this little scheme. I'll take care of the overhead, too.

english: If there's one thing I know about Hayden, it's that he never lets a friend skip dinner.
french: Je connais bien Hayden. Il ne laissera jamais un<she>e amie</she><he> ami</he><they>·e ami·e</they> sauter le dîner.
russian: Кое-что я знаю про Хейдена точно: он не позволит друзьям пропустить обед.
bulgarian: If there's one thing I know about Hayden, it's that he never lets a friend skip dinner.

english: [Ari]! Are you skipping dinner? That won't do, grab yourself some quiche!
french: [Ari], tu sautes le dîner ? Ce n'est pas bien. Prends une part de quiche !
russian:
[Ari]! Ты что,

пропустите

пропустишьпропустишьпропустишь обед? Нет, так нельзя, вон,

возьмите

возьмивозьмивозьми пирога.
bulgarian: [Ari]! Are you skipping dinner? That won't do, grab yourself some quiche!

english: Olric was showing me his new routine. It's challenging, but I can't let this guy show me up.
french: Olric m'a montré son nouveau programme d'entraînement. Il a fallu que je m'accroche, mais je ne pouvais le laisser m'en remontrer.
russian: Ольрик показывал мне свой новый режим тренировок. Тяжеловато, но не могу же я позволить пацану меня обойти!
bulgarian: Olric was showing me his new routine. It's challenging, but I can't let this guy show me up.

english: Working out's not a competition, bro!
french: Faire de l'exercice, ce n'est pas faire de la compétition !
russian: Бро, тренировка это не состязание.
bulgarian: Working out's not a competition, bro!

english: Except against... yourself.
french: Enfin... sauf contre soi-même.
russian: Разве что... с самим собой.
bulgarian: Except against... yourself.

english: You boys look like you broke a sweat!
french: Vous avez transpiré, on dirait !
russian: Вид у вас, ребята, довольно уставший!
bulgarian: You boys look like you broke a sweat!

english: I mostly kept to the halls of academia. I was still studying at the time.
french: Je passais le plus clair de mon temps à l'académie. J'étais encore étudiante à cette époque-là.
russian: Я почти всё время проводила в университете. Постоянно надо было учиться.
bulgarian: I mostly kept to the halls of academia. I was still studying at the time.

english: A merchant's business is usually with other merchants. Most of my time was spent in the market quarter.
french: Un marchand se retrouve avec les autres commerçants. Moi, je sortais à peine du quartier du marché.
russian: У торговцев дела обычно с другими торговцами. Я чаще бывал в рыночном квартале.
bulgarian: A merchant's business is usually with other merchants. Most of my time was spent in the market quarter.

english: Still, it's interesting to think we might have walked right by each other!
french: Mais c'est drôle de se dire qu'on aurait pu se croiser !
russian: Всё равно занимательно, что мы с тобой ходили по одним и тем же улицам.
bulgarian: Still, it's interesting to think we might have walked right by each other!

english: It sounds like you two saw very different sides of the Capital!
french: On dirait que vous n'avez pas vu la capitale de la même façon !
russian: Звучит так, будто вы были в двух разных столицах!
bulgarian: It sounds like you two saw very different sides of the Capital!

english: You really do have a knack for rustling up the rarest of goods, Balor.
french: C'est vrai que tu es doué pour dénicher les articles les plus rares, Balor.
russian: У тебя талант доставать редкие товары, Балор.
bulgarian: You really do have a knack for rustling up the rarest of goods, Balor.

english: I think I've got everything I need, but I'll keep it in mind.
french: J'ai tout ce qu'il me faut, mais je garde ta proposition en tête.
russian: Вроде у меня есть всё, что нужно, но я буду иметь в виду.
bulgarian: I think I've got everything I need, but I'll keep it in mind.

english: How's the Clinic, Valen? Anything I can special order for you?
french: Tout se passe bien à la clinique, Valen ? Tu n'as besoin de rien en particulier ?
russian: Вален, как клиника? Тебе нужны какие-нибудь особенные заказы?
bulgarian: How's the Clinic, Valen? Anything I can special order for you?

english: Hah... big words, bartender. We'll flip our hands on three. One... two... three!
french: Ha... Que tu dis, tavernier. On montre nos cartes à trois. Un... deux... trois !
russian: Ха! Громкие слова от бармена. Раскрываем руки на три. Раз... два... три!
bulgarian: Hah... big words, bartender. We'll flip our hands on three. One... two... three!

english: I think you're bluffing, merchant.
french: Tu bluffes, marchand.
russian: По-моему, ты блефуешь, торгаш.
bulgarian: I think you're bluffing, merchant.

english: Balor, it's always time for cards.
french: Balor, je suis toujours partant pour une soirée poker.
russian: Балор, я всегда готов сыграть в карты.
bulgarian: Balor, it's always time for cards.

english: What do you think? Is it time to get another night of cards going?
french: Alors ? On se prévoit une autre soirée poker ?
russian: Как насчёт ещё разок сыграть в карты вечером? Что думаешь?
bulgarian: What do you think? Is it time to get another night of cards going?

english: That's our Reina! She's always coming up with new recipes.
french: C'est grâce à notre Reina ! Elle invente toujours de nouvelles recettes.
russian: Это всё наша Рейна! Она всё время придумывает новые рецепты.
bulgarian: That's our Reina! She's always coming up with new recipes.

english: Mistria's only had access to local produce since the earthquake, but the Inn has still managed to have a nice and varied menu every day.
french: Depuis le tremblement de terre, on n'a accès qu'aux produits locaux. Ça n'empêche pas l'auberge de proposer des menus variés tous les jours.
russian: После землетрясения в Мистрии есть только продукты местного производства. Но в трактире всё равно справляются и подают разнообразные и вкусные блюда.
bulgarian: Mistria's only had access to local produce since the earthquake, but the Inn has still managed to have a nice and varied menu every day.

english: I tell you, the kids are obsessed. And then they always come back and tell us about it!
french: À vrai dire, les enfants adorent. Quand ils en reviennent, ils nous expliquent tout de A à Z.
russian: Я тебе говорю, дети просто в восторге! А потом они приходят к нам и рассказывают.
bulgarian: I tell you, the kids are obsessed. And then they always come back and tell us about it!

english: I bet they know more about Mistria's history than us grown-ups!
