english: I've always wondered about draconic culture... tell me, what are the societal and familial structures like? Holiday observances? Food?
french: Je me suis toujours interrogé sur la culture draconique... Qu'en est-il des structures sociétales et familiales ? Y a-t-il des jours que vous fêtez ? Et quid de la nourriture ?
russian: Я всегда интересовался культурой драконов... Расскажи, как были устроены ваш общественный и семейный уклады? Праздничные обычаи? Любимая пища?
bulgarian: I've always wondered about draconic culture... tell me, what are the societal and familial structures like? Holiday observances? Food?

english: While I receive compliments often enough, it is something else entirely to hear it from a being as long-lived as yourself.
french: Même si j'entends souvent des compliments, je dois dire que c'est tout à fait différent venant de quelqu'un qui a vécu si longtemps que vous.
russian: Я часто получаю комплименты, однако услышать подобное от такого долгожителя, как ты, — нечто весьма особенное.
bulgarian: While I receive compliments often enough, it is something else entirely to hear it from a being as long-lived as yourself.

english: Thank you, Caldarus.
french: Merci, Caldarus.
russian: Спасибо, Кальдарус.
bulgarian: Thank you, Caldarus.

english: Elsie... I have seen many a performance, but your singing is unique among all of them.
french: Elsie... J'ai assisté à de nombreuses performances artistiques, mais je dois dire que votre tour de chant est tout à fait unique en son genre.
russian: Элси... Я видел множество представлений, но ваше пение отличается от них всех.
bulgarian: Elsie... I have seen many a performance, but your singing is unique among all of them.

english: Oh! You're observant in these matters, Caldarus.
french: Oh ! Vous êtes très attentif à ce genre de choses, Caldarus.
russian: Ого! Ты весьма наблюдателен, Кальдарус.
bulgarian: Oh! You're observant in these matters, Caldarus.

english: Yes, a memory. A happy one!
french: En effet, c'était un souvenir. Mais un souvenir joyeux !
russian: Да, это было воспоминание. И очень приятное!
bulgarian: Yes, a memory. A happy one!

english: Pardon me, Elsie, but in the middle of your last song... you seemed to be feeling something quite deeply. An old memory?
french: Pardonnez-moi, Elsie, mais au cours de votre dernière chanson... vous sembliez ressentir quelque chose de très profond. Un ancien souvenir ?
russian: Прошу прощения, Элси, в середине прошлой песни... Вас как будто захватило глубокое чувство. Воспоминание былых лет?
bulgarian: Pardon me, Elsie, but in the middle of your last song... you seemed to be feeling something quite deeply. An old memory?

english: Oho! If you'd like recommendations, I'm your girl!
french: Oh ho ! Si vous voulez des recommandations, comptez sur moi !
russian: Хо-хо! Если тебе нужны рекомендации, обращайся ко мне!
bulgarian: Oho! If you'd like recommendations, I'm your girl!

english: Mortals created so much music while I slumbered. To hear it all, now that I am awake... It is rather exciting, Elsie.
french: Les mortels ont créé tant de musique pendant mon sommeil. Le fait de pouvoir entendre tout cela maintenant que je suis réveillé... c'est un plaisir, Elsie.
russian: Смертные сочинили так много музыки, пока я спал. А теперь, проснувшись... мне весьма интересно послушать, Элси.
bulgarian: Mortals created so much music while I slumbered. To hear it all, now that I am awake... It is rather exciting, Elsie.

english: Why yes, thank you. My plate overflows with potatoes.
french: Je crois que oui, merci. Mon assiette déborde littéralement.
russian: Конечно, спасибо. Моя тарелка переполнена картофелем.
bulgarian: Why yes, thank you. My plate overflows with potatoes.

english: And what of the quiche? Another slice, perhaps?
french: Une autre part de quiche, peut-être ?
russian: А как насчёт киша? Может, ещё кусочек?
bulgarian: And what of the quiche? Another slice, perhaps?

english: I am appreciative, but I have enough slices.
french: J'apprécie la proposition, mais j'en ai déjà suffisamment.
russian: Благодарю, однако у меня уже достаточно кусков.
bulgarian: I am appreciative, but I have enough slices.

english: Don't mind us, Lord Caldarus. We're simply thinking of your health!
french: Ne nous en veuillez pas, Seigneur Caldarus. Nous nous préoccupons pour votre santé, rien de plus !
russian: Не подумайте плохого, лорд Кальдарус. Мы всего лишь думаем о вашем здоровье!
bulgarian: Don't mind us, Lord Caldarus. We're simply thinking of your health!

english: You're a guest, I can't let you go hungry!
french: En tant qu'invité, je ne peux pas vous laisser mourir de faim !
russian: Ты у нас гость — не отпускать же тебя голодным!
bulgarian: You're a guest, I can't let you go hungry!

english: You got enough potatoes, Caldarus?
french: Vous avez assez de patates, Caldarus ?
russian: Тебе хватает картофеля, Кальдарус?
bulgarian: You got enough potatoes, Caldarus?

english: Yes, they have a most interesting flavor. Smoky and sweet!
french: Oui, leur goût est très intéressant. Ils sont à la fois fumés et légèrement sucrés !
russian: Точно, у них весьма интересный вкус. Сладкий и подкопчёный!
bulgarian: Yes, they have a most interesting flavor. Smoky and sweet!

english: Ah, it was intended to be a cake. But perhaps I baked it too long... or too hot?
french: Ah, c'était censé être un gâteau. Mais je l'ai peut-être fait cuire trop longtemps... ou trop fort ?
russian: А, это должен был быть торт. Вероятно, я пёк его слишком долго... Или при слишком высокой температуре?
bulgarian: Ah, it was intended to be a cake. But perhaps I baked it too long... or too hot?

english: You see, it shattered when I retrieved it from the oven.
french: Car voyez-vous, il est tombé en miettes au moment où je l'ai sorti du four.
russian: Дело в том, что он рассыпался, когда я достал его из печи.
bulgarian: You see, it shattered when I retrieved it from the oven.

english: Regardless, I am grateful you are enjoying my latest culinary endeavor.
french: Mais quoi qu'il en soit, je suis heureux de voir que vous appréciez ma dernière réalisation culinaire.
russian: В любом случае, благодарю вас, что оценили моё новое кулинарное творение.
bulgarian: Regardless, I am grateful you are enjoying my latest culinary endeavor.

english: Caldarus, thanks so much for bringing the... hrm. Croutons?
french: Caldarus, merci beaucoup d'avoir apporté les, hum... croûtons ?
russian: Кальдарус, спасибо большое за... кхм, сухарики?
bulgarian: Caldarus, thanks so much for bringing the... hrm. Croutons?

english: I must know, are you simply a natural born chef? Or is there a trick to it?
french: Il faut que je sache : est-ce un talent inné, ou as-tu un secret ?
russian: Скажи мне: ты прирождённый кулинар? Или у тебя есть какой-то секрет?
bulgarian: I must know, are you simply a natural born chef? Or is there a trick to it?

english: Shucks, thank you! I dunno about natural talent... I just do what Grandma taught me.
french: Ben ça alors, merci ! Je ne sais pas si c'est un talent inné... Je reproduis ce que ma grand-mère m'a appris.
russian: Да ладно! Спасибо. Насчёт прирождённого таланта не знаю... Я просто делаю, как учила бабушка.
bulgarian: Shucks, thank you! I dunno about natural talent... I just do what Grandma taught me.

english: But I do have a secret ingredient that always makes any dish better...
french: Mais j'ai bien un ingrédient secret qui améliore n'importe quel plat...
russian: Но у меня и правда есть секретный ингредиент. С ним любое блюдо вкуснее...
bulgarian: But I do have a secret ingredient that always makes any dish better...

english: Oh yes?
french: Ah oui ?
russian: И что же это?
bulgarian: Oh yes?

english: Extra $Butter$!
french: Une double dose de $beurre$ !
russian: Больше $масла$!
bulgarian: Extra $Butter$!

english: I thank you for sharing your treasured family secret, Hayden.
french: Je vous remercie d'avoir partagé votre précieux secret de famille, Hayden.
russian: Благодарю тебя, Хейден, что поделился ценным семейным секретом.
bulgarian: I thank you for sharing your treasured family secret, Hayden.

english: This knowledge will serve me well when I am next in the kitchen.
french: Je saurai utiliser ce savoir nouvellement acquis à bon escient, la prochaine fois que je me mettrai aux fourneaux.
russian: Я воспользуюсь этой мудростью, когда в следующий раз возьмусь за готовку.
bulgarian: This knowledge will serve me well when I am next in the kitchen.

english: Hayden, your home cooking is always excellent!
french: Hayden, ta cuisine est excellente, comme d'habitude !
russian: Хейден, твоя домашняя еда как всегда превосходна!
bulgarian: Hayden, your home cooking is always excellent!

english: Oh yeah, he's talked my ear off about them! He says this old farm sits on top of a site from the Alda age.
french: Ah oui, il m'a bassiné avec ça ! Il dit que cette vieille ferme est située sur un site qui remonte à l'époque aldarienne.
russian: О, да, он мне тоже все уши прожужжал! Говорит, что под моей фермой скопление древностей альдийской эпохи.
bulgarian: Oh yeah, he's talked my ear off about them! He says this old farm sits on top of a site from the Alda age.

english: I leave all that broken pottery to Eiland and [Ari]. I don't suppose it means anything to you?
french: Je laisse volontiers toutes ces poteries cassées à Eiland et [Ari]. Je suppose que vous n'y êtes pas attaché, vous ?
russian: Я все эти черепки оставляю, пусть разбираются Эйланд и [Ari]. Или тебе тоже нужны?
bulgarian: I leave all that broken pottery to Eiland and [Ari]. I don't suppose it means anything to you?

english: Alas, it was after my time... so I can comprehend neither the significance nor meaning of Alda works.
french: Hélas, c'est ultérieur à mon époque... donc je ne comprends ni l'importance ni la signification des œuvres de l'époque aldarienne.
russian: Увы, это было уже после меня... Так что я не смогу оценить важность и смысл изделий из Альды.
bulgarian: Alas, it was after my time... so I can comprehend neither the significance nor meaning of Alda works.

english: Then it's gibberish to the both of us!
french: Alors c'est du charabia pour nous deux !
russian: Выходит, мы оба в этом ничего не смыслим!
bulgarian: Then it's gibberish to the both of us!

english: GYA HA HA!
french: GAH HA HA !
russian: ГА-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: GYA HA HA!

english: Eiland tells me this farm is unusually rich in artifacts ornamented in bronze and lapis lazuli.
french: Eiland m'a dit que cette ferme renfermait une quantité exceptionnelle d'artéfacts ornés de bronze et de lapis-lazuli.
russian: Эйланд говорит, что на этой ферме встречается необыкновенно много артефактов из бронзы и ляпис-лазури.
bulgarian: Eiland tells me this farm is unusually rich in artifacts ornamented in bronze and lapis lazuli.

english: Now they will even eat from my hand. I appreciate such trust towards one they might see as a beast of prey.
french: À présent, ils viennent même me manger dans la main. J'apprécie une telle confiance envers une créature qu'ils pourraient prendre pour un prédateur.
russian: Теперь они даже берут еду у меня из рук. Я впечатлён их доверием, ведь они могли бы счесть меня хищником.
bulgarian: Now they will even eat from my hand. I appreciate such trust towards one they might see as a beast of prey.

english: I'd say the critters of Sweetwater Farm are all pretty straight-forward...
french: Je dirais que les animaux de la ferme de Doucerive sont faciles à vivre.
russian: По-моему, у нас на ферме «сладководье» все мыслят очень просто...
bulgarian: I'd say the critters of Sweetwater Farm are all pretty straight-forward...

english: Feed 'em once and you've got a friend for life!
french: Il suffit de les nourrir une fois pour devenir les meilleurs amis du monde !
russian: Покормил разок — значит, друг на всю жизнь!
bulgarian: Feed 'em once and you've got a friend for life!

english: And I'm no exception!
french: Et je suis un peu comme eux !
russian: Меня это тоже касается!
bulgarian: And I'm no exception!

english: The animals of this farm were wary of me, at first... but lately we have grown closer.
french: Les animaux de cette ferme semblaient se méfier de moi, au début... mais nous avons fini par nous rapprocher, ces derniers temps.
russian: Вначале животные на этой ферме меня побаивались... Но в последнее время мы подружились.
bulgarian: The animals of this farm were wary of me, at first... but lately we have grown closer.

english: Humans and animals have been living together and changing each other for as long as humans have been around, I reckon.
french: Les humains et les animaux vivent ensemble et s'adaptent les uns aux autres depuis les origines de l'humanité, il me semble.
russian: Люди и животные живут вместе и подстраиваются друг под друга. Думаю, ещё с тех пор, как вообще появились люди.
bulgarian: Humans and animals have been living together and changing each other for as long as humans have been around, I reckon.

english: We've learned to trust and rely on each other!
french: Nous avons appris à nous faire confiance et à compter les uns sur les autres !
russian: Мы научились доверять и полагаться друг на друга!
bulgarian: We've learned to trust and rely on each other!

english: In fact, all the critters down here love a good pet. You're welcome to give it a try, Cal!
french: D'ailleurs, tous ceux qui sont ici aiment se faire cajoler. N'hésitez pas à essayer de les caresser, Caldarus !
russian: И, кстати, Кальд, тут всем зверям нравится, когда их гладят. Можешь попробовать, если хочешь!
bulgarian: In fact, all the critters down here love a good pet. You're welcome to give it a try, Cal!

english: In that case... I shall.
french: Dans ce cas... je vais m'y atteler.
russian: В таком случае... да, я попробую.
bulgarian: In that case... I shall.

english: The demeanor of the creatures here differs from those in the wild. They seem to enjoy the company and affection of humans.
french: Les créatures d'ici ont un comportement très différent de celles qui vivent à l'état sauvage. Elles semblent apprécier la compagnie et l'affection des humains.
russian: Здешние звери своими повадками отличаются от диких. Судя по всему, им нравится общество людей и их забота.
bulgarian: The demeanor of the creatures here differs from those in the wild. They seem to enjoy the company and affection of humans.

english: It's hard work for sure, but I like it! It feels good, walking around town and seeing all the effort you've put in.
french: Ouais, c'est sûr que c'est pas évident, mais j'aime ça ! C'est agréable de se balader en ville et de voir les résultats de mes efforts.
russian: Это верно, работа непростая. Но мне нравится! Приятно ходить по городу и видеть результат своих трудов.
bulgarian: It's hard work for sure, but I like it! It feels good, walking around town and seeing all the effort you've put in.

english: Much goes into keeping the town in good condition. Watching you, I am learning to appreciate how laborious it truly is.
french: Maintenir la ville en bon état nécessite beaucoup de travail. Plus je vous observe, plus je me rends compte à quel point c'est un dur labeur.
russian: На поддержание города в хорошем состоянии уходит много сил. Наблюдая за тобой, я начинаю понимать, насколько это тяжёлый труд.
bulgarian: Much goes into keeping the town in good condition. Watching you, I am learning to appreciate how laborious it truly is.

english: I would like to hammer something, too. Might I borrow your tools?
french: J'aimerais bien donner des coups de marteau sur quelque chose, moi-même. Puis-je vous emprunter vos outils ?
russian: Мне тоже нужно кое-что приколотить. Могу я одолжить твои инструменты?
bulgarian: I would like to hammer something, too. Might I borrow your tools?

english: I'm gonna need special permission from Adeline for that...
french: Je dois demander une dérogation spéciale à Adeline, pour ça...
russian: На такое мне лучше получить разрешение у Аделины...
bulgarian: I'm gonna need special permission from Adeline for that...

english: I have watched you make a number of repairs, and it has made me realize...
french: Je vous ai vu effectuer un certain nombre de réparations, et j'en suis venu à la conclusion que...
russian: Я видел, как ты ремонтируешь вещи, и кое-что осознал...
bulgarian: I have watched you make a number of repairs, and it has made me realize...

english: Absolutely. Without <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none>, we would still be putting the pieces together after the earthquake. <he>His</he><she>Her</she><they>Their</they><it>Its</it><none>[Ari]'s</none> hard work really made a difference!
french: Absolument. Sans <he>lui</he><she>elle</she><they>ellui</they>, on serait encore en train de déblayer les dégâts du tremblement de terre. Tout son travail acharné a vraiment fait la différence !

bulgarian: Absolutely. Without <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none>, we would still be putting the pieces together after the earthquake. <he>His</he><she>Her</she><they>Their</they><it>Its</it><none>[Ari]'s</none> hard work really made a difference!

english: [Ari] has done much to make this town shine. <he>He works</he><she>She works</she><they>They work</they><it>It works</it><none>[Ari] works</none> hard in all aspects of <he>his</he><she>her</she><they>their</they><it>its</it><none>[Ari]'s</none> life, it seems.

english: It is not of any true importance, but it is... nostalgic.
french: Ce n'est pas d'une importance capitale, mais c'est plus... de la nostalgie.
russian: Это не очень важно, просто... ностальгия.
bulgarian: It is not of any true importance, but it is... nostalgic.

english: I like a challenge! Tell me more, and I'll keep it in mind when I'm out foraging.
french: Aucun défi ne me fait peur ! Dites-m'en plus et j'y penserai quand je serai à la recherche d'ingrédients sauvages.
russian: Звучит как вызов! Расскажи мне, я буду иметь в виду, когда пойду собирать травы.
bulgarian: I like a challenge! Tell me more, and I'll keep it in mind when I'm out foraging.

english: Juniper, there is a scent I was hoping you might be able to recreate.
french: Juniper, j'espérais que vous puissiez recréer une odeur pour moi.
russian: Джунипер, ты можешь попробовать воссоздать для меня один запах?
bulgarian: Juniper, there is a scent I was hoping you might be able to recreate.

english: I guess it never occurred to me that dragons wouldn't be of a mind with one another.
french: Je crois que le fait que des dragons puissent ne pas partager le même point de vue ne m'avait jamais traversé l'esprit.
russian: Мне не приходило в голову, что драконы могут не соглашаться друг с другом.
bulgarian: I guess it never occurred to me that dragons wouldn't be of a mind with one another.

english: Of a mind? With Seridia? I do not think such a thing is possible.
french: Avoir la même vision des choses que Seridia ? Je ne pense pas qu'une telle chose soit possible.
russian: Соглашаться? С Серидией? Не представляю, как это было бы возможно.
bulgarian: Of a mind? With Seridia? I do not think such a thing is possible.

english: To begin with, have you seen her sense of decor?
french: Déjà, avez-vous vu ses goûts en décoration ?
russian: Для начала: ты хоть видела, какое у неё чувство вкуса?
bulgarian: To begin with, have you seen her sense of decor?

english: You and Seridia have very different philosophies on things, don't you?
french: Seridia et vous avez des visions des choses très différentes, n'est-ce pas ?
russian: У вас с Серидией очень разные взгляды на мир.
bulgarian: You and Seridia have very different philosophies on things, don't you?

english: Is that right? Perhaps he can sense my appreciation for him...
french: Vraiment ? Il ressent peut-être que je l'apprécie...
russian: Правда? Возможно, он чувствует, что я его полюбил...
bulgarian: Is that right? Perhaps he can sense my appreciation for him...

english: He is a calming and stabilizing presence in this bathhouse.
french: Sa présence aux bains est source d'apaisement et stabilité.
russian: Он наполняет купальню спокойствием и умиротворённостью.
bulgarian: He is a calming and stabilizing presence in this bathhouse.

english: That's true.
french: C'est vrai.
russian: Это правда.
bulgarian: That's true.

english: Wait. What does that make me?
french: Une minute. Qu'est-ce que ça signifie pour moi ?
russian: Погоди. А что тогда делаю я?
bulgarian: Wait. What does that make me?

english: Dozy has always been friendly, but you get along with him more than I anticipated.
french: Dozy a toujours été de bonne composition, mais vous vous entendez mieux tous les deux que ce que je me serais imaginé.
russian: Дрёма дружит со всеми, но ты с ним поладил больше, чем я думала.
bulgarian: Dozy has always been friendly, but you get along with him more than I anticipated.

english: Of course. I'm an expert, after all.
french: Évidemment. Je ne suis pas experte pour rien.
russian: Ну конечно. В конце концов, я в этом специалист.
bulgarian: Of course. I'm an expert, after all.

english: But I suppose it was Celine who showed me where to do the best foraging. That country girl is surprising.
french: Je reconnais que c'est Céline qui m'a indiqué les meilleurs endroits pour la cueillette de produits sauvages. Cette fille de la campagne est surprenante.
russian: Хотя это Селин показала мне, где лучше всего собирать травы. Эта деревенская девчонка иногда удивляет.
bulgarian: But I suppose it was Celine who showed me where to do the best foraging. That country girl is surprising.

english: Yes... you both have a strong connection to this land.
french: Oui... Vous avez toutes les deux un lien très fort avec ces terres.
russian: Да... У вас обеих есть сильная связь с этой землёй.
bulgarian: Yes... you both have a strong connection to this land.

english: You are quite knowledgeable about what grows along the Eastern Road, Juniper.
french: Vous connaissez tout ce qui pousse le long de la route de l'est, Juniper.
russian: Ты многое знаешь о растениях у Западной дороги, Джунипер.
bulgarian: You are quite knowledgeable about what grows along the Eastern Road, Juniper.

english: It explains why I detected such unique magic emanating from <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none>.
french: Ça explique pourquoi je ressentais une force magique aussi unique émanant <he>de lui</he><she>d'elle</she><they>d'ellui</they>.
russian:
Это объясняет, почему я почувствовала в

них

нейнёмнём такую своеобразную магию.
bulgarian: It explains why I detected such unique magic emanating from <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none>.

english: I merely opened a door. [Ari] is capable of great things, with or without me.
french: Je n'ai fait que lui ouvrir les yeux. [Ari] est capable d'accomplir des choses incroyables, avec ou sans moi.
russian:
Я лишь раскрыл двери. [Ari]

способны

способнаспособенспособно на великие свершения — с моей помощью или без.
bulgarian: I merely opened a door. [Ari] is capable of great things, with or without me.

english: Still... I imagine having a dragon on your side doesn't hurt.
french: Certes, mais... j'imagine que s'allier avec un dragon doit aider.
russian: И всё-таки... Я полагаю, поддержка дракона была не лишней.
bulgarian: Still... I imagine having a dragon on your side doesn't hurt.

english: [Ari] told me that you're the one who lent <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> your power.
french: [Ari] m'a expliqué que c'était vous qui lui aviez prêté vos pouvoirs.
russian:
[Ari]

рассказывали

рассказываларассказывалрассказывало, что это ты даровал

им

ейемуему свою силу.
bulgarian: [Ari] told me that you're the one who lent <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> your power.

english: But you do not seem relaxed, Juniper. What is the matter?
french: Vous ne semblez pourtant pas détendue, Juniper. Quelque chose ne va pas ?
russian: Но ты выглядишь напряжённой, Джунипер. Что-то не так?
bulgarian: But you do not seem relaxed, Juniper. What is the matter?

english: Well, Seridia doesn't like you very much. I'm just hoping she doesn't see us foraging together.
french: Eh bien, Seridia ne vous porte pas dans son cœur. J'espère juste qu'elle ne nous surprendra pas ensemble en pleine cueillette.
russian: Ну, Серидия тебя не очень любит. Я переживаю, что она увидит, как мы вместе собираем травы.
bulgarian: Well, Seridia doesn't like you very much. I'm just hoping she doesn't see us foraging together.

english: Oh, do not worry. I know how to deal with her.
french: Oh, n'ayez crainte. Je sais comment gérer la situation avec elle.
russian: О, не волнуйся. Я знаю, как с ней общаться.
bulgarian: Oh, do not worry. I know how to deal with her.

english: If she asks, I will say that you are researching my weaknesses, or something of the like.
french: Si elle demande, je dirais que vous êtes en train de faire des recherches sur mes points faibles, ou quelque chose de ce genre.
russian: Если она спросит, я скажу, что ты исследуешь мои слабые места или что-нибудь в этом роде.
bulgarian: If she asks, I will say that you are researching my weaknesses, or something of the like.

english: You are right to be concerned, though. She can be quite... territorial.
french: Vous avez toutefois raison de vous en préoccuper. Elle peut se montrer assez... possessive.
russian: Но твои переживания не беспочвенны. Она бывает весьма... деспотична.
bulgarian: You are right to be concerned, though. She can be quite... territorial.

english: It is quite relaxing, seeking out herbs with you.
french: Cueillir des herbes avec vous a quelque chose d'apaisant.
russian: Для меня прогулка с тобой за травами — хороший отдых.
bulgarian: It is quite relaxing, seeking out herbs with you.

english: I wonder if Louis could craft something similar for me...
french: Je me demande si Louis pourrait me confectionner quelque chose dans ce genre...
russian: Может, Луи сможет и для меня сделать что-то похожее.
bulgarian: I wonder if Louis could craft something similar for me...

english: If it would assist in your pursuit, I would not mind loaning you a garment for pattern-making.
french: Si cela peut vous aider, je suis disposé à vous prêter une tenue pour réaliser le patron.
russian: Я не против одолжить своё одеяние в качестве образца, если тебе это поможет.
bulgarian: If it would assist in your pursuit, I would not mind loaning you a garment for pattern-making.

english: Oh ho, me too, me too! Who couldn't use a flashy robe or two!
french: Ho ho, et à moi aussi ! J'ai bien besoin de quelques vêtements un peu plus tape-à-l'œil !
russian: Хо-хо, и мне, и мне! Эффектный костюмчик ещё никогда не мешал!
bulgarian: Oh ho, me too, me too! Who couldn't use a flashy robe or two!

english: A layered look with a big silhouette... nice style, Caldarus.
french: Des strates de vêtements pour une silhouette imposante... Vous avez un style irréprochable, Caldarus.
russian: Многослойный образ с широким кроем... У тебя отличный стиль, Кальдарус.
bulgarian: A layered look with a big silhouette... nice style, Caldarus.

english: In an earlier age, their name translated to "red candle wick." Do you know the modern name, Ryis?
french: À une époque lointaine, leur nom se serait traduit par « mèche de bougie allumée ». Savez-vous comment on les appelle de nos jours, Ryis ?
russian: В былую эпоху она носила имя, означающее «красный воск». Ты не знаешь, как их называют сейчас, Риз?
bulgarian: In an earlier age, their name translated to "red candle wick." Do you know the modern name, Ryis?

english: These days we call them ember tanagers. Striking, right?
french: Ce sont des passereaux flamboyants. C'est révélateur, non ?
russian: Сейчас мы называем их пламенные овсянки. Поразительно, да?
bulgarian: These days we call them ember tanagers. Striking, right?

english: Cool how everyone clues in on the fiery thing they have going on.
french: C'est surprenant de voir que tout le monde met l'accent sur leur ressemblance aux flammes.
russian: Забавно, что все находят в них что-то огненное.
bulgarian: Cool how everyone clues in on the fiery thing they have going on.

english: Anything you need to know about birds, Ryis is your guy!
french: Pour tout ce qui concerne les oiseaux, il suffit de demander à Ryis !
russian: Если будут вопросы по птицам, сразу спрашивай Риза!
bulgarian: Anything you need to know about birds, Ryis is your guy!

english: You don't have to over-sell me like that, Uncle...
french: Ce n'est pas la peine d'exagérer mes mérites comme ça, oncle Landen...
russian: Дядя, незачем меня так нахваливать...
bulgarian: You don't have to over-sell me like that, Uncle...

english: He's right, though.
french: Même s'il a raison.
russian: Но он прав, я отвечу.
bulgarian: He's right, though.

english: I have observed a red-crested bird quite common to this region.
french: J'ai observé des oiseaux à crête rouge qui semblent assez répandus dans la région.
russian: Недавно я встретил характерную для этих мест птицу с красным хохолком.
bulgarian: I have observed a red-crested bird quite common to this region.

english: Now that we've got all these new faces in town, it's going to be a proper party!
french: Avec ces nouveaux habitants en ville, je me disais que nous devrions vraiment marquer le coup !
russian: Раз у нас в городе новые лица, пора покутить как следует!
bulgarian: Now that we've got all these new faces in town, it's going to be a proper party!

english: Uncle...
french: Oncle Landen...
russian: Дядя...
bulgarian: Uncle...

english: You and me, we're gonna paint the town red!
french: Vous et moi, nous allons faire une fête de tous les diables !
russian: Оттянемся с тобой на всю катушку!
bulgarian: You and me, we're gonna paint the town red!

english: An all-night rager!
french: On va festoyer toute la nuit !
russian: Будем куролесить до утра!
bulgarian: An all-night rager!

english: Come on, Cal! What do you say?
french: Allez, Cal ! Qu'est-ce que vous en pensez ?
russian: Ну же, Кальд! Как тебе идея?
bulgarian: Come on, Cal! What do you say?

french: Je...

english: Will endeavor to keep up.
french: Je ferai de mon mieux pour suivre votre rythme.
russian: Постараюсь не отставать.
bulgarian: Will endeavor to keep up.

english: I've been thinking, Caldarus...
french: Caldarus...
russian: Кальдарус, я тут подумал...
bulgarian: I've been thinking, Caldarus...

english: Baking soda reacts to acidity in the wet ingredients when they combine. Makes air bubbles, which makes the batter rise in the oven.
french: Le bicarbonate de soude réagit à l'acidité des ingrédients liquides lorsqu'ils se mélangent. Ça crée des bulles d'air qui permettent à la pâte de gonfler au four.
russian: Соприкасаясь с влажными ингредиентами, пищевая сода реагирует на их кислотность. Получаются пузырьки, от которых тесто лучше поднимается в печи.
bulgarian: Baking soda reacts to acidity in the wet ingredients when they combine. Makes air bubbles, which makes the batter rise in the oven.

english: It's all about timing.
french: Tout est une question de timing.
russian: Главное рассчитать время.
bulgarian: It's all about timing.

english: Cooking is far more alchemical than I ever realized... you are a font of knowledge, Ryis.
french: J'ignorais que l'alchimie avait une telle importance en cuisine... Vous êtes un vrai puits de science, Ryis.
russian: Я и не думал, что готовка так похожа на алхимию... Ты просто кладезь премудрости, Риз.
bulgarian: Cooking is far more alchemical than I ever realized... you are a font of knowledge, Ryis.

english: See, the secret to making a quick bread is you don't want the mixture to sit too long before baking it.
french: Vous voyez, le secret pour faire du pain rapidement, c'est de ne pas laisser reposer la pâte trop longtemps avant de la cuire.
russian: При работе с бездрожжевым тестом главное — не давать ему застояться перед выпечкой.
bulgarian: See, the secret to making a quick bread is you don't want the mixture to sit too long before baking it.

english: If you mix it too much, it pushes all the air out. Then your cake collapses in the oven and gets all dense.
french: Si vous la mélangez trop longtemps, tout l'air est expulsé et votre gâteau s'affaisse et devient compact, une fois passé au four.
russian: Если взбивать слишком интенсивно, то весь воздух выйдет. При запекании тесто осядет и станет слишком плотным.
bulgarian: If you mix it too much, it pushes all the air out. Then your cake collapses in the oven and gets all dense.

english: Incredible... my past mistakes are illuminated and laid bare.
french: C'est fascinant... Cela met en évidence toutes mes erreurs passées.
russian: Невероятно... Мои ошибки предстают ясно как на ладони.
bulgarian: Incredible... my past mistakes are illuminated and laid bare.

english: And you say you are a carpenter? It seems I have much to learn...
french: Et vous êtes menuisier, dites-vous ? J'ai visiblement encore beaucoup à apprendre...
russian: И при этом ты считаешь себя плотником? Вижу, мне ещё многому предстоит научиться...
bulgarian: And you say you are a carpenter? It seems I have much to learn...

english: Yeah, cake batter doesn't want too much attention.
french: Oui, il ne faut pas trop travailler la pâte à gâteaux.
russian: Ах, да, со смесью нужно быть аккуратным.
bulgarian: Yeah, cake batter doesn't want too much attention.

english: The more you agitate them, the more they break up. Then the texture comes out all wrong when you cook them.
french: Plus vous les remuez, plus ils se dissocient, ce qui altère leur texture au moment de les cuisiner.
russian: Если сильно взбалтывать, можно всё испортить. Текстура получится неправильная, когда будешь выпекать.
bulgarian: The more you agitate them, the more they break up. Then the texture comes out all wrong when you cook them.

english: Something simple like an omelette gets rubbery. For something delicate like meringue, it curdles.
french: Une chose aussi simple qu'une omelette devient vite caoutchouteuse, et une chose délicate comme de la meringue risque de tourner.
russian: Если это простой омлет, то он получится резиновый. А если что-то более тонкое вроде безе, то оно свернётся.
bulgarian: Something simple like an omelette gets rubbery. For something delicate like meringue, it curdles.

english: I see... even the humble omelette has its secrets.
french: Je vois... Alors même une modeste omelette a ses secrets.
russian: Понятно... Выходит, даже у скромного омлета есть свои секреты.
bulgarian: I see... even the humble omelette has its secrets.

english: You can't get too intense about whisking eggs.
french: Quand on bat des œufs, il ne faut pas y aller trop fort.
russian: Яйца никогда нельзя чрезмерно взбивать.
bulgarian: You can't get too intense about whisking eggs.

english: We are enjoying the musical ensemble that nature has provided.
french: Nous sommes en train de profiter de l'ensemble musical que dame nature a organisé pour nous.
russian: Мы наслаждаемся музыкальным ансамблем, который устроила для нас природа.
bulgarian: We are enjoying the musical ensemble that nature has provided.

english: It's pretty nice.
french: C'est très agréable.
russian: Звучит приятно.
bulgarian: It's pretty nice.

english: Hey, [Ari]. Want to join us?
french: Salut [Ari]. Tu veux te joindre à nous ?
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Хочешь с нами?
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. Want to join us?

english: I am certain that several generations of trees have lived within this ruin.
french: Je suis sûr que plusieurs générations d'arbres se sont succédé au sein de ces ruines.
russian: Я убеждён, что внутри этих руин сменилось несколько поколений деревьев.
bulgarian: I am certain that several generations of trees have lived within this ruin.

english: The old hawthorne tree we lost in the earthquake was hundreds of years old. So this building must be from before it was even a sprout.
french: L'arbre déraciné lors du tremblement de terre était une aubépine vieille de plusieurs centaines d'années. Ce bâtiment devait donc déjà être là avant qu'elle ne pousse.
russian: До землетрясения здесь рос боярышник, которому было несколько сотен лет. А это здание возникло ещё до того, как он появился на свет.
bulgarian: The old hawthorne tree we lost in the earthquake was hundreds of years old. So this building must be from before it was even a sprout.

english: Makes you think, right? How the Mistria we know is built on top of its past lives.
french: Ça donne à réfléchir, hein ? La ville de Mistria telle que nous la connaissons a été bâtie sur ses vies antérieures.
russian: Заставляет задуматься! Мистрия, какой мы её знаем, стоит на плечах прошлого.
bulgarian: Makes you think, right? How the Mistria we know is built on top of its past lives.

english: From decay, much can blossom.
french: Du déclin renaît la vie.
russian: Многие цветы растут из праха.
bulgarian: From decay, much can blossom.

english: Oh... I like that.
french: Oh... J'aime cette idée.
russian: О... Хорошо сказано.
bulgarian: Oh... I like that.

english: This wall looks more ancient than Mistria's modern architecture.
french: Ce mur semble ancien, comparé à l'architecture moderne de Mistria.
russian: Эта стена выглядит старше, чем современные мистрийские постройки.
bulgarian: This wall looks more ancient than Mistria's modern architecture.

english: It is wonderful to see a mortal who has mastered her destiny.
french: C'est merveilleux de voir une mortelle qui a pris le contrôle de son destin.
russian: Наблюдать за смертным, который взял судьбу в свои руки, — восхитительное зрелище.
bulgarian: It is wonderful to see a mortal who has mastered her destiny.

english: Oho... them's some pretty words, Caldarus.
french: Oh ho... Ce sont de bien belles paroles, Caldarus.
russian: Хо-хо... Какие красивые слова, Кальдарус.
bulgarian: Oho... them's some pretty words, Caldarus.

english: I'd better get serious... we'll both look pretty silly if I let the next fish get away!
french: Je n'ai pas intérêt à me relâcher... Si ma prochaine prise m'échappe, on aura tous les deux l'air bête !
russian: Значит, мне нельзя расслабляться... Теперь, если рыба от меня ускользнёт, мы оба будем выглядеть дураками.
bulgarian: I'd better get serious... we'll both look pretty silly if I let the next fish get away!

english: Watching you draw in a fish is like a poem with words in perfect arrangement.
french: Lorsque je vous vois remonter un poisson de la sorte, c'est comme un poème dont chaque mot a été parfaitement choisi.
russian: Когда ты вытягиваешь рыбу, ты словно плетёшь стихи, где каждое слово на своём месте.
bulgarian: Watching you draw in a fish is like a poem with words in perfect arrangement.

english: Don't it bother you that I'm out here fishing up all manner of critters?
french: Ça ne vous dérange pas que je passe ma vie à pêcher tout un tas de bestioles ?
russian: Тебя не беспокоит, что я ловлю в реке всякую живность?
bulgarian: Don't it bother you that I'm out here fishing up all manner of critters?

english: I am not bothered. After all, I ate great mouthfuls of fish when I was in my draconic form.
french: Pas le moins du monde. Après tout, j'ai moi-même englouti des quantités conséquentes de poisson lorsque je vivais sous ma forme de dragon.
russian: Меня это не тревожит. Ведь в драконьем обличье я и сам ел рыбу горстями.
bulgarian: I am not bothered. After all, I ate great mouthfuls of fish when I was in my draconic form.

english: You are judicious, and you are generous, and you are thankful. It is all one can ask.
french: Vous êtes sensée, généreuse et reconnaissante. Nul besoin d'en demander plus.
russian: Ты рассудительна, щедра и благодарна. О большем и просить не нужно.
bulgarian: You are judicious, and you are generous, and you are thankful. It is all one can ask.

english: Nature is a cycle. Life will come again.
french: La nature fonctionne par cycles. La vie renaît.
russian: Природа — это цикл. Жизнь всегда возвращается.
bulgarian: Nature is a cycle. Life will come again.

english: I've been wondering, Caldarus... you're one with nature and all that.
french: Caldarus, vous qui êtes si proche de la nature et tout ça, je me demandais...
russian: Кальдарус, я тут размышляла... Ты же един с природой и всё такое.
bulgarian: I've been wondering, Caldarus... you're one with nature and all that.

english: Sounds like the only fish you caught was yourself!
french: On dirait qu'un gros poisson a mordu à votre hameçon... mais c'était vous !
russian: Получается, на свою удочку сам же и попался!
bulgarian: Sounds like the only fish you caught was yourself!

english: KYA HA HA!
french: HÉ HÉ HÉ !
russian: КЯ-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: KYA HA HA!

english: I tried to catch fish with a rod like yours, Terithia, but my claws became tangled in the line. It was most vexing.
french: J'ai essayé de pêcher du poisson avec une canne comme la vôtre, Terithia, mais mes griffes se sont prises dans la ligne. Cela m'a fort déplu.
russian: Теризия, я попробовал ловить рыбу с такой же палкой, как у тебя. Но, к моему великому огорчению, я запутался в леске когтями.
bulgarian: I tried to catch fish with a rod like yours, Terithia, but my claws became tangled in the line. It was most vexing.

english: Awesome! It was so cool.
french: Génial ! C'était trop cool.
russian: Потрясающе! Всё очень круто.
bulgarian: Awesome! It was so cool.

english: That's what I like to hear!
french: Eh bien, tant mieux !
russian: Как приятно слышать!
bulgarian: That's what I like to hear!

english: But suspiciously light on the details...
french: Mais je te trouve ça bizarre que tu ne nous donnes pas de détails...
russian: Но подозрительно мало подробностей...
bulgarian: But suspiciously light on the details...

english: How was your day, Dell?
french: Comment s'est passée ta journée, Dell ?
russian: Как твой день, Делл?
bulgarian: How was your day, Dell?

english: You can have all the carrots! They're icky!
french: Prends-les toutes ! Je déteste ça !
russian: Да хоть всю забирай! Она противная.
bulgarian: You can have all the carrots! They're icky!

english: Carrots are good for your eyes. If you eat enough, you'll get eagle vision!
french: C'est excellent pour la vue pourtant. Si tu en manges beaucoup, tu auras un œil de lynx !
russian: Морковь полезна для глаз. Если будешь много есть, будешь зоркой, как орёл.
bulgarian: Carrots are good for your eyes. If you eat enough, you'll get eagle vision!

english: Wow! Give the carrots back dad, I'm gonna eat them all!
french: Quoi ? Redonne-moi les carottes, papa. Je vais tout manger !
russian: Ух ты! Отдай обратно, папа, сейчас всю её съем.
bulgarian: Wow! Give the carrots back dad, I'm gonna eat them all!

english: Just remember moderation, Dell. If you eat too many carrots, you'll turn orange.
french: N'exagère pas, Dell. Si tu manges trop de carottes, tu vas devenir orange.
russian: Всё хорошо в меру, Делл. Если съешь много моркови, станешь вся рыжая.
bulgarian: Just remember moderation, Dell. If you eat too many carrots, you'll turn orange.

english: But that's even COOLER!
french: Mais... c'est encore PLUS COOL !
russian: Но так даже круче!
bulgarian: But that's even COOLER!

english: Can you pass the carrots, Dell?
french: Tu peux me passer les carottes, Dell ?
russian: Делл, можешь передать морковь?
bulgarian: Can you pass the carrots, Dell?

english: I supervised!
french: Je l'ai surveillé !
russian: Я присматривала!
bulgarian: I supervised!

english: And I supervised Dell.
french: Et moi, j'ai surveillé Dell.
russian: А я присматривала за Делл.
bulgarian: And I supervised Dell.

english: Otherwise we'd be having candy salad for dinner!
french: Sinon, on aurait eu une salade de bonbons au dîner !
russian: Иначе у нас на обед был бы конфетный салат.
bulgarian: Otherwise we'd be having candy salad for dinner!

english: Did you help Dad make dinner, Dell?
french: Tu as aidé papa à préparer le dîner, Dell ?
russian: Ты помогала папе с обедом, Делл?
bulgarian: Did you help Dad make dinner, Dell?

english: It's so pretty!
french: Il est vraiment joli !
russian: Он такой красивый!
bulgarian: It's so pretty!

english: Yes, and it makes a wonderful habitat for our insect friends.
french: Oui, et c'est l'habitat idéal pour nos amis les insectes.
russian: И это отличная среда обитания для наших друзей-насекомых.
bulgarian: Yes, and it makes a wonderful habitat for our insect friends.

english: This garden is Dragonguard approved!
french: Ce jardin est validé par la Garde des dragons !
russian: Драконья стража одобряет!
bulgarian: This garden is Dragonguard approved!

english: What does the Dragonguard think of my garden?
french: Que pense la Garde des dragons de mon jardin ?
russian: Что Драконья стража думает о моём саде?
bulgarian: What does the Dragonguard think of my garden?

english: Your dinners are like Reina's, but... greener.
french: Tes repas sont aussi bons que ceux de Reina... en plus verts.
russian: У тебя блюда, как у неё... только зеленее.
bulgarian: Your dinners are like Reina's, but... greener.

english: More leafy. I feel like a caterpillar when I have dinner at your house.
french: Et avec de la salade. J'ai l'impression d'être une chenille quand je mange chez toi.
russian: С листочками. Я чувствую себя гусеницей, когда обедаю у вас.
bulgarian: More leafy. I feel like a caterpillar when I have dinner at your house.

english: I like to pretend I'm the princess of the veggie kingdom!
french: J'aime faire semblant d'être la princesse du royaume des légumes !
russian: Я представляю, что я принцесса вегетарианского королевства!
bulgarian: I like to pretend I'm the princess of the veggie kingdom!

english: I'm no Reina, but I hope you liked dinner all the same!
french: Je n'ai pas les talents de cuisinière de Reina, mais j'espère que le dîner vous a plu !
russian: Я, конечно, не Рейна, но, надеюсь, обед вам понравился!
bulgarian: I'm no Reina, but I hope you liked dinner all the same!

english: It's important! You have to eat them, even if you think they're the ickiest thing ever!
french: C'est important ! Tu dois les manger, même si tu trouves ça dégoûtant !
russian: Именно! Их нужно есть, даже если кажется, что они ужасно противные.
bulgarian: It's important! You have to eat them, even if you think they're the ickiest thing ever!

english: My big sister says bullying is wrong! Tell them, Celine!
french: Ma grande sœur dit que ce n'est pas bien de forcer les autres ! Dis-leur, Céline !
russian: Моя старшая сестра говорит, нехорошо издеваться над людьми! Правда, Селин?
bulgarian: My big sister says bullying is wrong! Tell them, Celine!

english: Eat your vegetables, Dell.
french: Mange tes légumes, Dell.
russian: Ешь овощи, Делл.
bulgarian: Eat your vegetables, Dell.

english: Eat your vegetables, Dell! How else will you grow up to be a big strong knight?
french: Mange tes légumes, Dell ! Sinon, tu ne deviendras jamais une grande chevaleresse !
russian: Надо есть овощи, Делл! Иначе как ты станешь большим сильным рыцарем?
bulgarian: Eat your vegetables, Dell! How else will you grow up to be a big strong knight?

english: It's a secret, Celine.
french: C'est un secret, Céline.
russian: Это секрет, Селин.
bulgarian: It's a secret, Celine.

english: Classified.
french: Top secret.
russian: Закрытая информация.
bulgarian: Classified.

english: We'll tell you if you join the Dragonguard!
french: Tu le sauras seulement si tu rejoins la Garde des dragons !
russian: Мы расскажем, если вступишь в Драконью стражу.
bulgarian: We'll tell you if you join the Dragonguard!

english: Who gave the kids chocolate at his hour?
french: Qui a donné du chocolat aux enfants à cette heure-ci ?
russian: Кто дал детям шоколад так поздно вечером?
bulgarian: Who gave the kids chocolate at his hour?

english: Yeah! I'm going to grow so many hot peppers!
french: Oui ! J'ai décidé de faire pousser plein de piments rouges !
russian: Да! У меня будет просто куча острых перцев!
bulgarian: Yeah! I'm going to grow so many hot peppers!

english: I'm going to grow lots of flowers so the insects have something to pollinate!
french: Et moi, je vais faire pousser plein de fleurs pour que les insectes puissent polliniser !
russian: Я буду выращивать цветы, чтобы насекомым было что опылять.
bulgarian: I'm going to grow lots of flowers so the insects have something to pollinate!

english: I'm growing potatoes... so many potatoes... this is where my potato empire begins!
french: Et moi, je vais faire pousser des pommes de terre... pour fonder un empire de la patate !
russian: У меня будет картошка... Много картошки... Здесь начнётся моя картофельная империя!
bulgarian: I'm growing potatoes... so many potatoes... this is where my potato empire begins!

english: I'll have to think of a special meal to cook with all three when it's harvest time!
french: Il faudra que je trouve comment cuisiner tout ça quand ce sera l'heure de la récolte !
russian: Надо будет что-нибудь приготовить вместе, когда соберём урожай!
bulgarian: I'll have to think of a special meal to cook with all three when it's harvest time!

english: How are you kids doing? Getting the hang of gardening?
french: Comment ça va, les enfants ? Vous commencez à apprécier le jardinage ?
russian: Как ваши дела, ребята? Справляетесь тут, в саду?
bulgarian: How are you kids doing? Getting the hang of gardening?

english: Yes, Queen Maple!
french: À vos ordres, reine Maple !
russian: Да, королева Мэйпл!
bulgarian: Yes, Queen Maple!

english: Royal dirt for your royal highness!
french: De la terre royale pour Sa Majesté !
russian: Королевская грязь для вашего королевского величества!
bulgarian: Royal dirt for your royal highness!

english: Thank you all so much for helping out! I'll think of you every time I look out at my garden.
french: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide, tout le monde ! Je penserai à vous à chaque fois que je regarderai mon jardin.
russian: Спасибо вам всем большое! Я каждый раз о вас вспоминаю, когда смотрю на свой сад.
bulgarian: Thank you all so much for helping out! I'll think of you every time I look out at my garden.

english: Are you sure it's not Queen Maple's garden?
french: Tu es sûre que ce n'est pas plutôt le jardin de la reine Maple ?
russian: Ты уверена, что это не сад королевы Мэйпл?
bulgarian: Are you sure it's not Queen Maple's garden?

english: More dirt! More dirt, I say!
french: Plus de terre ! Plus de terre, j'ai dit !
russian: Больше грязи! Я сказала, больше грязи!
bulgarian: More dirt! More dirt, I say!

english: Can you guess what Dell has us looking at?
french: Essaie de deviner ce que Dell a envie de voir...
russian: Догадайся с трёх раз, что Делл хочет посмотреть?
bulgarian: Can you guess what Dell has us looking at?

english: Swords! Swords! Swords!
french: Les épées ! Les épées ! Les épées !
russian: Мечи! Мечи! Мечи!
bulgarian: Swords! Swords! Swords!

english: Oh, hi [Ari]. We thought we'd bring Dell to the Museum today, since it's too rainy for her to play swords outside.
french: Oh, c'est toi, [Ari]. On a décidé d'emmener Dell au musée aujourd'hui, vu qu'il pleut trop dehors pour jouer à l'épée.
russian: О, привет, [Ari]. Мы хотели сегодня сводить Делл в музей, потому что на улице не та погода для игр с мечами.
bulgarian: Oh, hi [Ari]. We thought we'd bring Dell to the Museum today, since it's too rainy for her to play swords outside.

english: You'd do well in the Capital! None of those nobles has done anything so thoughtful with their gardens.
french: On s'arracherait tes services dans la capitale ! Aucune famille de l'aristocratie n'a jamais eu de jardin aussi élégant.
russian: Ты бы отлично устроилась в столице! Никто из тамошней знати не относится к своему саду так внимательно.
bulgarian: You'd do well in the Capital! None of those nobles has done anything so thoughtful with their gardens.

english: Aw, thank you! I don't know if the city is for me, though. I'm a country girl at heart!
french: Merci, c'est gentil ! Mais je ne suis pas sûre d'être faite pour la ville. Je suis une fille de la campagne !
russian: Ох, спасибо! Но не думаю, что мне найдётся место в городе. В душе я деревенская девчонка!
bulgarian: Aw, thank you! I don't know if the city is for me, though. I'm a country girl at heart!

english: Celine, you've done such a beautiful job with the garden.
french: Céline, ce jardin est absolument magnifique grâce à toi.
russian: Селин, у тебя выходит такой прелестный сад.
bulgarian: Celine, you've done such a beautiful job with the garden.

english: We were just talking about... um...
french: Nous étions juste en train de discuter de... hum...
russian: Мы тут обсуждали... эм...
bulgarian: We were just talking about... um...

english: A bit of this and that. Be a dear and allow us some privacy, won't you?
french: De choses et d'autres. Tu serais un amour si tu pouvais nous laisser.
russian:
Всякую всячину. Будь

добры

добрадобрдобро, дай нам погворить наедине, пожалуйста.
bulgarian: A bit of this and that. Be a dear and allow us some privacy, won't you?

english: Oh, [Ari]! When did you get here?
french: Oh, [Ari] ! Ça fait longtemps que tu es là ?
russian: Ой, [Ari]! Ты давно здесь стоишь?
bulgarian: Oh, [Ari]! When did you get here?

english: I'm glad to know someone who likes flowers as much as I do. They really do transform a room!
french: Je suis ravie de connaître quelqu'un qui aime les fleurs autant que moi. Elles transforment littéralement une pièce !
russian: Рада, что рядом есть кто-то, кто любит цветы, как я. Они преображают всю комнату!
bulgarian: I'm glad to know someone who likes flowers as much as I do. They really do transform a room!

english: They do! And I admit, I got used to having them in the Capital. My adoring fans spared no expense.
french: Effectivement ! Et je dois avouer que je me suis habituée à en avoir quand je vivais dans la capitale. Mes admirateurs m'en envoyaient sans arrêt.
russian: Это правда! И, признаюсь, в столице я привыкла держать цветы. Мои обожатели не жалели на них денег.
bulgarian: They do! And I admit, I got used to having them in the Capital. My adoring fans spared no expense.

english: You're so sweet, Celine! You always take my request for flowers so seriously.
french: Tu es adorable, Céline ! Tu prends toujours mes demandes de fleurs très au sérieux.
russian: Какая ты милая, Селин! Всегда серьёзно относишься к моим просьбам о цветах.
bulgarian: You're so sweet, Celine! You always take my request for flowers so seriously.

english: Oh, thank you!
french: Oh, merci !
russian: Ой, спасибо!
bulgarian: Oh, thank you!

english: I'm fond of the manor garden in the cold season... it's so pretty!
french: J'adore les jardins du manoir à la saison froide... Ils sont si beaux !
russian: Мне нравится бывать в саду особняка зимой... Он такой красивый!
bulgarian: I'm fond of the manor garden in the cold season... it's so pretty!

english: It's a winter wonderland out here! And you look perfectly suited to it, Celine!
french: Cet endroit est merveilleux en hiver ! Et tu y as toute ta place, Céline !
russian: На дворе царит настоящая зимняя сказка! А ты смотришься, как главная героиня, Селин!
bulgarian: It's a winter wonderland out here! And you look perfectly suited to it, Celine!

english: Really? Flowers talk to each other? The Codex Mistria didn't cover this...
french: Vraiment ? Les fleurs communiquent entre elles ? Je n'ai rien lu là-dessus dans le Codex Mistria...
russian: Правда? Цветы разговаривают друг с другом? В «Кодексе Мистрии» об этом ничего нет...
bulgarian: Really? Flowers talk to each other? The Codex Mistria didn't cover this...

english: I don't think that's quite where Elsie was going with it, Celine.
french: Je ne crois pas que c'est ce qu'Elsie a voulu dire, Céline.
russian: Кажется, Элси имела в виду другое, Селин.
bulgarian: I don't think that's quite where Elsie was going with it, Celine.

english: It's more like a language of romance, isn't it?
french: C'est plutôt exprimer ses sentiments avec des fleurs, c'est ça ?
russian: Это же про язык романтики, да?
bulgarian: It's more like a language of romance, isn't it?

english: Did you know that there's a language of flowers, Celine?
french: Sais-tu qu'il existe un langage des fleurs, Céline ?
russian: Селин, ты знала, что существует язык цветов?
bulgarian: Did you know that there's a language of flowers, Celine?

english: Oh, well... I commend your taste, Celine.
french: Ah... tu as bon goût, Céline.
russian: А, да... У тебя хороший вкус, Селин.
bulgarian: Oh, well... I commend your taste, Celine.

english: Look at you! Pleased as punch! Or whatever's in that cauldron of yours.
french: Tu es ravie du compliment ! Arrête de faire ta timide.
russian: У тебя улыбка на лице написана! Что там у тебя в котелке?
bulgarian: Look at you! Pleased as punch! Or whatever's in that cauldron of yours.

english: I love how you've decorated the place, Juniper. It's so pretty!
french: J'adore la façon dont tu as décoré cet endroit, Juniper. C'est ravissant !
russian: Мне нравится, как ты обставила комнату, Джунипер. Очень красиво!
bulgarian: I love how you've decorated the place, Juniper. It's so pretty!

english: I want it to conjure that summery ocean feeling, but it doesn't quite get there, does it? How frustrating.
french: Je veux qu'elle fasse penser à l'été en bord de mer, mais je n'y suis pas tout à fait... C'est vraiment frustrant.
russian: Оно должно создавать летнее океанское настроение, но не совсем получается, да? Вот незадача.
bulgarian: I want it to conjure that summery ocean feeling, but it doesn't quite get there, does it? How frustrating.

english: Try adding something citrus! I think you'll be surprised at how breezy it smells.
french: Tu n'as qu'à essayer d'ajouter une pointe d'agrume ! Ça devrait te permettre d'obtenir la note que tu cherches.
russian: Попробуй добавить цитруса! Ты удивишься, но он сразу даст морские нотки.
bulgarian: Try adding something citrus! I think you'll be surprised at how breezy it smells.

english: Your new bath oil does smell nice, Juniper, but it's missing something.
french: Ta nouvelle huile de bain sent divinement bon, Juniper, mais il manque un petit quelque chose.
russian: Твоё масло для ванн приятно пахнет, Джунипер, но как будто чего-то не хватает.
bulgarian: Your new bath oil does smell nice, Juniper, but it's missing something.

english: Hmm, I'm not sure. Hops and barley are strong flavors to balance.
french: Mmm, je ne sais pas trop. Le houblon et l'orge ont des goûts puissants et difficiles à contrebalancer.
russian: Хмм, сложно сказать. Ячмень и хмель дают сильный вкус, его сложно сбалансировать.
bulgarian: Hmm, I'm not sure. Hops and barley are strong flavors to balance.

english: I'll sleep on it and get back to you!
french: Je vais y réfléchir ce soir. Je te dirai ça demain !
russian: Я подумаю денёк и вернусь к тебе завтра!
bulgarian: I'll sleep on it and get back to you!

english: I was thinking about the ale for next spring. Can you think of anything that might give it a light floral taste? I think Josie would like that.
french: Je réfléchissais au brassin pour le printemps prochain. Tu aurais une idée pour rendre la bière légèrement florale ? Je crois que ça plairait à Jo.
russian: Я размышляю над новым элем для грядущей весны. Не подскажешь, как бы ему придать легкий цветочный привкус? Думаю, Джози должно понравиться.
bulgarian: I was thinking about the ale for next spring. Can you think of anything that might give it a light floral taste? I think Josie would like that.

english: That always makes me nervous...
french: Ça m'inquiète toujours un peu...
russian: Меня такие фразы всегда тревожат...
bulgarian: That always makes me nervous...

english: Hah! Don't worry, Maple and Luc will keep her out of trouble.
french: Ah ! Ne t'en fais pas, Maple et Luc l'empêcheront de faire des bêtises.
russian: Ха! Не переживай, Мэйпл и Люк присмотрят за ней.
bulgarian: Hah! Don't worry, Maple and Luc will keep her out of trouble.

english: Well... Luc will keep Maple and Dell out of trouble. Right?
french: Enfin... Disons plutôt que Luc empêchera Dell et Maple de faire des bêtises.
russian: Точнее... Люк присмотрит за Мэйпл и Делл. Так ведь?
bulgarian: Well... Luc will keep Maple and Dell out of trouble. Right?

english: Dell said the Dragonguard was on important business today!
french: Dell a dit que la Garde des dragons avait une mission importante aujourd'hui !
russian: Делл сказала, что у Драконьей стражи сегодня важное дело.
bulgarian: Dell said the Dragonguard was on important business today!

english: She loved it. Thanks again for letting me raid your garden, I've always wanted to make her fresh tea!
french: Elle a adoré. Merci encore de m'avoir autorisé à cueillir des plantes dans ton jardin. J'ai toujours voulu lui préparer une tisane avec des herbes fraîches !
russian: Ещё как! Спасибо ещё раз, что дала покопаться в своём саду. Я всегда хотел приготовить для неё свежий чай.
bulgarian: She loved it. Thanks again for letting me raid your garden, I've always wanted to make her fresh tea!

english: How did the tea-making go? Did Josephine like your special blend?
french: Comment ça s'est passé avec la tisane ? Joséphine a aimé ton mélange spécial ?
russian: Как там рецепт чая? Джозефине понравилась твоя фирменная смесь?
bulgarian: How did the tea-making go? Did Josephine like your special blend?

english: It went over great! Thanks again for telling me where I could forage that stuff... doing it all myself made it more special.
french: Oui, beaucoup ! Merci de m'avoir indiqué où trouver les plantes que je cherchais... Ça a ajouté un petit quelque chose que je les cueille moi-même.
russian: Да, очень! Спасибо ещё раз, что показала, где собрать травы... Когда собираешь сам, подарок получается особенным.
bulgarian: It went over great! Thanks again for telling me where I could forage that stuff... doing it all myself made it more special.

english: How did Josephine like the new tea?
french: Joséphine a aimé la nouvelle tisane ?
russian: Джозефине понравился новый чай?
bulgarian: How did Josephine like the new tea?

english: I'm not planting carnations, dad...
french: Ce n'est pas du lilas que je plante, papa...
russian: Папа, у меня не растёт чертополох...
bulgarian: I'm not planting carnations, dad...

english: But... but how else is my pun going to work?
french: D'accord... mais mon jeu de mots tombe à l'eau sinon.
russian: Вижу... Но как иначе я сделаю каламбур?
bulgarian: But... but how else is my pun going to work?

english: Now what in carnation is going on here?
french: Ah lilas là là ! Qu'est-ce qui se passe ici ?
russian: Что за чертополох у тебя творится?
bulgarian: Now what in carnation is going on here?

english: Ohoho... hohoho!
french: Oh ho ho... ha ha ha !
russian: О-хо-хо... хо-хо-хо!
bulgarian: Ohoho... hohoho!

english: What? Huh? No, that wasn't a pun! I didn't...
french: Quoi ? Euh... Non, ce n'était pas un calembour ! Je...
russian: Что? А? Нет, это не каламбур! Я не нарочно...
bulgarian: What? Huh? No, that wasn't a pun! I didn't...

english: Don't look at me, [Ari]!
french: Ne me regarde pas comme ça, [Ari] !
russian: Не смотри на меня так, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Don't look at me, [Ari]!

english: Thank you so much for keeping my cottage in good repair, dad! You really nailed it.
french: Merci de t'être occupé de ma maison, papa ! J'avais peur que tu en aies marre tôt.
russian: Спасибо, что помог с ремонтом дома, папа! С тобой — как за стеной.
bulgarian: Thank you so much for keeping my cottage in good repair, dad! You really nailed it.

english: I wouldn't say it's too many for <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none>.
french: Je ne crois pas que ce soit trop pour <he>lui</he><she>elle</she><they>ellui</they>.
russian: По-моему, не так уж их и много.
bulgarian: I wouldn't say it's too many for <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none>.

english: I'd say... it's just enough!
french: Je dirais que c'est la dose recommandée !
russian: Я думаю... в самый раз!
bulgarian: I'd say... it's just enough!

english: I hope you're not making [Ari] endure too many of your puns, dad.
french: Papa, j'espère que tu n'embêtes pas trop [Ari] avec tes jeux de mots.
russian: Надеюсь, [Ari] не загибается от кучи твоих каламбуров, папа.
bulgarian: I hope you're not making [Ari] endure too many of your puns, dad.

english: You should have us over for dinner some time! We can even help you cook something up!
french: Tu devrais nous inviter à dîner un de ces quatre ! On pourra même mettre la main à la pâte, si tu veux !
russian: Надо нам как-нибудь отобедать у тебя! Можем даже помочь с готовкой!
bulgarian: You should have us over for dinner some time! We can even help you cook something up!

english: Oh, that would be so fun! We can use ingredients from my garden!
french: Oh, ce serait super, oui ! On utilisera les ingrédients de mon jardin !
russian: О, это отличная идея! Можем использовать травы прямо из моего сада.
bulgarian: Oh, that would be so fun! We can use ingredients from my garden!

english: I was worried when you first moved out, Celine, but your cottage is so cute. And very you, with the ivy growing all over. It's wonderful.
french: Je me faisais du souci quand tu es partie de chez nous, Céline, mais ta petite maison est adorable. Et elle te ressemble, avec tout ce lierre. C'est merveilleux.
russian: Когда ты только съехала, я за тебя переживала, Селин. Но у тебя такой милый домик! И очень в твоём духе, со всем этим плющом. Выглядит чудесно.
bulgarian: I was worried when you first moved out, Celine, but your cottage is so cute. And very you, with the ivy growing all over. It's wonderful.

english: I can tell your father is impressed because he didn't sneak a pun in there. That's basically the same as being speechless.
french: Je t'assure que ton père est impressionné. La preuve, il n'a pas fait de jeu de mots. Tu lui en as bouché un coin.
russian: Вижу, твой отец правда впечатлён, потому что он не вставил каламбур. Для него это, как без слов остаться.
bulgarian: I can tell your father is impressed because he didn't sneak a pun in there. That's basically the same as being speechless.

english: Haha! I'm so glad you both like it!
french: Ha ha ! Je suis vraiment contente que ça vous plaise à tous les deux !
russian: Ха-ха! Я рада, что вам у меня так нравится!
bulgarian: Haha! I'm so glad you both like it!

english: I'm proud of you, sweetheart! You've really made this cottage into a happy home. And look at all those nice plants!
french: Je suis fier de toi, ma chérie ! Tu as vraiment fait de cette maison un endroit où il fait bon vivre. Et regarde-moi toutes ces belles plantes !
russian: Я горжусь тобой, родная! У тебя в домике — просто образец уюта. И какие прекрасные цветы!
bulgarian: I'm proud of you, sweetheart! You've really made this cottage into a happy home. And look at all those nice plants!

english: But Celine really knows her stuff.
french: Mais Céline maîtrise son domaine.
russian: Но Селин, оказывается, и правда неглупа.
bulgarian: But Celine really knows her stuff.

english: Between us, [Ari], I had written most of this village off as country bumpkins...
french: Tu sais, [Ari], au début, je prenais tous les habitants d'ici pour des ploucs...
russian: Между нами говоря, [Ari], я уже думала, что в этой глухомани живёт только деревенщина.
bulgarian: Between us, [Ari], I had written most of this village off as country bumpkins...

english: Gosh, I wonder what I'm helping her make. I should probably ask!
french: Je me demande bien ce qu'elle va en faire... Je devrais lui poser la question !
russian: Ох, интересно, во что я ввязалась? Наверное, лучше спросить, что это за зелье!
bulgarian: Gosh, I wonder what I'm helping her make. I should probably ask!

english: Hi, [Ari]! I'm helping Juniper forage some rare flowers for one of her potions. They can be a bit tricky to identify if you're a novice to Mistria's flora.
french: Salut, [Ari] ! J'aide Juniper à trouver des fleurs pour une de ses potions. Elles peuvent être difficiles à reconnaître si tu ne connais pas bien la flore de Mistria.
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Я решила помочь Джунипер достать редкие цветы для её зелья. Их довольно трудно опознать, если не очень знаешь флору Мистрии.
bulgarian: Hi, [Ari]! I'm helping Juniper forage some rare flowers for one of her potions. They can be a bit tricky to identify if you're a novice to Mistria's flora.

english: These are good for tea, and these are good for extracts.
french: Celles-ci seront pour les infusions, et celles-ci pour les essences.
russian: Эти подойдут для чая, а эти — для экстрактов.
bulgarian: These are good for tea, and these are good for extracts.

english: Perfect. And do you want payment in tesserae, or bath coupons?
french: C'est parfait. Tu veux que je te règle en tesserae ou en entrées pour les bains ?
russian: Отлично! Тебе заплатить тессерами или купальными купонами?
bulgarian: Perfect. And do you want payment in tesserae, or bath coupons?

english: Tesserae, please!
french: En tesserae, ça ira !
russian: Лучше тессерами!
bulgarian: Tesserae, please!

english: I brought you those herbs you wanted, Juniper!
french: Voici les herbes qu'il te fallait, Juniper !
russian: Я принесла травы, которые ты просила, Джунипер.
bulgarian: I brought you those herbs you wanted, Juniper!

english: I'm fine, Mom. Really... I've got food at home.
french: Ça va, maman. Je t'assure... J'ai de quoi manger à la maison.
russian: Мам, я в порядке. Правда... Дома есть еда.
bulgarian: I'm fine, Mom. Really... I've got food at home.

english: A girl can't live on peanut butter sandwiches alone, you know...
french: Tu ne peux pas te nourrir uniquement de sandwichs au beurre de cacahouète, tu sais...
russian: Знаешь, нельзя же питаться одними сэндвичами с арахисовой пастой...
bulgarian: A girl can't live on peanut butter sandwiches alone, you know...

english: M-mom.
french: M-Maman.
russian: М-мам.
bulgarian: M-mom.

english: Not in front of [Ari]!
french: Ne dis pas ça devant [Ari] !
russian: Только не при [Ari]!
bulgarian: Not in front of [Ari]!

english: Are you sure you don't want me to drop off some dinner for the week?
french: Tu es sûre que tu ne veux pas que je passe t'apporter de quoi manger pour la semaine ?
russian: Точно не хочешь, чтобы я занесла тебе ужин на неделю?
bulgarian: Are you sure you don't want me to drop off some dinner for the week?

english: Mom! Not in front of [Ari]!
french: Maman ! Ne dis pas ça devant [Ari] !
russian: Мама, давай потише! Тут же [Ari]!
bulgarian: Mom! Not in front of [Ari]!

english: You know, Dell is half the handful you were at her age.
french: Tu sais, Dell est moins turbulente que toi à son âge.
russian: Знаешь, с Делл хлопот вдвое меньше, чем с тобой в её возрасте.
bulgarian: You know, Dell is half the handful you were at her age.

english: Ryis is watching the kids!
french: C'est Ryis qui s'occupe des enfants !
russian: С детьми уже гуляет Риз.
bulgarian: Ryis is watching the kids!

english: I just hope he doesn't let Dell near the tools.
french: J'espère juste qu'il ne laissera pas Dell jouer avec les outils.
russian: Надеюсь, он не пустит Делл к инструментам.
bulgarian: I just hope he doesn't let Dell near the tools.

english: Do you need me to watch Dell today? I don't mind.
french: Tu veux que je garde Dell aujourd'hui ? Ça ne me dérange pas.
russian: Хочешь, я сегодня присмотрю за Делл? Я не против.
bulgarian: Do you need me to watch Dell today? I don't mind.

english: What a twist of an ending!
french: Quel rebondissement !
russian: Какой неожиданный финал!
bulgarian: What a twist of an ending!

english: You know, the adorable little sister would have been my first guess.
french: Mais tu sais, j'aurais parié sur l'adorable petite sœur dès le début.
russian: Знаешь, а я бы в первую очередь подумала именно на очаровательную сестрёнку.
bulgarian: You know, the adorable little sister would have been my first guess.

english: And then in the last chapter, it turned out that the true culprit was the adorable little sister! She was a conniving mastermind the entire time!
french: Et dans le dernier chapitre, on a découvert que le coupable n'était autre que l'adorable petite sœur. C'est elle qui tirait les ficelles depuis le début !
russian: ...А в последней главе оказалось, что за преступлениями стояла его очаровательная младшая сестрёнка! Всё это время она устраивала коварные манипуляции!
bulgarian: And then in the last chapter, it turned out that the true culprit was the adorable little sister! She was a conniving mastermind the entire time!

english: Mistria is so big, you never know!
french: Qui sait ? Mistria est tellement vaste.
russian: Мистрия такая большая — никогда не знаешь наверняка!
bulgarian: Mistria is so big, you never know!

english: The Codex Mistria describes all kinds of fall flowers that aren't around anymore. I wonder if some of them still grow in some hidden place...
french: Le Codex Mistria décrit toutes sortes de fleurs d'automne qui ont disparu. Je me demande si certaines poussent encore dans des endroits cachés...
russian: В «Кодексе Мистрии» описано множество осенних цветов, которых тут давно нет. И всё же любопытно, вдруг какие-то из них растут в каком-нибудь укромном уголке.
bulgarian: The Codex Mistria describes all kinds of fall flowers that aren't around anymore. I wonder if some of them still grow in some hidden place...

english: Celine, did you add dandelions to one of my salads?
french: Céline, tu as mis du pissenlit dans une de mes salades ?
russian: Селин, ты что, добавила одуванчики в мой салат?
bulgarian: Celine, did you add dandelions to one of my salads?

english: You want to know my favorite dish from the summer seasonal menu? I liked that dandelion salad the most.
french: Tu veux connaître mon plat estival préféré ? Je dirais la salade de pissenlit.
russian: Знаешь, какое моё любимое блюдо в летнем меню? Мне больше всего понравился салат из одуванчиков.
bulgarian: You want to know my favorite dish from the summer seasonal menu? I liked that dandelion salad the most.

english: Roses, dandelions, violents, snapdragons, cosmos... they should all be edible.
french: Les roses, les pissenlits, les violettes, les gueules-de-loup, les cosmos... Elles devraient toutes être comestibles.
russian: Розы, одуванчики, фиалки, львиный зев, космея... Их все можно есть.
bulgarian: Roses, dandelions, violents, snapdragons, cosmos... they should all be edible.

english: They'd look so pretty on a cake, too!
french: Elles feraient jolies sur un gâteau !
russian: И они красиво смотрятся на торте!
bulgarian: They'd look so pretty on a cake, too!

english: Are there edible flowers, Celine? I thought they might look pretty as a garnish.
french: Il y a des fleurs qui sont comestibles, Céline ? Je me disais que ça pourrait faire un bel accompagnement.
russian: А бывают съедобные цветы, Селин? Я подумала: можно сделать красивое кулинарное украшение.
bulgarian: Are there edible flowers, Celine? I thought they might look pretty as a garnish.

english: Good job, Reina! That's a beautiful =Frost Lily=!
french: Super, Reina ! Quel magnifique =lys de givre= !
russian: Молодец, Рейна! Прекрасная =снежная лилия=!
bulgarian: Good job, Reina! That's a beautiful =Frost Lily=!

english: Celine, I found another one! Look!
french: Céline, j'en ai trouvé un autre ! Regarde !
russian: Селин, я ещё одну нашла!
bulgarian: Celine, I found another one! Look!

english: Any time, Celine!
french: Avec plaisir, Céline !
russian: Обращайся, Селин!
bulgarian: Any time, Celine!

english: I think we've found just about everything on my foraging list, Reina! Thank you so much for helping!
french: Je crois qu'on a trouvé tout ce qui était sur ma liste, Reina ! Merci beaucoup pour ton aide !
russian: По-моему, это был последний пункт в моём списке, Рейна! Спасибо тебе большое за помощь!
bulgarian: I think we've found just about everything on my foraging list, Reina! Thank you so much for helping!

english: It might have a more bitter taste than you're used to, but yes! You can forage that.
french: Elle aura un goût plus amer que ce à quoi tu es habituée, mais oui ! Tu peux en cueillir.
russian: Вкус будет непривычно горьковатый, но да, можно! Собирай, если хочешь.
bulgarian: It might have a more bitter taste than you're used to, but yes! You can forage that.

english: What about this one? Is it edible?
french: Et celle-là ? On peut la manger ?
russian: А как насчёт этого? Его можно есть?
bulgarian: What about this one? Is it edible?

english: Only if you want to make stomach ache cupcakes. I wouldn't bake it into anything!
french: Si tu veux faire des gâteaux qui retournent l'estomac, vas-y. Plus sérieusement, je te déconseille de l'utiliser en cuisine !
russian: Если хочешь, чтобы от твоего печенья болел живот, то да. Не советую их запекать ни в каком виде!
bulgarian: Only if you want to make stomach ache cupcakes. I wouldn't bake it into anything!

english: Oh, this plant is so pretty! Can I forage it, Celine?
french: Oh, cette plante est si jolie ! Je peux en récolter, Céline ?
russian: Ой, какой красивый! Можно, его заберу, Селин?
bulgarian: Oh, this plant is so pretty! Can I forage it, Celine?

english: Which one? There are so many! Wait, why does this one have holes in it?
french: Laquelle ? Il y en a tellement ! Et pourquoi il y a des trous dans celle-là ?
russian: А какой? Тут их так много! Ой, а почему этот весь дырявый?
bulgarian: Which one? There are so many! Wait, why does this one have holes in it?

english: Pass me the ladle, Celine!
french: Passe-moi la cuillère, Céline !
russian: Передай половник, Селин!
bulgarian: Pass me the ladle, Celine!

english: Of course! Let me know how much you want and I'll start planning!
french: Oui, bien sûr ! Dis-moi combien il t'en faut et je m'en occuperai !
russian: Обязательно! Скажи сразу, сколько тебе понадобится, чтобы я запланировала посадку!
bulgarian: Of course! Let me know how much you want and I'll start planning!

english: Do you think you'll grow lavender next season? Papa and I want to surprise Mama with a new tea, and I've got some ideas...
french: Est-ce que tu comptes faire pousser de la lavande la saison prochaine ? Papa et moi, on aimerait créer une nouvelle infusion pour maman et j'ai quelques idées...
russian: Ты не знаешь заранее, будет ли у тебя лаванда в следующем сезоне? Мы с папой хотим удивить маму новым чаем, и у меня появилась идейка...
bulgarian: Do you think you'll grow lavender next season? Papa and I want to surprise Mama with a new tea, and I've got some ideas...

english: Oh, I like to plan the next season's menu out like that, too. Maybe we can hang out and do it together, Celine!
french: Oh, moi aussi j'aime bien réfléchir au menu de la saison suivante. On pourrait peut-être se retrouver pour travailler ensemble, Céline !
russian: А, я так же планирую меню сезонное меню наперёд. Может, как-нибудь соберёмся делать записи вместе, Селин?
bulgarian: Oh, I like to plan the next season's menu out like that, too. Maybe we can hang out and do it together, Celine!

english: I'd love that!
french: Ce serait super !
russian: Было бы здорово!
bulgarian: I'd love that!

english: I've been planning out the manor garden! It helps me to write it all down ahead of time.
french: Je travaille à l'agencement des jardins du manoir ! Ça m'aide de tout poser sur le papier avant de commencer.
russian: Я занимаюсь планировкой сада особняка! Мне очень помогает записывать всё заранее.
bulgarian: I've been planning out the manor garden! It helps me to write it all down ahead of time.

english: Pretty good! I even figured out how to use up the last of the potatoes in the cellar.
