bulgarian: So? Did you enjoy the song, Seridia?

english: Maybe that's my problem with trying to catch the Big One... it's too suspecting!
french: C'est peut-être le problème que j'ai pour pêcher le Titan... Il est trop méfiant !
russian: Может, поэтому у меня и не получается поймать Здоровяка... Он слишком внимательный!
bulgarian: Maybe that's my problem with trying to catch the Big One... it's too suspecting!

english: Oh, but keep at it Terithia. You'll have such a tale to tell when you catch it!
french: Oh, mais ne baissez pas les bras Terithia. Cela vous fera une histoire fantastique à raconter lorsque vous l'aurez enfin !
russian: О, Теризия, не опускай руки. Когда поймаешь — будет такая история!
bulgarian: Oh, but keep at it Terithia. You'll have such a tale to tell when you catch it!

english: I have vivid memories of flying on high, before plunging down into the water to seize my prey.
french: Je me revois très nettement en train de voler dans les cieux avant de plonger dans l'eau pour me saisir de ma proie.
russian: Пролетать высоко над водой, а затем камнем падать вниз за добычей — это одно из самых ярких воспоминаний.
bulgarian: I have vivid memories of flying on high, before plunging down into the water to seize my prey.

english: It ultimately fled from my might, but I expect some day it will return to finish our dance of death.
french: Il préféra fuir, mais je crois qu'il reviendra un jour pour que nous terminions notre danse macabre.
russian: В конце концов он отступил перед моей силой. Но я думаю, однажды он вернётся, чтобы закончить наш танец смерти.
bulgarian: It ultimately fled from my might, but I expect some day it will return to finish our dance of death.

english: Huh... I also tangled with a beast of a crab in my younger days. It also scuttled off... wonder if it was the same fella!
french: Oh... Moi aussi je me suis retrouvée aux prises avec un crabe impressionnant dans ma jeunesse, et il s'était carapaté... C'était peut-être le même !
russian: Хм... В молодые годы я тоже один раз поцапалась с большущим крабом. И он тоже удрал... Интересно, вдруг это был один и тот же краб.
bulgarian: Huh... I also tangled with a beast of a crab in my younger days. It also scuttled off... wonder if it was the same fella!

english: Wouldn't that be something?
french: Ce serait une sacrée coïncidence, non ?
russian: Вот это была бы история!
bulgarian: Wouldn't that be something?

english: It's too bad, the only giant crab I've ever met is March!
french: Pour ma part, je me suis souvent retrouvée au beau milieu de paniers de crabes !
russian: Жаль, что я огромных крабов не встречала. Разве что Март угрюмый, как рак-отшельник!
bulgarian: It's too bad, the only giant crab I've ever met is March!

english: I battled a gigantic crab, once. On a beach much like this one.
french: Une fois, j'ai affronté un crabe gigantesque. C'était sur une plage semblable à celle-là.
russian: Однажды на пляже вроде этого я сражалась с гигантским крабом.
bulgarian: I battled a gigantic crab, once. On a beach much like this one.

english: It's nice, retiring from that part of our lives.
french: C'est plutôt agréable de laisser cette partie de sa vie derrière soi.
russian: Приятно, наконец, оставить эту жизнь позади.
bulgarian: It's nice, retiring from that part of our lives.

english: The problem with retirement is that there's always some problem that brings you out of it.
french: Le problème, c'est qu'il y a toujours quelque chose qui nous oblige à reprendre du service.
russian: Одна беда с уходом на покой: вечно находятся проблемы, из-за которых надо возвращаться в строй!
bulgarian: The problem with retirement is that there's always some problem that brings you out of it.

english: Ooh... I read a book like that, once!
french: Oooh... Cela me rappelle un livre que j'ai lu.
russian: О... Я однажды читала про это книгу!
bulgarian: Ooh... I read a book like that, once!

english: It had lots of explosions...
french: Il y avait beaucoup d'explosions...
russian: Там было много разных выражений...
bulgarian: It had lots of explosions...

english: You and I spent our youth on fightin', Seridia...
french: Vous et moi, on a passé toute notre jeunesse à lutter, Seridia...
russian: Мы с тобой провели молодые годы в сражениях, Серидия...
bulgarian: You and I spent our youth on fightin', Seridia...

english: You're speaking my language, Terithia.
french: Nous sommes bien d'accord, Terithia.
russian: Наконец ты меня понимаешь, Теризия!
bulgarian: You're speaking my language, Terithia.

english: I've always preferred a cold, salty brine, but these days warm water and bath salts does have its appeal.
french: J'ai toujours préféré les embruns froids et salés, mais maintenant, je ne crache pas sur de l'eau chaude et des sels de bain.
russian: Я всегда любила холодные морские воды, но с возрастом начинаю ценить тёплую воду и соли для ванн.
bulgarian: I've always preferred a cold, salty brine, but these days warm water and bath salts does have its appeal.

english: It's a big wide world, Elsie! There's even fish I've never seen before, I'm sure of it!
french: Le monde est immense, Elsie ! Il y a même sûrement des poissons que je n'ai encore jamais vus !
russian: Мир необъятен, Элси! Я уверена, бывают рыбы, о которых даже я не слышала.
bulgarian: It's a big wide world, Elsie! There's even fish I've never seen before, I'm sure of it!

english: We get plenty of imports in the Capital, but I had no idea there were so many kinds of fish.
french: Dans la capitale, on fait venir des produits de partout, mais je n'imaginais pas qu'il existait autant d'espèces de poisson.
russian: У нас в столице много импортных товаров, но я даже не подозревала, что рыбы бывают такие разные.
bulgarian: We get plenty of imports in the Capital, but I had no idea there were so many kinds of fish.

english: You're a woman of the sea, Terithia! What's more romantic than the salty stoicism of the fisherwoman?
french: Vous êtes une louve de mer, Terithia ! Quoi de plus romantique que la sérénité iodée d'une pêcheuse ?
russian: Ты же рыбачка, Теризия! Что может быть романтичнее непреклонной леди солёных морей?
bulgarian: You're a woman of the sea, Terithia! What's more romantic than the salty stoicism of the fisherwoman?

english: I'm not much of a romantic, Elsie! I don't have a way with words.
french: Je ne suis pas une grande romantique, Elsie ! Je ne sais pas trop y faire avec les mots.
russian: Романтика это не моё, Элси! Я не умею подбирать слова.
bulgarian: I'm not much of a romantic, Elsie! I don't have a way with words.

english: Sure have! I don't miss the long hauls, though. Happy to trade it in for this pretty piece of Mistria's coastline!
french: Pour sûr ! Mais les voyages au long cours ne me manquent pas. Je suis contente d'avoir arrêté pour m'installer ici, sur les rivages de Mistria !
russian: Ещё как! Но я не скучаю по дальним странствиям. Я и рада променять их на милый мистрийский берег.
bulgarian: Sure have! I don't miss the long hauls, though. Happy to trade it in for this pretty piece of Mistria's coastline!

english: You've done quite a bit of sailing in your day, haven't you Terithia?
french: Vous avez pas mal navigué dans votre vie, n'est-ce pas, Terithia ?
russian: Ты же много ходила по морям в своё время, Теризия?
bulgarian: You've done quite a bit of sailing in your day, haven't you Terithia?

english: Sure is. Just gotta keep your eyes peeled!
french: Oui. Il suffit de bien regarder !
russian: Всё верно. Надо только смотреть в оба!
bulgarian: Sure is. Just gotta keep your eyes peeled!

english: Terithia tells me all manner of lovely shells wash up on this beach. Isn't that right?
french: Terithia m'expliquait qu'il y a plein de jolis coquillages qui restent sur le sable après la marée. N'est-ce pas ?
russian: Теризия мне рассказала, что море выносит на пляж самые разные красивые раковины. Да ведь?
bulgarian: Terithia tells me all manner of lovely shells wash up on this beach. Isn't that right?

english: You know, they age this one by submerging it in the sea! They call it underwater wine.
french: Vous savez qu'ils le font vieillir en le plongeant dans la mer ! On appelle ça du vin sous-marin.
russian: Ты знала, что это вино они настаивают в бочках под водой? Его ещё называют подводным вином.
bulgarian: You know, they age this one by submerging it in the sea! They call it underwater wine.

english: No wonder I like it so much!
french: Normal qu'il me plaise autant !
russian: Тогда понятно, почему оно мне так нравится!
bulgarian: No wonder I like it so much!

english: I'm so glad you're enjoying the wine, Terithia! I tried to find a vintage you'd like.
french: Je suis contente que vous appréciiez le vin, Terithia ! J'ai essayé de trouver un cru qui vous plairait.
russian: Я так рада, что тебе понравилось вино, Теризия! Я старалась подобрать сорт тебе по вкусу.
bulgarian: I'm so glad you're enjoying the wine, Terithia! I tried to find a vintage you'd like.

english: Of course. Many medicines of the past are still in use today, and sometimes we can increase their efficacy with modern methods.
french: Oh oui. De nombreux médicaments d'antan sont toujours utilisés aujourd'hui, et on peut parfois améliorer leur efficacité avec les techniques d'aujourd'hui.
russian: Именно. Множество старых лекарств используется до сих пор. Иногда мы можем улучшить их действие с помощью современных методов.
bulgarian: Of course. Many medicines of the past are still in use today, and sometimes we can increase their efficacy with modern methods.

english: Please let me know if you come across anything promising.
french: Préviens-moi si jamais tu tombes sur quelque chose de prometteur.
russian: Сообщите мне, пожалуйста, если найдёте что-нибудь подходящее.
bulgarian: Please let me know if you come across anything promising.

english: You're looking for records of ancient medicines?
french: Tu cherches des documents sur les remèdes d'autrefois ?
russian: Ты ищешь заметки о древних лекарствах?
bulgarian: You're looking for records of ancient medicines?

english: The heroine's actions make no sense at all. Being passionate is one thing, but a love potion? Think of the side effects!
french: L'héroïne fait n'importe quoi. La passion, c'est une chose, mais un philtre d'amour ? Tu imagines les effets secondaires !
russian: Героиня действует совершенно необдуманно. Я понимаю страсть, но любовное зелье? Могут быть побочные эффекты!
bulgarian: The heroine's actions make no sense at all. Being passionate is one thing, but a love potion? Think of the side effects!

english: Well, sometimes you need a little drama to get the plot moving, darling.
french: Il faut parfois quelques rebondissements pour relancer l'intrigue, ma chère.
russian: Ну, милая моя, иногда для сюжета нужно добавить немного драмы!
bulgarian: Well, sometimes you need a little drama to get the plot moving, darling.

english: What did you think of the book I lent you?
french: Qu'as-tu pensé du livre que je t'ai prêté ?
russian: Как тебе книга, которую я одолжила?
bulgarian: What did you think of the book I lent you?

english: Of course! All I ask is that you share your thoughts with me when you're done reading!
french: Oh, je t'en prie ! Tout ce que je te demande en retour, c'est de me dire ce que tu en as pensé quand tu les termines !
russian: Это не проблема! Взамен я прошу лишь, чтобы ты поделилась впечатлениями, когда прочитаешь.
bulgarian: Of course! All I ask is that you share your thoughts with me when you're done reading!

english: You really do have an endless supply of books, Elsie. And an endless well of generosity for lending them out.
french: Tu as une bibliothèque incroyable, Elsie. Et surtout, tu n'hésites pas à les prêter.
russian: Элси, ваш запас книг просто бесконечен. Как и ваша щедрость их одалживать.
bulgarian: You really do have an endless supply of books, Elsie. And an endless well of generosity for lending them out.

english: Oh, thank you. Some have been passed down through the family, though I did have Louis bring them in for a better fit.
french: Oh, merci. Certaines sont dans ma famille depuis plusieurs générations, mais j'ai demandé à Louis de faire quelques retouches pour qu'elles m'aillent mieux.
russian: О, благодарю. Некоторые я получила по наследству, но всё же отнесла их Луи, чтобы он перешил по размеру.
bulgarian: Oh, thank you. Some have been passed down through the family, though I did have Louis bring them in for a better fit.

english: Valen, I adore your collection of jackets. They're quite dashing.
french: J'adore ta collection de vestes, Valen. Elles sont très élégantes.
russian: Вален, я просто без ума от твоей коллекции курток. Они у тебя такие стильные!
bulgarian: Valen, I adore your collection of jackets. They're quite dashing.

english: Wonderful! This calls for mimosas.
french: Fantastique ! Fêtons ça au champagne, alors.
russian: Чудно! Это можно отметить коктейлем.
bulgarian: Wonderful! This calls for mimosas.

english: Well, as long as you keep it in moderation.
french: Tant que c'est avec modération.
russian: Можно, только потребляйте умеренно.
bulgarian: Well, as long as you keep it in moderation.

english: You're fit as a fiddle. As for your question... I don't know that I have any health advice for you, Elsie. You eat properly and have an active lifestyle.
french: Tu es en pleine forme. Concernant ta question... je ne suis pas sûre d'avoir des conseils santé à te donner, Elsie. Tu manges sainement et tu fais de l'exercice.
russian: Вы в отличной форме. А насчёт вашего вопроса... Даже не знаю, что вам посоветовать, Элси. У вас и так хорошее питание и здоровый образ жизни.
bulgarian: You're fit as a fiddle. As for your question... I don't know that I have any health advice for you, Elsie. You eat properly and have an active lifestyle.

english: Made from our own Mistria's grain! Warms the belly, and fills you up to boot! Cheers!
french: Elle est brassée avec des céréales de Mistria ! Ça réchauffe et ça remplit l'estomac ! Santé !
russian: Из местного мистрийского зерна! Согревает и насыщает! За тебя!
bulgarian: Made from our own Mistria's grain! Warms the belly, and fills you up to boot! Cheers!

english: Hemlock called this his seasonal winter ale? It's delightful! Heavenly, even!
french: C'est donc ça qu'Hemlock appelle sa bière d'hiver... C'est délicieux ! Divin, même !
russian: Хемлок, говорит, это его фирменный зимний эль. Восхитительный вкус! Просто райский, я бы сказал!
bulgarian: Hemlock called this his seasonal winter ale? It's delightful! Heavenly, even!

english: I see she passed on her good taste.
french: Je vois qu'elle t'a aussi transmis ses goûts.
russian: Вижу, хороший вкус она передала по наследству.
bulgarian: I see she passed on her good taste.

english: Shucks, I'm glad to hear Grandma passed on more than her square jaw!
french: Eh bien, content d'apprendre que je n'ai pas seulement hérité de sa mâchoire carrée !
russian: Да ну! Приятно, что от бабушки мне досталась не только квадратная челюсть!
bulgarian: Shucks, I'm glad to hear Grandma passed on more than her square jaw!

english: Gya ha ha!
french: Gah ha ha !
russian: Га-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Gya ha ha!

english: Oh my, this is the exact type of beer Miss Greta used to drink!
french: Oh, c'est le type de bière que mademoiselle Greta aimait boire !
russian: Ну и ну, как раз такое пиво когда-то пила мисс Грета!
bulgarian: Oh my, this is the exact type of beer Miss Greta used to drink!

english: Not at all, my boy! I'm always thrilled to pay your splendid abode a visit.
french: Avec plaisir, mon garçon ! Je suis toujours ravi de voir cette magnifique exploitation.
russian: Вовсе нет, мальчик мой! Зайти к тебе для меня — всегда удовольствие.
bulgarian: Not at all, my boy! I'm always thrilled to pay your splendid abode a visit.

english: Thanks for coming out here! I know it's a bit out of the way.
french: Merci d'être venu, Errol ! Je sais que ce n'est pas tout près.
russian: Спасибо, что зашёл ко мне. Знаю, тебе не близко.
bulgarian: Thanks for coming out here! I know it's a bit out of the way.

english: She's the one who taught me how to run a farm! I got strong just trying to keep up with her.
french: C'est elle qui m'a appris le travail à la ferme ! Tous ces muscles, c'est à elle que je les dois. J'essayais de suivre son rythme.
russian: Это она учила меня фермерскому хозяйству! Пришлось набирать форму, чтобы за ней поспевать.
bulgarian: She's the one who taught me how to run a farm! I got strong just trying to keep up with her.

english: Gya ha ha!
french: Gah ha ha !
russian: Га-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Gya ha ha!

english: Your grandmother was quite a woman, Hayden. She could work a field and tend her animals, all before breakfast.
french: Ta grand-mère était une sacrée femme, Hayden. Elle travaillait les champs et s'occupait des animaux avant de prendre le petit-déjeuner.
russian: Что за женщина была твоя бабушка, Хейден! Она успевала и поработать в поле и обойти скот — всё до завтрака!
bulgarian: Your grandmother was quite a woman, Hayden. She could work a field and tend her animals, all before breakfast.

english: Well now, thank you Errol! That's mighty nice to hear.
french: Merci, c'est gentil, Errol ! Ça me fait bien plaisir ce que tu dis.
russian: Спасибо на добром слове, Эррол! Приятно слышать.
bulgarian: Well now, thank you Errol! That's mighty nice to hear.

english: Your grandmother would be proud of how well you've done with the farm, Hayden.
french: Ta grand-mère serait fière de voir ce que tu as fait de sa ferme, Hayden.
russian: Твоя бабушка бы гордилась твоими успехами на ферме, Хейден.
bulgarian: Your grandmother would be proud of how well you've done with the farm, Hayden.

english: Much obliged, sir! Now where was I? Oh, the time Landen and I were lost in the Mines...
french: Merci bien, mon ami ! Alors, où en étais-je ? Oh, à la fois où Landen s'est perdu dans la mine...
russian: Покорно благодарю, сударь! Итак, на чём я остановился? Ах, да, мы с Ланденом заблудились в шахтах...
bulgarian: Much obliged, sir! Now where was I? Oh, the time Landen and I were lost in the Mines...

english: Let me top you off, old-timer! A little bit of drink keeps a fella warm in this weather.
french: Laisse-moi te payer un autre verre, l'ancien ! Il faut bien ça pour se réchauffer par ce temps.
russian: Давай долью, старик! В такую погоду не помешает немного выпить для разогрева.
bulgarian: Let me top you off, old-timer! A little bit of drink keeps a fella warm in this weather.

english: Yes! You're a right thoughtful host!
french: Oui, tu as vraiment le cœur sur la main !
russian: Да! Мы тут твои гости!
bulgarian: Yes! You're a right thoughtful host!

english: Shucks! Food's always better when you got company!
french: C'est normal ! La nourriture a toujours meilleur goût quand on la partage !
russian: Ерунда! Обедать всегда веселее вместе!
bulgarian: Shucks! Food's always better when you got company!

english: Thank you for having us over for dinner, Hayden.
french: Merci de nous avoir invités à dîner, Hayden.
russian: Спасибо, что пригласил нас на обед, Хейден.
bulgarian: Thank you for having us over for dinner, Hayden.

english: It's nice to be company!
french: Je suis toujours content de venir ici !
russian: А нам приятно в твоей компании!
bulgarian: It's nice to be company!

english: I'm just here for the gossip!
french: Moi, je viens pour les ragots !
russian: Я пришла за сплетнями!
bulgarian: I'm just here for the gossip!

english: KYA HA HA!
french: HÉ HÉ HÉ !
russian: КЯ-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: KYA HA HA!

english: Thank you both for coming over! It's nice to have company.
french: Merci à vous d'être venus ! C'est agréable d'avoir de la compagnie.
russian: Спасибо, что пришли! Всегда радуюсь вашей компании.
bulgarian: Thank you both for coming over! It's nice to have company.

english: Well, I learned from the best. You've had a magnificent 'stache for as long as I can remember!
french: J'ai pris exemple sur le meilleur. Depuis que je te connais, ta moustache a toujours été impeccable !
russian: Ну, я же учился у лучших! У вас великолепные усы были всегда, сколько я себя помню.
bulgarian: Well, I learned from the best. You've had a magnificent 'stache for as long as I can remember!

english: These men and their mustaches...
french: Les hommes et leur moustache...
russian: Ох, мужики со своими усами...
bulgarian: These men and their mustaches...

english: I must say, Holt, you've done well for yourself. I was admiring your mustache from across the room.
french: Eh bien, Holt, c'est une vraie œuvre d'art ! Même de l'autre bout de la pièce, on ne voit que ta moustache.
russian: Должен сказать, Хольт, ты отлично выглядишь. Я засмотрелся на твои усы через всю комнату.
bulgarian: I must say, Holt, you've done well for yourself. I was admiring your mustache from across the room.

english: That's back before he was Baron! That man always had a helping hand for everyone.
french: C'était avant qu'il ne devienne baron ! Cet homme avait toujours à cœur d'aider tout le monde.
russian: Он тогда ещё не был бароном! Это человек великой души, он всегда протягивал руку помощи.
bulgarian: That's back before he was Baron! That man always had a helping hand for everyone.

english: How do you suppose the lord and lady are getting by in the Capital?
french: À ton avis, ça se passe comment pour eux dans la capitale ?
russian: Как, по-твоему, у них с баронессой дела в столице?
bulgarian: How do you suppose the lord and lady are getting by in the Capital?

english: The Baroness understands politics, and the Baron's stark honesty passes for it. Truth to tell, I feel sorry for those who come up against them!
french: La baronne maîtrise la politique, et le franc-parler du baron en impose. À vrai dire, je plains ceux qui se retrouveront face à eux !
russian: Баронесса знает толк в политике, а барон, наоборот, прямолинеен и строг. Честно говоря, не завидую я тем, кто решится встать у них на пути!
bulgarian: The Baroness understands politics, and the Baron's stark honesty passes for it. Truth to tell, I feel sorry for those who come up against them!

english: You remember when we did the rounds with Baron Wiskar? Those were the days!
french: Tu te souviens de l'époque où on faisait les tournées avec le baron Wiskar ? C'était le bon temps !
russian: Помнишь, как мы дружили с бароном Вискаром? Вот это были деньки!
bulgarian: You remember when we did the rounds with Baron Wiskar? Those were the days!

english: We were both lost, sir! Why, I recall that you got us even more lost! And furthermore-
french: Excuse-moi, mais tu ne savais pas non plus où on était ! Et si je me souviens bien, on s'est encore plus perdus à cause de toi ! D'ailleurs...
russian: Мы заблудились вместе, сэр! Вообще, насколько я помню, это было из-за тебя. Более того...
bulgarian: We were both lost, sir! Why, I recall that you got us even more lost! And furthermore-

english: [Ari], [Ari]! Did I ever tell you about the time Errol got us lost in the woods?
french: [Ari], [Ari] ! Est-ce que je t'ai raconté la fois où Errol nous a perdus dans les bois ?
russian: [Ari], [Ari]! Я тебе рассказывал, как мы из-за Эррола заблудились в лесу?
bulgarian: [Ari], [Ari]! Did I ever tell you about the time Errol got us lost in the woods?

english: That would be your stomach, Landen. Get yourself some breakfast!
french: C'est ton ventre qui gargouille, Landen. Tu ferais mieux de prendre ton petit-déjeuner !
russian: По-моему, это твой живот, Ланден. Не забудь позавтракать!
bulgarian: That would be your stomach, Landen. Get yourself some breakfast!

english: You hear that, old-timer? That's the seagull's cry. It's calling me to the ocean.
french: Tu entends ça, l'ancien ? C'est le cri de la mouette. La mer m'appelle.
russian: Слышал, старик? Это кричат чайки. Они зовут меня к океану.
bulgarian: You hear that, old-timer? That's the seagull's cry. It's calling me to the ocean.

english: Oh, that's kind of you! And thank you, [Ari]. Without your assistance, our collection wouldn't be so grand!
french: Merci, c'est très gentil ! Et merci, [Ari]. Sans ton aide, nos collections ne seraient pas aussi belles !
russian: Ох, спасибо! И спасибо тебе, [Ari]. Без тебя наша коллекция была бы существенно беднее.
bulgarian: Oh, that's kind of you! And thank you, [Ari]. Without your assistance, our collection wouldn't be so grand!

english: I swung by the Museum, Errol! You've really outdone yourself, old-timer!
french: Je suis passé au musée, Errol ! Tu t'es surpassé, hein, l'ancien !
russian: Я недавно заглянул в музей, Эррол. Ну ты и молодчина, старик!
bulgarian: I swung by the Museum, Errol! You've really outdone yourself, old-timer!

english: Didn't you hear? They picked up and moved to the CAPITAL! Heard their eldest just got married...
french: Tu n'es pas au courant ? Ils se sont installés à la CAPITALE ! Il paraît que l'aîné vient de se marier...
russian: А ты не слышал? Они собрали вещи и уехали в СТОЛИЦУ! Говорят, у них недавно старший сын женился...
bulgarian: Didn't you hear? They picked up and moved to the CAPITAL! Heard their eldest just got married...

english: Where do you suppose her family went off to after the earthquake?
french: À ton avis, où sa famille est partie après le tremblement de terre ?
russian: Куда, по-твоему, её семья отправилась после землетрясения?
bulgarian: Where do you suppose her family went off to after the earthquake?

english: No way!
french: Mais non ?
russian: Не может быть!
bulgarian: No way!

english: Oh yes, we were all scared out of our wits! The entire thing came down and missed us by a hair. But it was from that tree that Landen crafted the haft of the legendary axe...
french: Si si, et on a vraiment eu très peur ! En tombant, l'arbre est tombé et a failli nous écraser. Mais c'est dans cet arbre que Landen a sculpté le manche de la hache légendaire qu'on appelle...
russian: Ещё как может! Мы испугались до чёртиков. Мы были на волосок от рухнувшего ствола. Позже Ланден сделал легендарный топор, с рукоятью именно из этого дерева...
bulgarian: Oh yes, we were all scared out of our wits! The entire thing came down and missed us by a hair. But it was from that tree that Landen crafted the haft of the legendary axe...

english: THUNDERSTRUCK!
french: FULGURANCE !
russian: ГРОМОВЕРЖЕЦ!
bulgarian: THUNDERSTRUCK!

english: And then the wind starts picking up and we hear this #CRACK# like a thunderclap! But it wasn't thunder, it was the trunk of the tree we were standing beneath!
french: Et là, le vent s'est levé et on a entendu un énorme #CRAC#, on aurait dit un coup de tonnerre ! Ce n'était pas la foudre, mais le tronc de l'arbre sous lequel on se trouvait !
russian: И тут разбушевался ветер, и мы слышим #ХРЯСЬ#, как будто раскат грома! Но звук был не от грозы, а от дерева, под которым мы стояли!
bulgarian: And then the wind starts picking up and we hear this #CRACK# like a thunderclap! But it wasn't thunder, it was the trunk of the tree we were standing beneath!

english: We're not bringing that back! I'm so not arm-wrestling you two.
french: Oui, mais cette époque est révolue ! Hors de question que je vous affronte au bras de fer, tous les deux.
russian: Нет уж, давайте не возвращать эту традицию! Даже не собираюсь с вами бороться.
bulgarian: We're not bringing that back! I'm so not arm-wrestling you two.

english: Oh, don't worry... that all came to an end when Terithia moved to town.
french: Oh, ne t'en fais pas... Tout ça, c'est terminé depuis que Terithia est arrivée.
russian: Ой, не волнуйся... мы перестали так делать, когда у нас поселилась Теризия.
bulgarian: Oh, don't worry... that all came to an end when Terithia moved to town.

english: That lady's got an arm on her!
french: C'est qu'elle a une de ces forces !
russian: Вот у этой дамы чемпионские руки!
bulgarian: That lady's got an arm on her!

english: She's the arm-wrestling queen of Mistria!
french: C'est la reine du bras de fer à Mistria !
russian: Да, в Мистрии она — королева армрестлинга!
bulgarian: She's the arm-wrestling queen of Mistria!

english: You know, there was a time when we'd arm-wrestle over who would pay for breakfast!
french: À une époque, on faisait des bras de fer pour décider qui paierait le petit-déjeuner !
russian: Знаешь, в былые времена мы решали, кто платит за завтрак, поединком в армрестлинг!
bulgarian: You know, there was a time when we'd arm-wrestle over who would pay for breakfast!

english: Oh, you know... a little of this, a little of that!
french: Oh... Des bricoles par-ci par-là !
russian: Да, знаешь... то там, то сям!
bulgarian: Oh, you know... a little of this, a little of that!

english: That translates to a no, Errol.
french: Ça veut dire « rien », Errol.
russian: Это значит «нет», Эррол.
bulgarian: That translates to a no, Errol.

english: So, do you gents have your days planned out?
french: Alors, mes amis, vous avez prévu des choses dans les prochains jours ?
russian: У вас, джентльмены, уже распланирована неделя?
bulgarian: So, do you gents have your days planned out?

english: I'm not sure... Terithia brought it with her.
french: Je ne sais pas trop... C'est Terithia qui l'a apporté.
russian: Не могу сказать... Его Теризия привезла.
bulgarian: I'm not sure... Terithia brought it with her.

english: This one's from the bottom of the bay!
french: Cette bouteille était au beau milieu de la baie !
russian: Эта бутылка — со дна залива!
bulgarian: This one's from the bottom of the bay!

english: And this next one I found in a sand dune on the Beach.
french: Et l'autre, je l'ai trouvée dans une dune, sur la plage.
russian: А другую я нашла в дюне не песчаном пляже.
bulgarian: And this next one I found in a sand dune on the Beach.

english: So you quite literally dug them up... I see...
french: Mais alors... tu les as vraiment pêchées de nulle part...
russian: Выходит, буквально откопала... Понятно...
bulgarian: So you quite literally dug them up... I see...

english: This wine's not bad, you two! Where'd you dig it up?
french: Il n'est pas mauvais, ce vin ! Il vient d'où ?
russian: Неплохое вино вы достали! Где вы его откопали?
bulgarian: This wine's not bad, you two! Where'd you dig it up?

english: Like that bakery that always had something new from the Capital!
french: Oui. La boulangerie proposait toujours une nouveauté de la capitale !
russian: В пекарне, например, всегда было что-то новое из столицы.
bulgarian: Like that bakery that always had something new from the Capital!

english: We used to make the rounds with Valen's father, you remember that doc?
french: Valen, tu te souviens qu'on accompagnait ton père dans ses tournées.
russian: Мы там бродили с отцом Вален, помнишь, док?
bulgarian: We used to make the rounds with Valen's father, you remember that doc?

english: I do. You always snuck me sweets when my father wasn't looking.
french: Oui, très bien. Tu me donnais toujours des bonbons en cachette, quand mon père avait le dos tourné.
russian: Помню. Вы тайком покупали мне сладости, пока отец не смотрит.
bulgarian: I do. You always snuck me sweets when my father wasn't looking.

english: KYA HA HA!
french: HÉ HÉ HÉ !
russian: КЯ-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: KYA HA HA!

english: You boys are making me nostalgic!
french: Vous allez me faire regretter de ne pas avoir été là.
russian: Мальчики, у меня от вас ностальгия!
bulgarian: You boys are making me nostalgic!

english: Remember the Saturday Market? We used to spend our entire day there. All the hustle and bustle, and there was always something new to eat!
french: Vous vous souvenez du marché du samedi ? On y passait la journée entière autrefois. Toute cette vie, et il y avait toujours des choses nouvelles à goûter !
russian: А помните Субботний базар? Там можно было весь день провести. Кругом такая суета, и всегда какая-то новенькая еда.
bulgarian: Remember the Saturday Market? We used to spend our entire day there. All the hustle and bustle, and there was always something new to eat!

english: You know, I think you're onto something young master Luc.
french: Tu sais quoi, je crois que tu as raison, jeune Luc.
russian: Должен признать, это светлая идея, юный господин Люк!
bulgarian: You know, I think you're onto something young master Luc.

english: Wouldn't it be more sensible to categorize the Museum's fauna by genus, rather than alphabet?
french: Est-ce qu'il ne vaudrait pas mieux classer la faune du musée par espèce plutôt que par ordre alphabétique ?
russian: Разве не логичнее было бы организовать фауну Мистрии по родам, а не по алфавиту?
bulgarian: Wouldn't it be more sensible to categorize the Museum's fauna by genus, rather than alphabet?

english: Wonderful!
french: C'est fascinant !
russian: Чудесно!
bulgarian: Wonderful!

english: But, erm, young master Luc... aren't I supposed to be teaching you?
french: Mais, euh, jeune Luc... n'est-ce pas moi qui suis censé t'apprendre des choses ?
russian: Но, эхм... юный господин Люк, мне кажется, это я должен вас учить.
bulgarian: But, erm, young master Luc... aren't I supposed to be teaching you?

english: You can even identify ancient species of insects by observing the shape of the wings on the imprint they've left behind!
french: On peut même identifier d'anciennes espèces d'insectes en observant la forme des ailes sur les fossiles !
russian: Даже древние виды насекомых можно опознать по отпечаткам крыльев, оставшимся в окаменелостях!
bulgarian: You can even identify ancient species of insects by observing the shape of the wings on the imprint they've left behind!

english: This looks good, Errol! We're on it!
french: Ça marche, Errol ! On s'en occupe !
russian: Поздравляю, Эррол! Займёмся этим.
bulgarian: This looks good, Errol! We're on it!

english: We have some new items going up on display, and so I'm here with another work order of nameplates!
french: Nous allons exposer de nouvelles pièces au musée, alors je viens te commander des plaques signalétiques !
russian: У нас в музее новые поступления, так что я снова пришёл с заказом на таблички.
bulgarian: We have some new items going up on display, and so I'm here with another work order of nameplates!

english: Egads! That's some splendid pottery you've found! Well done!
french: Bon sang ! Cette poterie est tout bonnement splendide ! Félicitations !
russian: Ну и ну! Это же блестяший образец керамики. Молодчина!
bulgarian: Egads! That's some splendid pottery you've found! Well done!

english: Oh, nice!
french: Ah, merci !
russian: О, класс!
bulgarian: Oh, nice!

english: Got any cool rocks to trade for it, Errol?
french: Tu n'aurais pas quelques jolies pierres contre lesquelles me l'échanger, Errol ?
russian: Может, обменяешь мне на какой-нибудь крутой камень, Эррол?
bulgarian: Got any cool rocks to trade for it, Errol?

english: What's that you've got there, Olric?
french: Qu'est-ce que tu as trouvé là, Olric ?
russian: Что это у тебя там, Ольрик?
bulgarian: What's that you've got there, Olric?

english: It was out along the coast, towards the ruins... I could never mistake that shadow beneath the waves!
french: Je pêchais près de la côte, au niveau des ruines... Cette ombre gigantesque sous l'eau, je ne peux pas me tromper !
russian: Он плыл вдоль берега в сторону руин... Я эту тень под водой ни с чем не спутаю.
bulgarian: It was out along the coast, towards the ruins... I could never mistake that shadow beneath the waves!

english: Terithia tells me she saw the Big One this week...
french: Terithia me disait qu'elle avait vu le Titan cette semaine...
russian: Таризия говорит, что видела Здоровяка на этой неделе...
bulgarian: Terithia tells me she saw the Big One this week...

english: Rising before dawn is ingrained in me, from when I used to work in the Mines. Hard to break old habits, I suppose.
french: Je ne peux pas m'empêcher de me lever avant l'aube. Ça remonte à l'époque où je travaillais dans les mines. C'est difficile de se défaire de ses habitudes.
russian: У меня организм привык вставать до рассвета, ещё когда я работал в шахтах. Трудно побороть старые привычки.
bulgarian: Rising before dawn is ingrained in me, from when I used to work in the Mines. Hard to break old habits, I suppose.

english: At your age, you should really be getting a full night's rest.
french: À ton âge, tu devrais vraiment faire des nuits complètes.
russian: В вашем возрасте я бы рекомендовала полноценный ночной отдых.
bulgarian: At your age, you should really be getting a full night's rest.

english: Well, health is one part mental. You do seem happier since you became the Museum's Curator!
french: La santé, c'est aussi dans la tête. Et tu sembles plus épanoui depuis que tu es devenu conservateur du musée !
russian: Ну, здоровье бывает и психическое. Вы явно выглядите счастливее с тем пор, как стали куратором музея.
bulgarian: Well, health is one part mental. You do seem happier since you became the Museum's Curator!

english: It's funny, Valen, but I feel even healthier nowadays.
french: C'est marrant, Valen, mais j'ai l'impression d'être en meilleure forme ces derniers temps.
russian: Забавно, Вален, с возрастом я чувствую себя только здоровее.
bulgarian: It's funny, Valen, but I feel even healthier nowadays.

english: Much obliged, Hayden. There's a barrel with your name on it when I'm done!
french: Merci beaucoup, Hayden. Je te réserve un fût quand la bière sera prête !
russian: Спасибо, Хейден. Когда закончу, одна из бочек — твоя.
bulgarian: Much obliged, Hayden. There's a barrel with your name on it when I'm done!

english: Here you go, Hemlock! Plenty of grain and hops for your next round of brewing.
french: Et voilà, Hemlock ! Le plein de céréales et de houblon pour ton prochain brassin.
russian: Держи, Хемлок! Этого зерна и хмеля должно хватить на твою следующую варку.
bulgarian: Here you go, Hemlock! Plenty of grain and hops for your next round of brewing.

english: Friend, singular. That would be you, Hayden. Please ask that one to pass the pepper.
french: Amis, c'est vite dit, Hayden. Tu peux demander à l'autre de me passer le poivre ?
russian: С другом, Хейден, в единственном числе. Я имею в виду тебя. Можешь попросить её передать перец?
bulgarian: Friend, singular. That would be you, Hayden. Please ask that one to pass the pepper.

english: This one heard you just fine. Here, the pepper. Now, are you going to share that wine or drink it all on your own?
french: « L'autre » a des oreilles et un prénom. Tiens, ton poivre. Dis, tu comptes te siffler le vin toute seule ou tu veux bien partager ?
russian: «Она» тебя и так услышала. Держи. Ты собираешься делиться вином, или выпьешь всё сама?
bulgarian: This one heard you just fine. Here, the pepper. Now, are you going to share that wine or drink it all on your own?

english: They're getting on well, aren't they [Ari]?
french: Elles s'entendent à merveille, hein, [Ari] ?
russian: Вроде они поладили, да, [Ari]?
bulgarian: They're getting on well, aren't they [Ari]?

english: (Henrietta clucks to herself. She seems... unconvinced.)
french: (Henrietta caquette dans ses barbillons. Elle n'a pas l'air... convaincue.)
russian: (Генриетта тихонько кудахчет. Звучит... недоверчиво.)
bulgarian: (Henrietta clucks to herself. She seems... unconvinced.)

english: What's better than a day at the Beach? Dinner with friends, that's what!
french: Quoi de mieux qu'une journée à la plage ? Un dîner entre amis !
russian: Что может быть лучше, чем день не пляже? Обед с друзьями, вот что!
bulgarian: What's better than a day at the Beach? Dinner with friends, that's what!

english: That's because they have im-peck-able taste.
french: Je les trouve sacrément ir-riz-tables.
russian: Они у тебя кур-маны!
bulgarian: That's because they have im-peck-able taste.

english: Have you gotten the new shipment of rice in, Holt? My chickens will never forgive me if I don't make them their special treat.
french: Tu as reçu du riz, Holt ? Mes poules vont m'en vouloir si je ne leur prépare pas leur encas préféré.
russian: Ты привёз мой заказ риса, Хольт? Куры мне не простят, если я не дам им лакомство.
bulgarian: Have you gotten the new shipment of rice in, Holt? My chickens will never forgive me if I don't make them their special treat.

english: Sounds like you miscowculated!
french: Tu étais « vachement » optimiste !
russian: Нео-бык-новенно сложный расчёт?
bulgarian: Sounds like you miscowculated!

english: I need to stop in at the Mill at some point. I thought I had enough feed for the weekend, but I'm going to be just short.
french: Je vais devoir faire un saut au moulin. Je pensais avoir de quoi nourrir les animaux pour tout le week-end, mais ça va être juste.
russian: Надо мне будет зайти на мельницу. Думал, корма хватит на выходные, но понял, что просчитался.
bulgarian: I need to stop in at the Mill at some point. I thought I had enough feed for the weekend, but I'm going to be just short.

english: To be clear, I'm only toasting you, Hayden.
french: Que ce soit clair, je ne lève mon verre qu'en ton honneur, Hayden.
russian: Поясню: я пью только за нашу с тобой дружбу, Хейден.
bulgarian: To be clear, I'm only toasting you, Hayden.

english: Funny, I was thinking the same thing.
french: C'est marrant, je me disais justement la même chose.
russian: Забавно, я хотела сказать то же самое.
bulgarian: Funny, I was thinking the same thing.

english: Let's have a toast! To friendship!
french: Levons notre verre à l'amitié !
russian: Поднимем тост! За нашу дружбу!
bulgarian: Let's have a toast! To friendship!

english: Thanks, Uncle. I couldn't get it done without Hayden or Adeline.
french: Merci, tonton. Mais je n'y arriverais pas sans Hayden et Adeline.
russian: Спасибо, дядя. Я бы не справился без Хейдена и Аделины.
bulgarian: Thanks, Uncle. I couldn't get it done without Hayden or Adeline.

english: Or [Ari], for that matter!
french: Ni [Ari], d'ailleurs !
russian: И [Ari] тоже очень помогает!
bulgarian: Or [Ari], for that matter!

english: You two are doing a bang-up job restoring the town!
french: Les travaux de réhabilitation de la ville sont parfaits !
russian: Вы вдвоём отлично справляетесь с восстановлением города!
bulgarian: You two are doing a bang-up job restoring the town!

english: You'd make for a great carpenter, Hayden.
french: Tu ferais un très bon menuisier, Hayden.
russian: Из тебя вышел бы хороший плотник, Хейден.
bulgarian: You'd make for a great carpenter, Hayden.

english: That means a lot coming from you two. But I bet if I mentioned a career change to Henrietta, she'd peck the hammer right out of my hand!
french: Venant de vous, ça me touche beaucoup. Mais si je disais à Henrietta que je veux changer de métier, je me prendrais un bon coup de bec sur la main pour me faire lâcher le marteau !
russian: От вас это очень ценные слова. Но если я заикнусь про смену работы при Генриетте, она тут же выклюет у меня молоток из рук!
bulgarian: That means a lot coming from you two. But I bet if I mentioned a career change to Henrietta, she'd peck the hammer right out of my hand!

english: GYA HA HA!
french: GAH HA HA !
russian: ГА-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: GYA HA HA!

english: You're a huge help, Hayden. Thanks for all the help doing repairs around town.
french: Qu'est-ce qu'on ferait sans toi, Hayden ? Merci pour toutes les réparations que tu fais en ville.
russian: Ты нас очень выручил, Хейден. Спасибо, что помог нам подлатать здания в городе.
bulgarian: You're a huge help, Hayden. Thanks for all the help doing repairs around town.

english: GYA HA HA!
french: GAH HA HA !
russian: ГА-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: GYA HA HA!

english: I consider myself more of a friend of cows and chickens, personally.
french: Personnellement, je me considère plus comme leur ami.
russian: Мне лично больше нравится считать себя другом коров и кур.
bulgarian: I consider myself more of a friend of cows and chickens, personally.

english: Yeah... Henrietta's definitely the real royalty around here.
french: C'est vrai... C'est Henrietta, la véritable reine ici.
russian: Да уж... Кто здесь настоящая королева — так это Генриетта.
bulgarian: Yeah... Henrietta's definitely the real royalty around here.

english: You're like the king of cows and chickens, Mister Hayden!
french: Vous êtes un peu le roi des poules et des vaches, monsieur Hayden !
russian: Вы, как король коров и кур, мистер Хейден!
bulgarian: You're like the king of cows and chickens, Mister Hayden!

english: It's good. Adeline keeps the jobs coming.
french: Ça va. Adeline nous donne beaucoup de travail.
russian: Хорошо. От Аделины всегда есть заказы.
bulgarian: It's good. Adeline keeps the jobs coming.

english: How's the forge treating you these days?
french: Comment ça se passe à la forge en ce moment ?
russian: Как у тебя дела в кузнице?
bulgarian: How's the forge treating you these days?

english: Nothing wrong with eggs for dinner, March.
french: Il n'y a rien de mal à manger des œufs le soir, March.
russian: Что плохого в яйцах на обед, Март?
bulgarian: Nothing wrong with eggs for dinner, March.

english: Nothing wrong with a dozen eggs for dinner, bro.
french: Oui, tout le monde a le droit de manger une douzaine d'œufs le soir.
russian: Да, бро, что плохого в десятке яиц на обед?
bulgarian: Nothing wrong with a dozen eggs for dinner, bro.

english: I just want to say, I think you might both be obsessed with getting enough protein.
french: Sans vouloir être désagréable, vous me paraissez un peu obsédés par vos apports en protéines, les gars.
russian: Просто хочу заметить, по-моему, вы оба помешаны на белках.
bulgarian: I just want to say, I think you might both be obsessed with getting enough protein.

english: That's when it helps to remind yourself to take it one day at a time. No way to build a bridge except stone by stone.
french: Mais c'est dans ces moments-là qu'il faut prendre les choses les unes après les autres. Tout se construit petit à petit.
russian: В такие времена помогает сконцентрироваться на сегодняшнем дне. Даже большой мост строится по одному камню.
bulgarian: That's when it helps to remind yourself to take it one day at a time. No way to build a bridge except stone by stone.

english: That's good advice, Hayden. Thanks.
french: Merci du conseil, Hayden.
russian: Хороший совет, Хейден. Спасибо.
bulgarian: That's good advice, Hayden. Thanks.

english: You listening, March? You're the impatient one.
french: Tu as entendu, March ? Toi qui es si impatient tout le temps.
russian: Ты слушаешь, Март? Это же тебе не терпится.
bulgarian: You listening, March? You're the impatient one.

english: Yeah, yeah... thanks, Hayden. That helps.
french: Oui, oui... Merci, Hayden. Je tâcherai de m'en souvenir.
russian: Да, да... Спасибо, Хейден. Хороший совет.
bulgarian: Yeah, yeah... thanks, Hayden. That helps.

english: Sometimes the work is going to feel overwhelming! No avoiding it.
french: Parfois, on a l'impression d'être écrasé de travail ! C'est inévitable.
russian: Иногда работа кажется неподъёмной. Ничего не поделаешь!
bulgarian: Sometimes the work is going to feel overwhelming! No avoiding it.

english: Aw, they can join us! We can all sweat together!
french: Elles peuvent même s'entraîner avec nous ! Histoire qu'on sue tous ensemble !
russian: О, они могут тренироваться с нами! Будем вместе выжимать пот!
bulgarian: Aw, they can join us! We can all sweat together!

english: Come by and work out sometime. We've got the whole yard, and the animals don't mind.
french: Viens me voir pour qu'on s'entraîne ensemble. On a la cour pour nous et les bêtes s'en moquent.
russian: Можешь зайти ко мне потренироваться. У нас целый двор в распоряжении, животные не против.
bulgarian: Come by and work out sometime. We've got the whole yard, and the animals don't mind.

english: I thought you wanted to come to the Museum!
french: Je croyais que c'était toi qui voulais aller au musée !
russian: Я думал, это ты хотел в музей.
bulgarian: I thought you wanted to come to the Museum!

english: GYA HA HA!
french: GAH HA HA !
russian: ГА-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: GYA HA HA!

english: Well, we're here! We might as well have ourselves a look around!
french: Maintenant qu'on y est, autant en profiter pour visiter !
russian: Что ж, мы уже пришли. Раз так, можем поглазеть, что тут есть!
bulgarian: Well, we're here! We might as well have ourselves a look around!

english: Why'd you want to come to the Museum, Olric?
french: Pourquoi tu voulais aller au musée, Olric ?
russian: Почему ты решил пойти в музей, Ольрик?
bulgarian: Why'd you want to come to the Museum, Olric?

english: Buddy, we didn't even get to the tough part yet! Keep it going!
french: Attends, on n'en est même pas à la partie où on force ! Continue !
russian: До трудной части мы ещё не добрались! Давай-давай!
bulgarian: Buddy, we didn't even get to the tough part yet! Keep it going!

english: This new routine of yours is pretty tough, Olric! But I think I'm getting the hang of it.
french: Ton nouveau programme d'entraînement est balèze, Olric, mais je commence à m'y faire.
russian: Твой новый режим занятий стал трудноват, Ольрик! Но ничего, я пока справляюсь.
bulgarian: This new routine of yours is pretty tough, Olric! But I think I'm getting the hang of it.

english: Thanks, I was thinking about it all day yesterday!
french: Merci. J'ai passé la journée d'hier à y réfléchir !
russian: Спасибо, вчера весь день придумывал!
bulgarian: Thanks, I was thinking about it all day yesterday!

english: Okay, time to start a new set! Ready?
french: Allez, on se refait une série ! Prêt ?
russian: Так, перерыв окончен. Готов?
bulgarian: Okay, time to start a new set! Ready?

english: This new workout routine is something else, Olric! I really feel the burn!
french: Cette nouvelle préparation physique est efficace, Olric ! Je sens que ça brûle !
russian: Твой новый режим занятий — просто безумие, Ольрик! У меня мышцы все горят!
bulgarian: This new workout routine is something else, Olric! I really feel the burn!

english: You're welcome kindly, friend! Say hi to your folks for me!
french: Je t'en prie, Reina ! Passe le bonjour à tes parents de ma part !
russian: Всегда пожалуйста, подруга! Передавай от меня привет!
bulgarian: You're welcome kindly, friend! Say hi to your folks for me!

english: Thank you kindly, Hayden! This should be more than enough eggs and milk to get the Inn through the week.
french: Merci beaucoup, Hayden ! J'ai sûrement assez d'œufs et de lait pour tenir la semaine à l'auberge.
russian: Спасибо большое, Хейден! Этих яиц и молока трактиру должно хватить до конца недели.
bulgarian: Thank you kindly, Hayden! This should be more than enough eggs and milk to get the Inn through the week.

english: Did you know? Reina took over the supply run for Hemlock after he hurt his back.
french: Oui, Reina fait la tournée des fournisseurs à la place d'Hemlock depuis qu'il s'est fait mal au dos.
russian: Знаешь, что случилось? Рейна стала ходить вместо Хемлока, потому что у него заболела спина.
bulgarian: Did you know? Reina took over the supply run for Hemlock after he hurt his back.

english: His back got better, but every time Reina brings it up he pretends like he threw it out again.
french: Son dos va mieux, mais chaque fois que Reina aborde le sujet, il prétend que ça recommence.
russian: Он поправился, но каждый раз, когда Рейна про это вспоминает, он притворяется, что снова её потянул.
bulgarian: His back got better, but every time Reina brings it up he pretends like he threw it out again.

english: I don't mind one bit! Mostly I like my dad's terrible acting.
french: Ça ne me dérange pas ! Mon père joue tellement mal la comédie que ça me fait rire.
russian: Я и не против! Мне просто нравится, как папа нелепо притворяется.
bulgarian: I don't mind one bit! Mostly I like my dad's terrible acting.

english: Oh, hi [Ari]! I'm doing a supply run for the Inn. We're Hayden's biggest customers!
french: Salut, [Ari] ! Je viens m'approvisionner pour l'auberge. On est les plus gros clients d'Hayden !
russian: А, привет, [Ari]! Я иду за продуктами для трактира. Мы у Хейдена — главные покупатели!
bulgarian: Oh, hi [Ari]! I'm doing a supply run for the Inn. We're Hayden's biggest customers!

english: We got milk, we got eggs, we got cheese! But give it a once over and make sure it's all there.
french: Il y a du lait, des œufs et du fromage ! Mais vérifie quand même que tout y est.
russian: Вот молоко, вот яйца, вот сыр. Но ты на всякий случай всё равно проверь сама.
bulgarian: We got milk, we got eggs, we got cheese! But give it a once over and make sure it's all there.

english: Aw, thanks Hayden! I can't wait!
french: Oh, merci, Hayden ! Je vais faire ça !
russian: О, спасибо, Хейден! Сейчас-сейчас!
bulgarian: Aw, thanks Hayden! I can't wait!

english: Reina! I've got those supplies for the Inn all ready to go.
french: Reina ! J'ai préparé la commande pour l'auberge.
russian: Рейна! Я собрал тебе продукты для трактира.
bulgarian: Reina! I've got those supplies for the Inn all ready to go.

english: I should be okay, but thanks Hayden!
french: Je devrais me débrouiller, mais merci Hayden !
russian: Я справлюсь, но спасибо, Хейден!
bulgarian: I should be okay, but thanks Hayden!

english: I've got that order of eggs set aside for you. Let me know if you need help taking it back to the Inn.
french: J'ai mis ta commande d'œufs de côté. Dis-moi si tu as besoin d'un coup de main pour les apporter à l'auberge.
russian: Я отложил яйца, которые ты заказывала. Скажи, если надо помочь донести до трактира.
bulgarian: I've got that order of eggs set aside for you. Let me know if you need help taking it back to the Inn.

english: Ooh, thanks Hayden! Maybe I'll bake a quiche!
french: Oooh, merci Hayden ! Je vais peut-être faire une quiche !
russian: Ой, спасибо, Хейден! Тогда, может, сделаю киш!
bulgarian: Ooh, thanks Hayden! Maybe I'll bake a quiche!

english: Here for the supply pickup? I threw in some extra eggs this time!
french: Tu viens chercher les provisions ? J'y ai ajouté quelques œufs, cette fois !
russian: Ты за продуктами? У меня завалялась ещё парочка яиц, возьми.
bulgarian: Here for the supply pickup? I threw in some extra eggs this time!

english: I'd say I feel pretty good about it!
french: Je suis carrément partant.
russian: Думаю, это очень хорошая идея!
bulgarian: I'd say I feel pretty good about it!

english: Whew, I worked up a serious appetite! How do you feel about double lunch, Ryis?
french: Eh bien, tout cet exercice m'a ouvert l'appétit ! Ça te dirait un double déjeuner, Ryis ?
russian: Фух, я уже нагулял аппетит! Что думаешь насчёт двойного обеда, Риз?
bulgarian: Whew, I worked up a serious appetite! How do you feel about double lunch, Ryis?

english: Oho, not a problem! And remember, if you work extra, you gotta eat extra!
french: Ho ho, pas de problème ! Et souviens-toi que si on s'active beaucoup, on doit manger plus !
russian: О-хо, не проблема! Не забывай: если больше работаешь, надо и больше есть!
bulgarian: Oho, not a problem! And remember, if you work extra, you gotta eat extra!

english: Gya ha ha!
french: Gah ha ha !
russian: Га-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Gya ha ha!

english: Glad you had us break for lunch, Hayden. I was hungrier than I thought.
french: Tu as eu raison pour cette pause déjeuner, Hayden. J'avais plus faim que je ne pensais.
russian: Спасибо, что оторвал нас от работы и позвал обедать, Хейден. Оказалось, я ещё голоднее, чем думал.
bulgarian: Glad you had us break for lunch, Hayden. I was hungrier than I thought.

english: Sounds right to me. You're getting good at making these estimates, Hayden!
french: Oui, c'est ça. Tu commences à te débrouiller, Hayden !
russian: Да, я тоже так думаю. Ты уже хорошо оцениваешь время, Хейден!
bulgarian: Sounds right to me. You're getting good at making these estimates, Hayden!

english: I took a look at that work order from Adeline. I think a day to get it done, maybe two at most?
french: J'ai jeté un coup d'œil au bon de commande d'Adeline. Je pense que ça prendra une journée, deux maximum, non ?
russian: Я глянул на тот заказ Аделины. Думаю, займёт день, максимум два.
bulgarian: I took a look at that work order from Adeline. I think a day to get it done, maybe two at most?

english: Worlds better than before. Thanks for the assist, Hayden.
french: C'est beaucoup mieux qu'avant. Merci pour ton aide, Hayden.
russian: В разы лучше, чем было. Спасибо за помощь, Хейден.
bulgarian: Worlds better than before. Thanks for the assist, Hayden.

english: And... there we go! How's that looking?
french: Et... voilà le travail ! Tu en penses quoi ?
russian: И... вот так! Ну как тебе?
bulgarian: And... there we go! How's that looking?

english: But you get up because you have to, and the floorboards are cold, and that gets you moving.
french: Mais vous vous levez quand même parce qu'il y a du boulot, et comme le plancher est glacial, ça force à s'activer.
russian: Но всё равно надо, поэтому ты встаёшь. Наступаешь на холодный пол, и это сразу так бодрит.
bulgarian: But you get up because you have to, and the floorboards are cold, and that gets you moving.

english: I love that feeling, if I'm being honest. This is my favorite time of year.
french: Pour être honnête, j'adore cette sensation. C'est ma période préférée de l'année.
russian: Я просто обожаю это чувство. Сейчас моё любимое время года.
bulgarian: I love that feeling, if I'm being honest. This is my favorite time of year.

english: You know that feeling when you're all cozy in bed, and it's a little chilly, so you don't want to get up?
french: Vous savez quand on est bien au lit, qu'il fait un peu froid et qu'on n'a pas envie de se lever...
russian: Знаете это чувство, когда укутался в постели, а вокруг прохладно, и вставать не хочется?
bulgarian: You know that feeling when you're all cozy in bed, and it's a little chilly, so you don't want to get up?

english: I thought I had a bit of action, but it was just the current playing tricks.
french: J'ai cru que je tenais un poisson, mais c'était le courant qui me jouait des tours.
russian: Пару раз показалось, что что-то ловится, но оказалось, просто течение.
bulgarian: I thought I had a bit of action, but it was just the current playing tricks.

english: Some days are more of a waiting game!
french: Certains jours, ça ne veut pas !
russian: Бывают дни, когда надо просто ждать!
bulgarian: Some days are more of a waiting game!

english: Any bites?
french: Ça mord ?
russian: Как клюёт?
bulgarian: Any bites?

english: Boat races! That must have been a sight! And I imagine you had to know the currents pretty well to get to the head of the pack.
french: Des courses de bateau ! Ça devait être quelque chose ! J'imagine que tu devais bien connaître les courants pour prendre l'avantage.
russian: Гонки на лодках! Выглядит, наверное, захватывающе! Думаю, надо было хорошо знать течение, чтобы выбиться вперёд.
bulgarian: Boat races! That must have been a sight! And I imagine you had to know the currents pretty well to get to the head of the pack.

english: Oho, you're right! And I won my share of races. The sea's a friend to me!
french: Ho ho, et comment ! C'est que j'en ai gagné des courses. La mer est mon amie !
russian: Хо-хо, ты прав! И я много раз побеждала. Моря — моя стихия!
bulgarian: Oho, you're right! And I won my share of races. The sea's a friend to me!

english: You know, when we were between soldiering, some of the lads and I would race boats!
french: Entre deux missions, je faisais des courses de bateau avec d'autres soldats !
russian: Знаешь, когда у нас не было службы, мы с ребятами иногда устраивали гонки на лодках!
bulgarian: You know, when we were between soldiering, some of the lads and I would race boats!

english: I respect that. Now, give me the latest about Henrietta! Is she still quarreling with that cow of yours?
french: Aucun souci. Et maintenant, parle-moi d'Henrietta ! Est-ce qu'elle continue de se prendre le bec avec ta vache ?
russian: Ничего, отказ я тоже уважаю. Тогда поделись новостями про Генриетту! Она до сих пор в ссоре с той твоей коровой?
bulgarian: I respect that. Now, give me the latest about Henrietta! Is she still quarreling with that cow of yours?

english: I'm not sure fishing is for me, but it's neighborly of you to ask!
french: Je ne suis pas sûr d'être fait pour la pêche, mais c'est gentil de me proposer !
russian: Не уверен, что рыбалка — это моё, но спасибо за соседское предложение!
bulgarian: I'm not sure fishing is for me, but it's neighborly of you to ask!

english: Oh, but what if they do? I want to see just how big they'll get!
french: Mais si c'est le cas ? J'ai envie de voir quelle taille elles vont atteindre !
russian: Ох, а вдруг вырастут? Хочу посмотреть, какие будут самые большие!
bulgarian: Oh, but what if they do? I want to see just how big they'll get!

english: You're welcome to any of the pumpkins I've got growing! I don't think they'll get much bigger.
french: Tu peux prendre toutes les citrouilles que tu veux ! Je crois qu'elles ne grossiront pas plus.
russian: Можешь угощаться тыквами с моего огорода! Думаю, ещё больше они уже не вырастут.
bulgarian: You're welcome to any of the pumpkins I've got growing! I don't think they'll get much bigger.

english: You're healthy as a bull, Hayden.
french: Non, tu es en pleine forme, Hayden.
russian: Ты здоров как бык, Хейден.
bulgarian: You're healthy as a bull, Hayden.

english: I know the signs when I see them... give it to me straight, Valen. The whole diagnosis.
french: Je sens qu'il y a quelque chose qui cloche... Vas-y, Valen, tu peux tout me dire. Je suis condamné ?
russian: Я знаю свои симптомы... Можешь говорить честно, Вален. Что со мной?
bulgarian: I know the signs when I see them... give it to me straight, Valen. The whole diagnosis.

english: I stopped by to say hi to my old pal Valen! My thumb is fine!
french: Je viens dire bonjour à une bonne copine ! Mes doigts vont bien !
russian: Палец в порядке! Я зашёл поздороваться со старой подругой Вален!
bulgarian: I stopped by to say hi to my old pal Valen! My thumb is fine!

english: Stopping by the Clinic? Did you hit your thumb with the hammer again?
french: Que fais-tu là ? Tu t'es encore tapé sur un doigt avec ton marteau ?
russian: Пришёл в клинику? Что такое, опять ударил молотком по пальцу?
bulgarian: Stopping by the Clinic? Did you hit your thumb with the hammer again?

english: First, there's no such thing as Mist Fever. And second, take this every morning for your allergies.
french: Premièrement, la brumellose, ça n'existe pas. Et deuxièmement, prends ça tous les matins pour tes allergies.
russian: Во-первых, не бывает никакой туманной лихорадки. Во-вторых, вот тебе от аллергии, пей каждое утро.
bulgarian: First, there's no such thing as Mist Fever. And second, take this every morning for your allergies.

english: I think this is it, Valen. I'm coming down with the Mist Fever!
french: Je crois que je suis fichu, Valen. J'ai attrapé la brumellose !
russian: Кажется, это она, Вален. Я подхватил туманную лихорадку!
bulgarian: I think this is it, Valen. I'm coming down with the Mist Fever!

english: <he>He sure has</he><she>She sure has</she><they>They sure have</they><it>It sure has</it><none>[Ari] sure has</none>!
french: Comme tu dis !
russian: Это точно!
bulgarian: <he>He sure has</he><she>She sure has</she><they>They sure have</they><it>It sure has</it><none>[Ari] sure has</none>!

english: I'm happy to see <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> breathe new life into that land. It was all rocks and weeds for too long!
french: Je suis très heureux de voir qu'<he>il</he><she>elle</she><they>iel</they> a réussi à redonner vie à ces terres. Il n'y a pas encore longtemps, c'était une étendue de cailloux et de mauvaises herbes !
russian:
Приятно видеть, что

они вдохнули

она вдохнулаон вдохнулоно вдохнуло новую жизнь в этот участок. Ещё недавно там были только сорняки да камни!
bulgarian: I'm happy to see <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> breathe new life into that land. It was all rocks and weeds for too long!

english: [Ari] has settled into the new farm nicely, <he>hasn't he</he><she>hasn't she</she><they>haven't they</they><it>hasn't it</it><none>hasn't [Ari]</none>?
french: Cette nouvelle vie à la ferme semble bien convenir à [Ari], non ?
russian:
[Ari] так хорошо

обустроились

обустроиласьобустроилсяобустроилось на ферме.
bulgarian: [Ari] has settled into the new farm nicely, <he>hasn't he</he><she>hasn't she</she><they>haven't they</they><it>hasn't it</it><none>hasn't [Ari]</none>?

english: Hmm. I think you're just cold. Warm your hands with a mug of tea before you go back out.
french: Mmm. Je crois que tu as froid, tout simplement. Réchauffe tes mains avec une tasse de thé avant de repartir.
russian: Хмм. Кажется, ты просто замёрз. Подержи кружку горячего чая, прежде чем пойдёшь на улицу.
bulgarian: Hmm. I think you're just cold. Warm your hands with a mug of tea before you go back out.

english: My fingers got so numb that I can't quite tell if I hammered my thumb or not.
french: J'ai les doigts tellement engourdis que je n'arrive pas à savoir si je me suis tapé sur un pouce ou pas.
russian: У меня пальцы до того онемели, что я даже не знаю, попал я по ним молотком или нет.
bulgarian: My fingers got so numb that I can't quite tell if I hammered my thumb or not.

english: Aw, nothing like that! Figured I'd stop in to say hello!
french: Non, ne t'inquiète pas ! Je suis juste passé te dire bonjour !
russian: Ай, да ничего такого! Просто решил зайти поздороваться.
bulgarian: Aw, nothing like that! Figured I'd stop in to say hello!

english: Is everything alright, Hayden? Are you injured? Are the animals down on the farm unwell?
french: Tout va bien, Hayden ? Tu es blessé ? Tes animaux sont malades ?
russian: Что-то случилось, Хейден? Ты поранился? Или животные плохо себя чувствуют?
bulgarian: Is everything alright, Hayden? Are you injured? Are the animals down on the farm unwell?

english: Nothing in particular! Just been a while since I dropped in to say hello.
french: Rien de particulier ! Ça faisait un moment que je n'étais pas passé te voir.
russian: Да ничему! Просто давно не заходил тебя навестить.
bulgarian: Nothing in particular! Just been a while since I dropped in to say hello.

english: To what do I owe the visit, Hayden?
french: Qu'est-ce qui me vaut l'honneur de cette visite, Hayden ?
russian: Чему обязана твоим визитом, Хейден?
bulgarian: To what do I owe the visit, Hayden?

english: Beach. COOKOUT.
french: Plage et BARBECUE.
russian: Пикник. На. ПЛЯЖЕ!
bulgarian: Beach. COOKOUT.

english: The two most important words of the season.
french: Ce sont les plus importants de la saison.
russian: Действительно, самые важные слова в этом сезоне.
bulgarian: The two most important words of the season.

english: Two words:
french: Deux mots :
russian: Три главных слова:
bulgarian: Two words:

english: Oh, I did a lot of shoveling when I was on the road with the band. Side jobs, you know?
french: Méfie-toi. J'ai roulé ma bosse quand j'étais sur les routes avec mon groupe. Les petits boulots, tu connais ?
russian: О, я много успел покопать снега, когда путешествовал с группой. Знаешь, разные подработки.
bulgarian: Oh, I did a lot of shoveling when I was on the road with the band. Side jobs, you know?

english: That's why they called me the Snow Sage! And in my sagely wisdom, I can tell you: I've definitely shoveled more than you.
french: À l'époque, on m'appelait l'Empereur de la pelle ! Et je peux déjà te dire que j'ai dégagé plus de neige que toi.
russian: Поэтому меня также звали снежным мудрецом! И со своей снежной мудростью я тебе говорю: я точно накопал больше.
bulgarian: That's why they called me the Snow Sage! And in my sagely wisdom, I can tell you: I've definitely shoveled more than you.

english: I'm telling you, Hemlock, you'll never shovel up more snow than me! When I was growing up, they called me the Snow King.
french: Hemlock, je te parie que tu ne déblaieras jamais plus de neige que moi ! Quand j'étais jeune, on m'appelait le Roi de la pelle.
russian: Говорю тебе, Хемлок, ты не сможешь накопать снега, как я! Когда я был маленький, меня называли снежный король!
bulgarian: I'm telling you, Hemlock, you'll never shovel up more snow than me! When I was growing up, they called me the Snow King.

english: Holt, that's the plain scramble.
french: Non, Holt, il n'y a que de l'œuf.
russian: Хольт, это обычная яичница.
bulgarian: Holt, that's the plain scramble.

english: Oh, this scramble is SPICY. What's in here, fire peppers?
french: Oh, ces œufs brouillés sont un peu relevés. Tu as ajouté du piment dedans ?
russian: Ох, яичница такая ОСТРАЯ! Что в ней, огненный перец?
bulgarian: Oh, this scramble is SPICY. What's in here, fire peppers?

english: She is! I'm proud of her, though I know Nora frets.
french: Et comment ! Je suis fier d'elle, même si Nora est un peu moins enthousiaste.
russian: Это точно! Я ей горжусь, хотя знаю, что Нора переживает.
bulgarian: She is! I'm proud of her, though I know Nora frets.

english: Oh, I can't help it. She's struck out on her own much earlier than I did.
french: Oh, c'est plus fort que moi. Elle a quitté la maison bien plus tôt que moi.
russian: Я не могу не переживать. Она отделилась от семьи гораздо раньше, чем я.
bulgarian: Oh, I can't help it. She's struck out on her own much earlier than I did.

english: Oh, Nora! She's not so far away! And we're even eating greens from her garden!
french: Nora, elle vit à deux pas d'ici ! On mange même les légumes de son jardin !
russian: Ой, Нора, не так уж она и отделилась! У нас на столе зелень из её сада!
bulgarian: Oh, Nora! She's not so far away! And we're even eating greens from her garden!

english: True... that does save us a lot of money.
french: C'est vrai... Ça permet de faire des économies.
russian: Это правда... Существенно сокращает наши расходы.
bulgarian: True... that does save us a lot of money.

english: And it's nice to have her so close.
french: Et c'est rassurant de la savoir aussi près.
russian: И приятно, что она недалеко.
bulgarian: And it's nice to have her so close.

english: I walked by Celine's cottage the other day! She's doing great on her own.
french: Je suis passé devant chez Céline l'autre jour ! Elle a l'air de bien se débrouiller toute seule.
russian: Я недавно проходил мимо домика Селин. Она отлично обустроилась.
bulgarian: I walked by Celine's cottage the other day! She's doing great on her own.

english: It really is so pretty out here. Celine's been outdoing herself with the gardening!
french: C'est vraiment joli ici. Céline fait un travail extraordinaire dans ces jardins !
russian: Здесь правда так красиво! Селин с этим садом превзошла саму себя!
bulgarian: It really is so pretty out here. Celine's been outdoing herself with the gardening!

english: Evening, [Ari]. We were just enjoying a romantic walk.
french: Bonsoir, [Ari]. On fait une petite balade en amoureux.
russian: Вечера, [Ari]. Мы тут наслаждаемся романтической прогулкой.
bulgarian: Evening, [Ari]. We were just enjoying a romantic walk.

english: Frowning? I don't frown...
french: Quoi ? Mais non, je ne fronce pas les sourcils...
russian: Хмурый? Я не хмурюсь...
bulgarian: Frowning? I don't frown...

english: Maple, mind your manners!
french: Maple, sois polie !
russian: Мэйпл, это невежливо!
bulgarian: Maple, mind your manners!

english: And you do frown, March. Like, a little.
french: Cela dit, c'est vrai que tu fronces souvent les sourcils, March.
russian: Но ты правда хмуришься, Март. Ну, чуть-чуть.
bulgarian: And you do frown, March. Like, a little.

english: More like a lot.
french: Tout le temps même !
russian: Вообще-то, не чуть-чуть.
bulgarian: More like a lot.

english: Honey, manners!
french: Chéri, voyons !
russian: Дорогой, это невежливо!
bulgarian: Honey, manners!

english: I have good manners, so I'm not going to talk about how Mister March frowns all day, every day. I'm going to keep that thought to myself.
french: Comme je suis poli, je ne dirai pas que monsieur March fronce les sourcils du matin au soir. Je préfère garder ça pour moi.
russian: А я веду себя вежливо, поэтому я не буду обсуждать, как мистер Март весь день хмурится, каждый день. Я лучше молча про это подумаю.
bulgarian: I have good manners, so I'm not going to talk about how Mister March frowns all day, every day. I'm going to keep that thought to myself.

english: Wow, Luc! You're such a grown-up!
french: Bravo, Luc ! J'admire ta maturité !
russian: Ух ты, Люк! Какой ты взрослый!
bulgarian: Wow, Luc! You're such a grown-up!

english: Mister March, why are you always frowning like that?
french: Monsieur March, pourquoi est-ce que vous froncez tout le temps les sourcils ?
russian: Мистер Март, почему вы всегда такой хмурый?
bulgarian: Mister March, why are you always frowning like that?

english: Honey, can you slide over the salt?
french: Chérie, tu peux me donner le sel ?
russian: Дорогая, передай соль, пожалуйста!
bulgarian: Honey, can you slide over the salt?

english: Luc, would you be a sweetheart and give me the salt?
french: Luc, mon ange, peux-tu me donner le sel ?
russian: Люк, дружочек, передай мне, пожалуйста, соль!
bulgarian: Luc, would you be a sweetheart and give me the salt?

english: I think Maple has it?
french: Je crois que c'est Maple qui l'a.
russian: По-моему, она у Мэйпл.
bulgarian: I think Maple has it?

english: I don't have it.
french: Non, je ne l'ai pas.
russian: У меня нет.
bulgarian: I don't have it.

english: Here it is!
french: Ah, le voilà !
russian: Вот она!
bulgarian: Here it is!

english: That's sugar, Olric.
french: C'est le sucre, Olric.
russian: Это сахар, Ольрик.
bulgarian: That's sugar, Olric.

english: Can someone pass the salt?
french: Quelqu'un peut me passer le sel ?
russian: Может кто-нибудь передать соль?
bulgarian: Can someone pass the salt?

english: Sweetheart, you wouldn't tell me even if it tasted bad. That's why March is here, to give his honest opinion. What do you think, March?
french: Même si c'était immangeable, tu ne me le dirais pas, mon chéri. March va me donner son avis. Alors, comment trouves-tu ça, March ?
russian: Дорогой, ты бы мне не сказал, даже если бы было невкусно. Поэтому я пригласила Марта, чтобы получить честный отзыв. Ну как тебе, Март?
bulgarian: Sweetheart, you wouldn't tell me even if it tasted bad. That's why March is here, to give his honest opinion. What do you think, March?

english: It's okay, I guess.
french: C'est pas mauvais.
russian: Сойдёт, пожалуй.
bulgarian: It's okay, I guess.

english: And Olric is here to translate!
french: Et Olric est là pour traduire !
russian: А Ольрик здесь в качестве переводчика!
bulgarian: And Olric is here to translate!

english: That means he loves it, and he wants seconds!
french: Autrement dit, il adore et il veut du rab !
russian: Это значит, что ему очень понравилось и он хочет добавки!
bulgarian: That means he loves it, and he wants seconds!

english: Oh, this is delicious!
french: Mmm, c'est délicieux !
russian: Ох, до чего вкусно!
bulgarian: Oh, this is delicious!

english: It's tart and sweet, just like you darling!
french: C'est frais et acidulé, comme toi, ma chérie !
russian: Сладкое и слегка остренькое, как и ты, моя любимая!
bulgarian: It's tart and sweet, just like you darling!

english: Mm, I love it. I might use less sugar and more cocoa.
french: J'aime beaucoup, mais je mettrais peut-être un peu moins de sucre et plus de cacao.
russian: Ммм, вкуснота. Я бы положила меньше сахара и больше какао.
bulgarian: Mm, I love it. I might use less sugar and more cocoa.

english: The cherries are my favorite part.
french: Ce qui me plaît le plus, c'est les cerises.
russian: Мне больше всего нравится вишня.
bulgarian: The cherries are my favorite part.

english: Seconds, please!
french: J'en reprendrais bien !
russian: Добавки, пожалуйста!
bulgarian: Seconds, please!

english: So? Tell me what you think and be honest!
french: Alors ? Dites-moi sincèrement ce que vous en pensez !
russian: Ну как? Только говори честно, что думаешь.
bulgarian: So? Tell me what you think and be honest!

english: Have mine too, bro!
french: Tu peux prendre ma part, si tu veux !
russian: Давай поделюсь, бро!
bulgarian: Have mine too, bro!

english: Wow, that's a rave review from March.
french: Eh bien, March fait rarement de commentaire de ce genre.
russian: Ого, это что, хвалебный отзыв от Марта?
bulgarian: Wow, that's a rave review from March.

english: That's why I like asking March to taste test my new dishes! He's a tough critic.
french: C'est pour ça que j'aime demander à March de goûter mes nouveaux plats ! Il ne prend pas de pincettes.
russian: Поэтому я и люблю давать новые блюда ему на дегустацию. Март — суровый критик.
bulgarian: That's why I like asking March to taste test my new dishes! He's a tough critic.

english: One of the toughest we've got!
french: C'est le moins qu'on puisse dire !
russian: Один из самых суровых, что я знаю!
bulgarian: One of the toughest we've got!

english: This new dish... it's good...
french: Ce nouveau plat... Il est bon...
russian: Это новое блюдо... такое вкусное...
bulgarian: This new dish... it's good...

english: And remember, bro... you can't say that it needs more salt.
french: Et March, tu n'as pas le droit de dire que ça manque de sel.
russian: Учти, бро... Нельзя просто сказать, что оно недосолено.
bulgarian: And remember, bro... you can't say that it needs more salt.

english: But it needs more salt.
french: Pourtant, ça manque de sel.
russian: Но оно недосолено.
bulgarian: But it needs more salt.

english: Hah!
french: Ha !
russian: Ха!
bulgarian: Hah!

english: You always say that! Give me something to work with, March.
french: Tu dis toujours ça ! Élabore un peu plus, March.
russian: Ты всегда так говоришь! Но мы же спрашиваем про сам состав блюда, Март.
bulgarian: You always say that! Give me something to work with, March.

english: So? What do you think? Does Reina's revised dish taste better?
french: Alors, qu'en pensez-vous ? La nouvelle version du plat de Reina est-elle meilleure ?
russian: Ну, что думаете? Рейна изменила рецепт. Так вкуснее?
bulgarian: So? What do you think? Does Reina's revised dish taste better?

english: It's looking promising! Adeline is all in.
french: Très bien ! Adeline s'investit à fond.
russian: Пока обнадёживающе. Аделина вся в работе.
bulgarian: It's looking promising! Adeline is all in.

english: With her and [Ari] here, it's only a matter of time! Soon we'll have those bustling Saturdays back again.
french: Avec elle et [Ari], ça va aller vite ! Bientôt, nous aurons à nouveau des samedis pleins d'animation, comme avant.
russian: А ещё ей помогает [Ari], так что это лишь вопрос времени. Скоро у нас снова по субботам будет толпа!
bulgarian: With her and [Ari] here, it's only a matter of time! Soon we'll have those bustling Saturdays back again.

english: How's the Saturday Market revival coming along?
french: Comment avance le projet de réouverture du marché du samedi ?
russian: Как идёт восстановление Субботнего базара?
bulgarian: How's the Saturday Market revival coming along?

english: Well, we can't have that! I'll pass it on to Ryis, he'll drop by and take a look.
french: Non, ce n'est pas possible ! Je dirai à Ryis de passer.
russian: Нет уж, это нельзя оставлять! Я передам Ризу, он зайдёт и посмотрит.
bulgarian: Well, we can't have that! I'll pass it on to Ryis, he'll drop by and take a look.

english: Not a rush, but one of our barstools has developed a bit of a wobble.
french: Ce n'est rien d'urgent, mais un de nos tabourets de bar commence à avoir un peu de jeu.
russian: Это не к спеху, но один из наших барных стульев слегка шатается.
bulgarian: Not a rush, but one of our barstools has developed a bit of a wobble.
