english: I bet I can learn something about foreign metalworking if I could just inspect it.
french: Si je pouvais y jeter un coup d'œil, ça me permettrait d'en savoir plus sur la façon dont ils travaillent le métal ailleurs.
russian: Я уверен, что много бы узнал о кузнечном деле за границей, если бы только мог осмотреть его.
bulgarian: I bet I can learn something about foreign metalworking if I could just inspect it.

english: I'd give up on that, March. If there's two things Juniper's protective of, it's Dozy and that cauldron of hers.
french: Oublie ça, March. S'il y a bien deux choses que Juniper protège bec et ongles, c'est Dozy et son chaudron.
russian: Я бы на твоём месте сдался, Март. Джунипер зорко следит за двумя вещами: за Дрёмой и за этим своим котлом.
bulgarian: I'd give up on that, March. If there's two things Juniper's protective of, it's Dozy and that cauldron of hers.

english: Three, if you're counting her shoe collection.
french: Trois, si on compte sa collection de chaussures.
russian: За тремя, если считать её коллекцию обуви.
bulgarian: Three, if you're counting her shoe collection.

english: Juniper won't empty that cauldron so I can get a closer look at it.
french: Juniper refuse de vider son chaudron pour que je l'examine de plus près.
russian: Джунипер отказывается выливать котёл, чтобы я мог на него посмотреть.
bulgarian: Juniper won't empty that cauldron so I can get a closer look at it.

english: I can make the pot, but I need to know...
french: Je peux te faire ça, mais dis-moi...
russian: Котёл сделать я могу, но ты скажи мне...
bulgarian: I can make the pot, but I need to know...

english: How was the soup?
french: Elle était comment la soupe ?
russian: Хороший вышел суп?
bulgarian: How was the soup?

english: Think you could make me a new pot? The kids burnt the other one trying to make Dragonguard soup.
french: Est-ce que tu pourrais me fabriquer une nouvelle marmite ? Les enfants ont brûlé la mienne en voulant préparer de la soupe pour la Garde des dragons.
russian: Как думаешь, сможешь сделать новый котёл? А то этот дети сожгли, когда хотели приготовить суп Драконьей стражи.
bulgarian: Think you could make me a new pot? The kids burnt the other one trying to make Dragonguard soup.

english: You got it, boss!
french: OK, patron !
russian: Понял, босс!
bulgarian: You got it, boss!

english: We're brewing today, Olric! The first step is mashing... we need to crush the grains so we can mix them up to make the mash.
french: C'est le jour du brassage, Olric ! On commence par l'empâtage... Il faut broyer les céréales pour obtenir la maïsche.
russian: Сегодня варим пиво, Ольрик! Начнём с растирки... зёрна надо растереть, чтобы они перемешались в однородную смесь.
bulgarian: We're brewing today, Olric! The first step is mashing... we need to crush the grains so we can mix them up to make the mash.

english: Any time! I'm not much for beer, but I do love picking up heavy stuff!
french: Tout le plaisir est pour moi ! Je n'aime pas trop la bière, mais j'adore soulever du poids !
russian: Обращайся! Я по пиву не очень, зато обожаю таскать тяжёлые штуки!
bulgarian: Any time! I'm not much for beer, but I do love picking up heavy stuff!

english: Thanks for the assist, Olric. I think this beer brewing project is going to be big!
french: Merci pour ton aide, Olric. Cette production de bière promet d'être une réussite !
russian: Спасибо за помощь, Ольрик. Кажется, у нас будет грандиозный пивоварный проект!
bulgarian: Thanks for the assist, Olric. I think this beer brewing project is going to be big!

english: For sure, boss! Just say the word and I'm there!
french: Pas de problème, patron ! Tu me dis quand et j'accours.
russian: Так точно, босс! Зови — и я приду!
bulgarian: For sure, boss! Just say the word and I'm there!

english: I've got another open shift at the Inn coming up, if you've got time in your schedule.
french: J'aurai bientôt besoin d'un extra à l'auberge, si jamais tu peux caser ça dans ton emploi du temps.
russian: У меня скоро будет окошко на смену в трактире. Приходи, если тебе подходит по графику.
bulgarian: I've got another open shift at the Inn coming up, if you've got time in your schedule.

english: I'd like to think so! But maybe we should give <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> an extra big helping of soup the next time <he>he comes</he><she>she comes</she><they>they come</they><it>it comes</it><none>[Ari] comes</none> through.
french: Je le pense, oui ! Mais on devrait peut-être quand même lui offrir une grosse ration de soupe en plus, la prochaine fois.
russian:
Я тоже надеюсь! Давай нальём

им

ейемуему огромную порцию супа, когда

они зайдут

она зайдётон зайдетоно зайдёт в следующий раз.
bulgarian: I'd like to think so! But maybe we should give <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> an extra big helping of soup the next time <he>he comes</he><she>she comes</she><they>they come</they><it>it comes</it><none>[Ari] comes</none> through.

english: I was once an out-of-towner like [Ari]... I hope we're giving <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> a warm enough welcome!
french: Moi aussi, je suis arrivé ici sans connaître personne, comme [Ari]... J'espère que nous lui avons fait un accueil assez chaleureux !
russian:
Когда-то я тоже был здесь приезжим, как [Ari]... Надеюсь, мы не слишком сурово

их

еёегоего встретили.
bulgarian: I was once an out-of-towner like [Ari]... I hope we're giving <he>him</he><she>her</she><they>them</they><it>it</it><none>[Ari]</none> a warm enough welcome!

english: Oho, now this is a stick! I know just what I'll carve out of this!
french: Ho ho, quel beau bâton ! Je sais exactement ce que je vais en faire !
russian: Ого, вот это палка! Уже вижу, что я из неё вырежу.
bulgarian: Oho, now this is a stick! I know just what I'll carve out of this!

english: Nothing like gathering wood out on the Eastern Road to get your blood pumping!
french: Il n'y a rien de mieux que de ramasser du bois sur la route de l'est pour faire de l'exercice !
russian: Собирать деревяшки на Восточной дороге — лучший способ размять мышцы!
bulgarian: Nothing like gathering wood out on the Eastern Road to get your blood pumping!

english: You're putting me on, Landen! You know that's a cow!
french: Tu te fiches de moi, Landen ? Tu vois bien que c'est une vache !
russian: Ты шутишь, Ланден? Видно же, что это корова.
bulgarian: You're putting me on, Landen! You know that's a cow!

english: Is it a bird? Oh, it's a capybara. No, that's not right. Don't tell me, I'm going to guess it!
french: C'est un oiseau ? Un capybara ? Non, ce n'est pas ça. Ne dis rien, je vais deviner !
russian: Это птица? А, это капибара. Нет, погоди. Не говори мне, сейчас угадаю.
bulgarian: Is it a bird? Oh, it's a capybara. No, that's not right. Don't tell me, I'm going to guess it!

english: Wish I'd known that before I started my new project... have any scraps lying around?
french: J'aurais bien aimé le savoir avant de démarrer mon nouveau projet... Tu n'en aurais pas un peu ?
russian: Жаль, что сейчас это узнал, когда уже начал... У тебя есть ненужные бруски?
bulgarian: Wish I'd known that before I started my new project... have any scraps lying around?

english: Oh, that wood's no good for whittling... too hard. You want something softer, like willow or cedar.
french: Oh, on ne peut rien sculpter dans ce bois... il est trop dur. Il faut un bois plus tendre, comme du saule ou du cèdre.
russian: О, нет, это дерево не для резьбы... Слишком твёрдое. Тебе бы что-нибудь помягче: иву или кедр, например.
bulgarian: Oh, that wood's no good for whittling... too hard. You want something softer, like willow or cedar.

english: You'll want something nice and soft for that. Next time you're by the woodshop, I'll see what we've got.
french: Pour ça, il faut du bois tendre. La prochaine fois que tu viens à la menuiserie, on regardera.
russian: Лучше подбери мягкое и податливое. В следующий раз, когда заглянешь в мастерскую, посмотрим, что у меня есть.
bulgarian: You'll want something nice and soft for that. Next time you're by the woodshop, I'll see what we've got.

english: I think I'm going to need some more whittling wood soon.
french: Je crois que je vais bientôt avoir besoin de plus de bois pour mes sculptures.
russian: Кажется, мне скоро понадобится ещё дерево для резьбы.
bulgarian: I think I'm going to need some more whittling wood soon.

english: Yeah. Dell had the idea to make it a dragon's head buckle, where the jaw is a hinge. It's a pretty interesting challenge.
french: Oui. Dell a suggéré une boucle en forme de tête de dragon. La mâchoire formerait la barre qui tient la boucle. C'est un défi plutôt intéressant.
russian: Ага. Делл придумала сделать её в виде головы дракона, чтобы изгиб был похож на челюсть. Занимательная задача.
bulgarian: Yeah. Dell had the idea to make it a dragon's head buckle, where the jaw is a hinge. It's a pretty interesting challenge.

english: She didn't offer to pay you, right March? You know she doesn't have any money...
french: Elle n'a pas proposé de te payer, hein, March ? Tu sais qu'elle n'a pas d'argent...
russian: Она же не предлагала тебе деньги, правда, Март? Ты же знаешь, что у неё нет...
bulgarian: She didn't offer to pay you, right March? You know she doesn't have any money...

english: Dell tells me you're working on a new project. A belt buckle?
french: Dell m'a dit que tu travaillais sur un nouveau projet. C'est une boucle de ceinture ?
russian: Делл говорит, у тебя новый проект. Пряжка для ремня?
bulgarian: Dell tells me you're working on a new project. A belt buckle?

english: I-
french: JE...
bulgarian: I-

english: And you get mad easily, too.
french: Sans compter que tu t'énerves facilement.
russian: Я же говорю: легко распаляешься!
bulgarian: And you get mad easily, too.

english: Bravo, Holt.
french: Bien tenté, Holt.
russian: Браво, Хольт.
bulgarian: Bravo, Holt.

english: Aw shucks!
french: Ah zut !
russian: Ну вот!
bulgarian: Aw shucks!

english: I've had that one in my pocket for weeks!
french: Ça faisait des semaines que je la préparais, celle-là !
russian: Я уже пару недель хотел это сказать.
bulgarian: I've had that one in my pocket for weeks!

english: Has anyone ever told you you've got a temper when you're at the forge, March? And you get mad easily, too.
french: On t'a déjà dit que tu avais un caractère bien trempé pour un forgeron, March ? Sans compter que tu t'énerves facilement.
russian: Тебе уже говорили, какой у тебя накал в кузнице, Март? И ты так легко распаляешься.
bulgarian: Has anyone ever told you you've got a temper when you're at the forge, March? And you get mad easily, too.

english: Remember when I tried to make a standing bass from my mom's wash basin?
french: Tu te souviens quand j'ai pris la corbeille à linge de ma mère pour en faire une contrebasse ?
russian: Помнишь, как я пытался сделать контрабас из маминого корыта?
bulgarian: Remember when I tried to make a standing bass from my mom's wash basin?

english: She NEVER forgave me for putting that hole in the bottom, hahaha!
french: Elle ne m'a jamais pardonné d'avoir fait un trou dans le fond, ha ha ha !
russian: Она так и не простила меня за дырку в дне, которую я проделал, ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: She NEVER forgave me for putting that hole in the bottom, hahaha!

english: When we were kids Holt and I tried to make a band with Jo, but the two of us never had any musical talent... I'm so happy she met Hemlock, they're such a pair.
french: Jeunes, Holt et moi, on avait voulu monter un groupe avec Jo, mais ni lui ni moi ne savions jouer... Je suis tellement heureuse qu'elle ait rencontré Hemlock. Ils font la paire.
russian: Когда мы были маленькие, мы с Хольтом хотели сделать группу с Джо, но у нас с ним нет таланта к музыке... Я так рада, что она нашла Хемлока: они отличная пара.
bulgarian: When we were kids Holt and I tried to make a band with Jo, but the two of us never had any musical talent... I'm so happy she met Hemlock, they're such a pair.

english: That's for sure! Between us we couldn't keep a cactus alive.
french: Ni de moi ! Même les cactus mouraient avec nous.
russian: Я тоже не знаю! У нас с тобой вдвоём и кактус не выживет!
bulgarian: That's for sure! Between us we couldn't keep a cactus alive.

english: Hahaha!
french: Ha ha ha !
russian: Ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Hahaha!

english: The flowers around the Manor look so nice! You know, Holt, I have no idea where Celine got her green thumb. It certainly wasn't me.
french: Les fleurs du manoir sont sublimes ! Je ne sais pas d'où Céline tient ce don, mais pas de moi. Je n'ai pas la main verte.
russian: Цветы вокруг особняка выглядят просто чудесно! Знаешь, Хольт, я без понятия, в кого Селин такая садовница. Точно не в меня.
bulgarian: The flowers around the Manor look so nice! You know, Holt, I have no idea where Celine got her green thumb. It certainly wasn't me.

english: It's a good thing Nora doesn't have trouble with dairy. I don't know how we'd make it work if she couldn't handle my cheesy jokes.
french: Heureusement que Nora a l'estomac bien solide, sinon je ne sais pas si elle pourrait supporter mes blagues moisies.
russian: Хорошо, что Нора не боится снега. А то я вечно несу пургу.
bulgarian: It's a good thing Nora doesn't have trouble with dairy. I don't know how we'd make it work if she couldn't handle my cheesy jokes.

english: Holt surprised me with a dinner date! Isn't he sweet, [Ari]?
french: Holt m'a fait la surprise d'un dîner en tête-à-tête ! C'est adorable, tu ne trouves pas, [Ari] ?
russian: Хольт неожиданно позвал меня на романтический ужин! Мило, правда, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Holt surprised me with a dinner date! Isn't he sweet, [Ari]?

english: I have no idea! But whenever I see a flower, I think of her frondly.
french: C'est peut-être parce que je mettais de la fleur de sel dans ses purées ?!
russian: Без понятия! Я каждый раз о ней вспоминаю, когда вижу красивый цветок.
bulgarian: I have no idea! But whenever I see a flower, I think of her frondly.

english: Where do you suppose Celine got her green thumb?
french: À ton avis, comment se fait-il que Céline ait la main verte ?
russian: Как думаешь, откуда у Селин её садоводческий талант?
bulgarian: Where do you suppose Celine got her green thumb?

english: It keeps getting better! What are you putting in the relish? What's your secret?
french: Il était à tomber ! Qu'est-ce que tu mets dans la sauce ? C'est quoi, ton secret ?
russian: С каждым разом всё лучше! Что ты кладёшь в этот соус? В чём секрет?
bulgarian: It keeps getting better! What are you putting in the relish? What's your secret?

english: How'd you like that sandwich I packed for your lunch, sweetie?
french: Tu as aimé le sandwich que je t'avais préparé pour le déjeuner, ma chérie ?
russian: Тебе понравился сэндвич, который я собрал тебе с собой, милая?
bulgarian: How'd you like that sandwich I packed for your lunch, sweetie?

english: You're drinking a cup of tea, dear.
french: Tu bois du thé, mon chéri.
russian: Дорогой, ты пьёшь чай из чашки.
bulgarian: You're drinking a cup of tea, dear.

english: It's all about the metaphor, my sweet!
french: Façon de parler, ma douce !
russian: Милая моя, это всё метафора!
bulgarian: It's all about the metaphor, my sweet!

english: No matter the season, nothing's better than cracking a cold one at home after the kids are tucked in.
french: Quelle que soit la saison, il n'y a pas mieux que de s'en jeter une petite bien fraîche quand les enfants sont couchés.
russian: В любое время года приятнее всего взять холодную бутылочку и сидеть дома, когда дети уложены спать.
bulgarian: No matter the season, nothing's better than cracking a cold one at home after the kids are tucked in.

english: I was waiting for the punchline!
french: Parce que je croyais que tu allais me sortir un calembour.
russian: Я думала это шутка!
bulgarian: I was waiting for the punchline!

english: You know, when I proposed to Nora, she left me hanging for quite a while.
french: Quand j'ai demandé Nora en mariage, elle n'a pas répondu aussitôt.
russian: Знаешь, когда я признавался Норе в любви, она долго мне не отвечала.
bulgarian: You know, when I proposed to Nora, she left me hanging for quite a while.

english: And I'm thankful there's no dishes to wash after the meal.
french: Et moi, je suis ravie qu'il n'y ait pas de vaisselle à faire après le repas.
russian: А я радуюсь, что после еды не надо мыть посуду.
bulgarian: And I'm thankful there's no dishes to wash after the meal.

english: Winter's when I'm most thankful that the General Store is a stone's throw away from the Inn.
french: En hiver, je suis content que le magasin général soit si près de l'auberge.
russian: Зимой я больше всего радуюсь, что от универмага до трактира рукой подать.
bulgarian: Winter's when I'm most thankful that the General Store is a stone's throw away from the Inn.

english: To work out her pecks...!
french: Elle doit couver quelque chose...
russian: Проклюнулась тяга к спорту!..
bulgarian: To work out her pecks...!

english: Whoa, good for her! The pecs are an important muscle!
french: Oh, la pauvre ! J'espère que ce n'est rien de grave.
russian: Ух, вот это она молодец! Спорт полезен каждому!
bulgarian: Whoa, good for her! The pecs are an important muscle!

english: No, no... to work out her PECKS.
french: Tu as compris ? Elle doit couver quelque chose.
russian: Да нет же... ПРОКЛЮНУЛАСЬ тяга.
bulgarian: No, no... to work out her PECKS.

english: Y-yeah? You already said that.
french: Ben oui, tu viens de me le dire.
russian: Ну... да? Ты так и сказал.
bulgarian: Y-yeah? You already said that.

english: Her... pecks?
french: Elle... couve...
russian: Про-клюнула-сь?..
bulgarian: Her... pecks?

english: Hey, Olric! Why'd Henrietta go to the gym?
french: Hé, Olric ! Tu sais pourquoi Henrietta est allée chez le médecin ?!
russian: Эй, Ольрик! Почему Генриетта пошла в спортзал?
bulgarian: Hey, Olric! Why'd Henrietta go to the gym?

english: Name the time and place, my man!
french: Tu me dis quand et où et j'arrive !
russian: Конечно, только скажи, когда и где!
bulgarian: Name the time and place, my man!

english: Think you could help me lift a shelf, Olric? It's gone a bit crooked and I'd love to get a shim under there.
french: Tu pourrais m'aider à soulever un présentoir, Olric ? Il est un peu de travers, et je voudrais mettre une cale.
russian: Можешь помочь мне поднять шкаф, Ольрик? Он слегка покосился, хочу под него что-нибудь подложить!
bulgarian: Think you could help me lift a shelf, Olric? It's gone a bit crooked and I'd love to get a shim under there.

english: Oh, does he now? Well, right back at him!
french: Ah oui ? Eh bien, tout pareil !
russian: Вот как? Тогда верни ему привет обратно.
bulgarian: Oh, does he now? Well, right back at him!

english: Uncle Landen says hi, Holt!
french: Oncle Landen te passe le bonjour, Holt !
russian: Дядя Ланден передаёт привет, Хольт!
bulgarian: Uncle Landen says hi, Holt!

english: Oh... haha, that's okay, Holt. I'm good.
french: Oh... ha ha, ne t'en fais pas, Holt. Tu finiras par trouver.
russian: Ох, Хольт... ха-ха, спасибо, но не надо.
bulgarian: Oh... haha, that's okay, Holt. I'm good.

english: Yeah... it's just that none of the jokes wood work!
french: Ouais... je touche du bois !
russian: Да, понимашь... не хотелось рубить с плеча!
bulgarian: Yeah... it's just that none of the jokes wood work!

english: I knew we were going to meet up today, so I've been trying to come up with a pun just for you.
french: Je savais qu'on se verrait aujourd'hui, alors j'ai essayé de trouver un jeu de mots.
russian: Я готовился к нашей сегодняшней встрече и хотел придумать какой-нибудь каламбур про древесину.
bulgarian: I knew we were going to meet up today, so I've been trying to come up with a pun just for you.

english: I appreciate it! Maybe now folks will stop calling me unhinged!
french: Merci bien ! Au moins, elle ne s'ouvrira plus n'im-porte comment !
russian: Спасибо! Может, теперь люди перестанут говорить, что у меня с крышей не в порядке!
bulgarian: I appreciate it! Maybe now folks will stop calling me unhinged!

english: I tightened those hinges on the door to your shop, Holt.
french: J'ai resserré les gonds de la porte du magasin, Holt.
russian: Хольт, я подлатал вам крышу универмага.
bulgarian: I tightened those hinges on the door to your shop, Holt.

english: 'Course we were a lot younger back then, neither of us had managed to grow a mustache yet.
french: On était jeunes à l'époque. Notre moustache n'avait pas encore poussé.
russian: Мы, конечно, тогда все были гораздо моложе, все ходили без усов.
bulgarian: 'Course we were a lot younger back then, neither of us had managed to grow a mustache yet.

english: That's... actually kind of hard to imagine.
french: C'est le genre de trucs que j'ai du mal à imaginer.
russian: В это даже... с трудом верится.
bulgarian: That's... actually kind of hard to imagine.

english: In fact, I helped your Uncle install these shelves!
french: Tu sais que j'ai aidé ton oncle à installer ces rayonnages !
russian: Вообще-то я помогал твоему дяде ставить эти шкафы!
bulgarian: In fact, I helped your Uncle install these shelves!

english: Before you arrived, things were really starting to... drag-on.
french: Moi je ne savais pas comment vous aborder, mais ma femme m'a dit « Dame Seridia, tu la sers, idiot ! ».
russian: С тобой наши беды, наконец... дра-кончились.
bulgarian: Before you arrived, things were really starting to... drag-on.

english: How delightful.
french: Quel ravissement !
russian: Восхитительно.
bulgarian: How delightful.

english: To drag on... meaning to persist excessively, but also a portmanteau creating the word "dragon".
french: « Sers, idiot »... Ces deux mots accolés forment presque mon prénom.
russian: Кончиться — означает «прекратить существование» и при этом начинается тем же слогом, которым кончается слово «дракон».
bulgarian: To drag on... meaning to persist excessively, but also a portmanteau creating the word "dragon".

english: I am amused. Tell me another, you funny little man.
french: Que c'est divertissant ! Un autre jeu de mots, je vous prie, petit homme amusant.
russian: Ты меня позабавил. Пошути ещё, смешной человек.
bulgarian: I am amused. Tell me another, you funny little man.

english: It's real fun having you in town, Seridia!
french: C'est vraiment bien que vous vous soyez installée en ville, Seridia !
russian: Хорошо, что ты теперь живёшь с нами, Серидия!
bulgarian: It's real fun having you in town, Seridia!

english: Oh! I'll do my best!
french: Oh ! Je vais faire de mon mieux.
russian: О! Сейчас попробую!
bulgarian: Oh! I'll do my best!

english: But just so you know, I don't have a whole lot of tales... I'm just winging it!
french: Mais si j'échoue, je serai dans de beaux draps... et vous sortirez de vos gonds !
russian: Но дело в том, что мне не хвостило историй про драконов... Приходится выдумывать на лету!
bulgarian: But just so you know, I don't have a whole lot of tales... I'm just winging it!

english: Ah. Using "tales" as a homophone for "tails"...
french: Ah. Vous avez placé les mots « draps » et « gonds » dans la même phrase...
russian: А. «Хватило» по звучанию похоже на «хвост»...
bulgarian: Ah. Using "tales" as a homophone for "tails"...

english: And using the word "winging", referring to wings, but also the act of improvising a story in the process of telling it.
french: Afin de former « dragon » et ainsi rendre hommage à ma forme originelle.
russian: А «выдумывать на лету» означает «импровизировать» и в то же время ассоциируется с полётом дракона.
bulgarian: And using the word "winging", referring to wings, but also the act of improvising a story in the process of telling it.

english: Wonderful. I am sated.
french: Merveilleux. Je suis satisfaite.
russian: Чудесно. Я довольна.
bulgarian: Wonderful. I am sated.

english: Shopkeep! I demand entertainment.
french: Boutiquier ! Veuillez me divertir.
russian: Эй, лавочник! Развлеки меня.
bulgarian: Shopkeep! I demand entertainment.

english: If I were still Witch Queen, you would be the dark jester of my retinue.
french: Si j'étais encore Reine-sorcière, je vous ferais bouffon funeste de la cour.
russian: Если бы я была на троне, ты в моей свите был бы мрачным шутом.
bulgarian: If I were still Witch Queen, you would be the dark jester of my retinue.

english: That's claw-some! I'm glad my jokes are up to scratch!
french: Pour vous, je serais prêt à descendre dans l'arène, Ma Reine.
russian: Я окрылён! Пламенно вас благодарю!
bulgarian: That's claw-some! I'm glad my jokes are up to scratch!

english: Yes... quite exquisite, my jester.
french: Oui... C'est exquis, mon gentil bouffon.
russian: Да... Прелестно, мой шут.
bulgarian: Yes... quite exquisite, my jester.

english: I am ever impressed by your skills at delivering exquisite pain with words, Holt.
french: Votre capacité à infliger une douleur si exquise à l'aide de mots ne cesse de m'impressionner, Holt.
russian: Меня восхищает твой талант доставлять невероятную боль словами, Хольт.
bulgarian: I am ever impressed by your skills at delivering exquisite pain with words, Holt.

english: It's more like they won't leave, no matter how many times I ask.
french: C'est surtout qu'ils ne veulent pas partir, même quand je leur demande.
russian: Скорее, дело в том, что они не уходят, сколько бы я ни просила.
bulgarian: It's more like they won't leave, no matter how many times I ask.

english: Huh?
french: Hein ?
russian: А?
bulgarian: Huh?

english: I said, no problem! Any time!
french: Je disais que c'était avec plaisir ! Quand tu veux !
russian: Говорю, мне несложно! Обращайся!
bulgarian: I said, no problem! Any time!

english: You get on so well with the kids! Thanks for keeping an eye on them every once in a while.
french: Tu t'entends à merveille avec les enfants ! Merci de les garder de temps en temps.
russian: Ты так хорошо ладишь с детьми! Спасибо, что присматриваешь за ними иногда.
bulgarian: You get on so well with the kids! Thanks for keeping an eye on them every once in a while.

english: Ah... that explains why the children keep running to my cauldron and yelling FREE SOUP!
french: Ah... C'est pour ça que les enfants tournent autour de mon chaudron en criant LA BONNE SOUPE GRATUITE !
russian: А... Тогда понятно, почему дети всё время лезут в мой котёл с криками: «БЕСПЛАТНЫЙ СУП!»
bulgarian: Ah... that explains why the children keep running to my cauldron and yelling FREE SOUP!

english: Oh, yes... the pot at the Inn is open to anyone who needs a bowl. Hadn't you noticed?
french: Mais oui. Tout le monde peut se servir dans la marmite à l'auberge. Tu n'avais pas remarqué ?
russian: А, да... котёл в трактире стоит для всех, кому хочется супа. Ты не пробовала?
bulgarian: Oh, yes... the pot at the Inn is open to anyone who needs a bowl. Hadn't you noticed?

english: Oho! I'll stop by as soon as I can.
french: Oh ho ! Je viens dès que j'ai deux minutes.
russian: О-хо! Я зайду, как только освобожусь.
bulgarian: Oho! I'll stop by as soon as I can.

english: We got in that wine you were asking for, Juniper! Come by any time and we'll pour you a glass.
french: On vient de recevoir le cru que tu cherchais, Juniper ! Passe le goûter quand tu veux.
russian: У нас есть вино, о котором ты спрашивала, Джунипер! Заходи, когда захочешь, нальём тебе бокальчик.
bulgarian: We got in that wine you were asking for, Juniper! Come by any time and we'll pour you a glass.

english: Dozy won't let me have wine in the bath, and if I can't do it, then no one can!
french: Dozy ne me laisse jamais prendre un verre quand je suis dans mon bain, alors je ne vois pas pourquoi les autres auraient ce droit !
russian: Дрёма не даёт мне пить вино в ванной, а раз мне нельзя, то и остальным тоже.
bulgarian: Dozy won't let me have wine in the bath, and if I can't do it, then no one can!

english: You're such a wine aficionado, I'm surprised you don't offer wine at the Bathhouse.
french: Vu que tu es amatrice de vin, je suis étonnée que tu n'en proposes pas aux bains.
russian: Ты такая ценительница вина, что даже странно, что ты не предлагаешь вино у себя в купальне.
bulgarian: You're such a wine aficionado, I'm surprised you don't offer wine at the Bathhouse.

english: She became known as the Mantis Queen, and established the Royal Society of Entomologists.
french: Elle devint Sa Majesté des mantes et fonda la Société royale d'entomologie.
russian: Она взяла имя Королева богомолов и основала королевское энтомологическое общество.
bulgarian: She became known as the Mantis Queen, and established the Royal Society of Entomologists.

english: Wowww! The Mantis Queen!
french: Waouh ! Sa Majesté des mantes !
russian: Ух ты-ы-ы, Королева богомолов!
bulgarian: Wowww! The Mantis Queen!

english: And so, the princess was able to identify the mysterious species of insect.
french: Et c'est ainsi que la princesse réussit à identifier cette espèce d'insecte mystérieuse.
russian: И наконец принцессе удалось опознать неведомое насекомое.
bulgarian: And so, the princess was able to identify the mysterious species of insect.

english: Mister March, how do you know Luc and I aren't sitting at the grown-ups table?
french: Monsieur March, vous êtes sûr que ce n'est pas Luc et moi qui sommes à la table des grands ?
russian: Мистер Март, откуда вы знаете, что это не мы с Люком сидим за взрослым столом?
bulgarian: Mister March, how do you know Luc and I aren't sitting at the grown-ups table?

english: That's true. There's no empirical evidence to prove it one way or the other.
french: Oui, nous ne disposons d'aucune preuve empirique ni dans un sens ni dans l'autre.
russian: Действительно. У нас нет эмпирических доказательств той или иной гипотезы.
bulgarian: That's true. There's no empirical evidence to prove it one way or the other.

english: You sure know a lot of big words, Luc!
french: Tu en connais des mots savants, Luc !
russian: Ничего себе ты слова знаешь, Люк!
bulgarian: You sure know a lot of big words, Luc!

english: I think he learned that one at the Museum.
french: Je crois qu'il l'a entendu au musée.
russian: Мне кажется, он этому в музее научился.
bulgarian: I think he learned that one at the Museum.

english: Errol does like to turn their visits into impromptu lessons.
french: Errol profite toujours des visites pour leur apprendre des mots nouveaux.
russian: Эррол любит превращать экскурсии в импровизированные уроки.
bulgarian: Errol does like to turn their visits into impromptu lessons.

english: Hey, how did we end up at the kid's table?
french: Pourquoi on est à la table des enfants ?
russian: Слушай, как так получилось, что мы за детским столом?
bulgarian: Hey, how did we end up at the kid's table?

english: It looks quite old... I wonder if Eiland's had a look at it.
french: Il a l'air très ancien... Je me demande si Eiland l'a bien regardé.
russian: Выглядит весьма старым... Интересно, изучал ли его Эйланд.
bulgarian: It looks quite old... I wonder if Eiland's had a look at it.

english: That bath always makes me feel like a queen! The stone dragon is so majestic...
french: J'ai toujours l'impression d'être une reine quand je suis aux bains ! Ce dragon de pierre est si majestueux...
russian: Когда я прихожу в купальню, сразу чувствую себя королевой! И тут такой великолепный каменный дракон...
bulgarian: That bath always makes me feel like a queen! The stone dragon is so majestic...

english: Ah, that explains why Dell's been muttering about the dragonguard practicing their beetle formation.
french: Ah, ça explique pourquoi Dell dit sans arrêt que la Garde des dragons doit mieux maîtriser la formation en scarabée.
russian: А, тогда понятно, почему Делл что-то бормочет про построение жуком у Драконьей стражи.
bulgarian: Ah, that explains why Dell's been muttering about the dragonguard practicing their beetle formation.

english: Luc is very into horned beetles right now. I never knew there were so many kinds!
french: Luc est obnubilé par les scarabées à cornes en ce moment. Je ne savais pas qu'il en existait autant de sortes !
russian: Люк сейчас увлекается жуками-рогачами. Я даже не знала, что их так много видов!
bulgarian: Luc is very into horned beetles right now. I never knew there were so many kinds!

english: I'm doing the same for Dell.
french: Je fais pareil pour Dell.
russian: Я точно так же откладываю для Делл.
bulgarian: I'm doing the same for Dell.

english: Although knowing her, she'll spend the money on a sword instead of books.
french: Même si, la connaissant, elle dépensera tout son argent pour acheter une épée plutôt que des livres.
russian: Хотя, зная её, она потратит всё на мечи, а не на учебники.
bulgarian: Although knowing her, she'll spend the money on a sword instead of books.

english: Nora's helping me put away some tesserae for Luc's schooling. I'm sure he'll want to study in the Capital one day.
french: Nora m'aide à mettre des tesserae de côté pour les études de Luc. Je suis sûre qu'il ira étudier à la capitale un jour.
russian: Нора помогает мне скопить тессер на обучение Люка. Уверена, ему захочется поехать учиться в столицу.
bulgarian: Nora's helping me put away some tesserae for Luc's schooling. I'm sure he'll want to study in the Capital one day.

english: Really? I can't wait! Holt and I will be there!
french: Vraiment ? Oh, j'ai hâte ! On sera là, Holt et moi !
russian: Правда? Жду с нетерпением! Мы с Хольтом придём послушать!
bulgarian: Really? I can't wait! Holt and I will be there!

english: I think we might sing a little tonight.
french: Je crois qu'on chantera un peu ce soir.
russian: Возможно, мы будем петь сегодня вечером.
bulgarian: I think we might sing a little tonight.

english: The kids are a great excuse to get us to the Beach, too.
french: Et puis, c'est une très bonne excuse pour aller à la plage, nous aussi.
russian: Думаю, дети — отличный повод выбраться на пляж самим.
bulgarian: The kids are a great excuse to get us to the Beach, too.

english: We should take the kids down to the Beach soon, don't you think?
french: Ce serait bien d'emmener les enfants à la plage, non ?
russian: Надо бы отвести детей на пляж, как думаешь?
bulgarian: We should take the kids down to the Beach soon, don't you think?

english: Terithia's stories always get them fired up.
french: Et ils adorent les histoires que leur raconte Terithia.
russian: Это их раззадорили рассказы Теризии.
bulgarian: Terithia's stories always get them fired up.

english: Honestly, me too. That lady's seen things!
french: Moi aussi. Elle a vécu tellement de choses !
russian: Да и меня, честно, тоже. Эта дама многое повидала!
bulgarian: Honestly, me too. That lady's seen things!

english: The children sure do have big imaginations.
french: Les enfants ont beaucoup d'imagination.
russian: У детей такое богатое воображение.
bulgarian: The children sure do have big imaginations.

english: Oh, thank you Valen! She's really blossomed into an exceptional chef, hasn't she?
french: Oh merci, Valen ! Oui, Reina est devenue une chef hors pair, pas vrai ?
russian: Ой, спасибо, Вален! Из неё вышел выдающаяся повариха, правда?
bulgarian: Oh, thank you Valen! She's really blossomed into an exceptional chef, hasn't she?

english: This is delicious, Josephine. Reina's handiwork, I presume?
french: Je me régale, Joséphine. C'était Reina aux fourneaux ?
russian: Восхитительный вкус, Джозефина! Это же Рейна готовила?
bulgarian: This is delicious, Josephine. Reina's handiwork, I presume?

english: The bathhouse is quite rejuvenating. The proprietor, however...
french: Les bains permettent de se ressourcer. Mais la propriétaire...
russian: Купальня отлично восстанавливает самочувствие! Чего не скажешь о её хозяйке...
bulgarian: The bathhouse is quite rejuvenating. The proprietor, however...

english: I see we all had the same idea, coming to the Bathhouse. How fun!
french: Je ne suis pas la seule à avoir eu l'idée de venir aux bains. J'adore !
russian: Я вижу, нам обеим пришла в голову мысль зайти в купальню. Чудно!
bulgarian: I see we all had the same idea, coming to the Bathhouse. How fun!

english: I don't know about suspicious, but Juni's right. The General Store, the Inn, the Blacksmith's, the Museum... you're everywhere!
french: Je ne sais pas si c'est louche, mais Juniper a raison. Au magasin général, à l'auberge, à la forge, à la menuiserie, au musée... tu es partout !
russian: Не думаю, что это подозрительно, но Джуни права. В универмаге, в трактире, в кузнице, в столярной лавке, в музее... ты просто везде!
bulgarian: I don't know about suspicious, but Juni's right. The General Store, the Inn, the Blacksmith's, the Museum... you're everywhere!

english: Aw, you noticed? I picked up some odd jobs. Life is all about the journey, you know?
french: Ah, vous avez remarqué ? C'est juste que je fais des petits boulots à droite à gauche. Et la vie est faite de rencontres, non ?!
russian: Ох, вы заметили, да? Я решил попробовать разные работы. В жизни всё надо попробовать, так ведь?
bulgarian: Aw, you noticed? I picked up some odd jobs. Life is all about the journey, you know?

english: Why am I seeing you everywhere these days, Olric? It's suspicious!
french: Pourquoi je n'arrête pas de te croiser, Olric ? C'est louche !
russian: Почему я тебя в последнее время везде встречаю, Ольрик? Подозрительно!
bulgarian: Why am I seeing you everywhere these days, Olric? It's suspicious!

english: The bathhouse is looking pretty good overall.
french: Dans l'ensemble, les bains sont en bon état.
russian: А в целом твоя купальня в полном порядке.
bulgarian: The bathhouse is looking pretty good overall.

english: Music to my ears. And please, enjoy your next five baths free of charge.
french: Je suis ravie de l'entendre. Profite bien de tes cinq prochains bains gratuits.
russian: Это музыка для моих ушей. Следущие пять раз можешь проходить бесплатно.
bulgarian: Music to my ears. And please, enjoy your next five baths free of charge.

english: Got the inspection all done, Juniper. Might do some weatherproofing on the exterior, but that's just about being prepared.
french: Je viens de finir mon inspection, Juniper. Je ferais peut-être un traitement imperméabilisant sur l'extérieur, mais ce serait pour fignoler.
russian: Джунипер, я закончил осмотр. Может, ещё чуть-чуть проконопачу снаружи — на всякий случай.
bulgarian: Got the inspection all done, Juniper. Might do some weatherproofing on the exterior, but that's just about being prepared.

english: Oh, these? I was simply born into this world with talons crimson as the blood moon.
french: Oh, ça ? Il se trouve que je suis simplement née avec des serres aussi écarlates que la lune rouge.
russian: О, пустяки! Я родилась на свет с когтями, алыми, словно кровавая луна.
bulgarian: Oh, these? I was simply born into this world with talons crimson as the blood moon.

english: Were you not also born with your intricately colored nails?
french: N'êtes-vous pas née vous-même avec des ongles d'une couleur bien particulière ?
russian: А твой замысловатый цвет ногтей у тебя разве не от рождения?
bulgarian: Were you not also born with your intricately colored nails?

english: I presumed it to be an innate characteristic.
french: Je pensais qu'il s'agissait d'une caractéristique innée.
russian: Я полагала, что это природная особенность.
bulgarian: I presumed it to be an innate characteristic.

english: Seridia, I'm always admiring your nails! How do you get them so brilliantly red?
french: Seridia, je suis toujours en train d'admirer vos ongles ! Comment faites-vous pour les vernir d'un rouge aussi vif ?
russian: Серидия, мне ужасно нравятся твои ногти! Как у тебя получается такой сверкающий красный цвет?
bulgarian: Seridia, I'm always admiring your nails! How do you get them so brilliantly red?

english: They were an evergreen fashion in my royal court, worn by followers of all stripes.
french: C'était un style indémodable porté par bien des membres de ma cour royale.
russian: У меня при дворе такие никогда не выходили из моды. Их носили все слои общества
bulgarian: They were an evergreen fashion in my royal court, worn by followers of all stripes.

english: I believe they wished to mimic the tall heel of my draconic gait.
french: Je crois qu'ils cherchaient à imiter la majesté et la hauteur que me conféraient mes serres de dragon.
russian: Полагаю, с помощью высоких каблуков они рассчитывали приблизиться к моей драконьей поступи.
bulgarian: I believe they wished to mimic the tall heel of my draconic gait.

english: Evergreen indeed!
french: Indémodable, comme vous dites !
russian: Поистине вечные ценности!
bulgarian: Evergreen indeed!

english: I have noticed your extensive collection of heeled boots, Juniper.
french: J'ai vu votre collection impressionnante de bottes à hauts talons, Juniper.
russian: Джунипер, я заметила у тебя обширную коллекцию каблуков.
bulgarian: I have noticed your extensive collection of heeled boots, Juniper.

english: I'll suffer for fashion up to point, but Lady Seridia...
french: Je veux bien souffrir pour rester à la mode, dame Seridia, mais il y a des limites...
russian: Я готова страдать за красоту до определённой степени, но всё же, леди Серидия...
bulgarian: I'll suffer for fashion up to point, but Lady Seridia...

english: Defeating a great beast so I can wear its bones? That's so much work!
french: Vaincre une créature redoutable juste pour porter sa carcasse ? Ça me fatigue d'avance !
russian: Сразить жуткое чудовище ради того, чтобы носить его кости, — это так муторно!
bulgarian: Defeating a great beast so I can wear its bones? That's so much work!

english: I do not understand why you will not incorporate bones into your wardrobe, my disciple.
french: Je ne comprends pas pourquoi vous n'intégrez pas davantage d'ossements à votre garde-robe, chère disciple.
russian: Я не понимаю, почему ты отказываешься добавлять в свой гардероб кости, моя послушница.
bulgarian: I do not understand why you will not incorporate bones into your wardrobe, my disciple.

english: Smelling the contents of this cauldron... I am not sure that I would like to be.
french: Et à sentir l'odeur se dégageant de ce chaudron, je préfère que cela reste ainsi.
russian: И, судя по запаху из этого котла... Кажется, и не хочу знать.
bulgarian: Smelling the contents of this cauldron... I am not sure that I would like to be.

english: The kids say the same thing...
french: Les enfants disent la même chose...
russian: Дети тоже жалуются...
bulgarian: The kids say the same thing...

english: It probably needs more lilac.
french: Je devrais peut-être ajouter du lilas.
russian: Надо добавить ещё сирени.
bulgarian: It probably needs more lilac.

english: I am adept at many schools of magic... but potions? I am not so familiar.
french: Je connais bien des types de magie, mais... les potions ? Je ne maîtrise pas très bien le sujet.
russian: Я владею многими школами магии, но... зелья? О зельях я ничего не знаю.
bulgarian: I am adept at many schools of magic... but potions? I am not so familiar.

english: You've been watching me for a while now.
french: Ça fait un fait un bon moment que vous êtes en train de m'observer.
russian: Ты меня пристально рассматриваешь.
bulgarian: You've been watching me for a while now.

english: I wished to observe you at work, my disciple.
french: Je voulais voir la façon dont vous travaillez, chère disciple.
russian: Я желала понаблюдать, как ты работаешь, послушница.
bulgarian: I wished to observe you at work, my disciple.

english: I have a dragon's instinct for hierarchy, and yet my confusion only grows.
french: J'ai un sens de la hiérarchie très prononcé grâce à mon instinct de dragon, pourtant ma confusion ne fait que grandir.
russian: Я дракон, а потому разбираюсь в иерархии от природы. Но ты приводишь меня в замешательство.
bulgarian: I have a dragon's instinct for hierarchy, and yet my confusion only grows.

english: Dozy is your familiar... but also your boss?
french: Dozy est votre animal de compagnie... mais c'est également votre chef ?
russian: Дрёма — твой фамильяр... и одновременно начальник?
bulgarian: Dozy is your familiar... but also your boss?

english: Er... is something the matter, Seridia?
french: Euh... Il y a un problème, Seridia ?
russian: Эм... Что-то не так, Серидия?
bulgarian: Er... is something the matter, Seridia?

english: What can I do to win his trust?
french: Que puis-je faire pour gagner sa confiance ?
russian: Как мне добиться его расположения?
bulgarian: What can I do to win his trust?

english: Dozy? Petting him usually does the trick.
french: Dozy ? Il suffit généralement de le caresser.
russian: Дрёмы? Обычно его достаточно погладить.
bulgarian: Dozy? Petting him usually does the trick.

english: If he comes to me, he will receive pets.
french: S'il vient à moi, alors je daignerai lui accorder des caresses.
russian: Он будет поглажен, если подойдёт ко мне.
bulgarian: If he comes to me, he will receive pets.

english: I think you have to go to him...
french: Je crois qu'il vaut mieux aller à lui...
russian: Думаю, лучше тебе подойти к нему...
bulgarian: I think you have to go to him...

english: Then it seems... we are at an impasse.
french: Dans ce cas, nous sommes dans une impasse.
russian: Что ж, значит... мы зашли в тупик.
bulgarian: Then it seems... we are at an impasse.

english: Your familiar is suspicious of me, my disciple.
french: Votre animal semble se méfier de moi, chère disciple.
russian: Послушница, твой фамильяр мне не доверяет.
bulgarian: Your familiar is suspicious of me, my disciple.

english: More clearly here than anywhere else... even back at the coven.
french: Bien mieux que n'importe où ailleurs... Encore plus qu'au sabbat.
russian: Лучше, чем где-либо ещё... Даже лучше, чем в шабаше.
bulgarian: More clearly here than anywhere else... even back at the coven.

english: Even during my reign, there were few able to sense leylines in this way.
french: Même lors de mon règne, très peu de personnes étaient capables de ressentir si bien ces lignes telluriques.
russian: Даже во времена моего правления немногие обладали подобным чутьём.
bulgarian: Even during my reign, there were few able to sense leylines in this way.

english: Take pride in it, my disciple.
french: Soyez-en fière, chère disciple.
russian: Можешь гордиться этим, послушница.
bulgarian: Take pride in it, my disciple.

english: Oh.
french: Oh.
bulgarian: Oh.

english: I... I will!
french: Très... très fière !
russian: Непременно!
bulgarian: I... I will!

english: I have been curious... Are you able to sense the leylines in Mistria clearly, my disciple?
french: Quelque chose pique ma curiosité... Ressentez-vous nettement les lignes telluriques qui existent à Mistria, chère disciple ?
russian: Мне стало интересно... Насколько чётко ты чувствуешь магические жилы в Мистрии, моя послушница?
bulgarian: I have been curious... Are you able to sense the leylines in Mistria clearly, my disciple?

english: Dozy?
french: Dozy ?
russian: Дрёма?
bulgarian: Dozy?

english: Contrary to his name, he dozes sparingly and works quite vigorously.
french: Il ne dort que très peu et travaille avec diligence.
russian: Вопреки такому имени, он не так часто дремлет и весьма энергично работает.
bulgarian: Contrary to his name, he dozes sparingly and works quite vigorously.

english: Whereas you...
french: Tandis que vous...
russian: А что касается тебя...
bulgarian: Whereas you...

english: I'm not switching names with Dozy!
french: Je n'échangerai pas ma place avec celle de Dozy !
russian: Я не буду меняться с ним именами!
bulgarian: I'm not switching names with Dozy!

english: Your familiar.
french: Votre animal de compagnie.
russian: Твой фамильяр.
bulgarian: Your familiar.

english: Floral, yet somehow... dark.
french: C'est fleuri, tout en étant... ténébreux.
russian: Цветочный, но каким-то образом... тёмный.
bulgarian: Floral, yet somehow... dark.

english: I could make one... let me think on what might complement it.
french: Je peux en concocter... mais je dois réfléchir à ce qui irait bien avec.
russian: Я могу сделать... Сейчас придумаю, чем её лучше дополнить.
bulgarian: I could make one... let me think on what might complement it.

english: It is wise that you possess talents beyond magic, Juniper.
french: C'est très sage de votre part d'avoir développé des talents autres que ceux de la magie, Juniper.
russian: Иметь таланты помимо магии мудро с твоей стороны, Джунипер.
bulgarian: It is wise that you possess talents beyond magic, Juniper.

english: A single-minded fervor is well and good, but diversions breed insight.
french: Il est bon de se dévouer corps et âme à une passion, mais la diversité ouvre l'esprit.
russian: Одержимость своей целью — это похвально, однако озарение рождается из отвлечений.
bulgarian: A single-minded fervor is well and good, but diversions breed insight.

english: Do you have a bath oil that utilizes the =Night Queen=, Juniper? The smell pleases me.
french: Juniper, avez-vous une huile de bain à base de =fleur de lune= ? J'aime cet arôme.
russian: У тебя есть масло для ванн с =царицей ночи=, Джунипер? Мне нравится её аромат.
bulgarian: Do you have a bath oil that utilizes the =Night Queen=, Juniper? The smell pleases me.

english: Er. Your Holiness?
french: Euh. Votre Excellence ?
russian: Эм... Ваше святейшество?
bulgarian: Er. Your Holiness?

english: Um... what is the appropriate way for me to address you?
french: Hum... Quelle est la façon la plus appropriée de s'adresser à vous ?
russian: Эм... Как мне следует к вам обращаться?
bulgarian: Um... what is the appropriate way for me to address you?

english: Unholy Dragon Seridia? The Witch Queen? Perhaps Dark Goddess?
french: Seridia, le dragon impie ? La Reine-sorcière ? Ou la Déesse des ombres, peut-être ?
russian: Нечестивый дракон Серидия? Королева-ведьма? Быть может, тёмная богиня?
bulgarian: Unholy Dragon Seridia? The Witch Queen? Perhaps Dark Goddess?

english: I have gone by all these names and more, my disciple.
french: J'ai en effet porté tous ces noms, et bien d'autres, chère disciple.
russian: Я использовала все эти имена, моя послушница, и многие другие.
bulgarian: I have gone by all these names and more, my disciple.

english: For the time being, I have agreed to forgo such titles.
french: Mais pour le moment, j'ai accepté de renoncer à tous ces titres.
russian: В настоящее время я согласилась отказаться от этих титулов.
bulgarian: For the time being, I have agreed to forgo such titles.

english: You will call me Seridia.
french: Vous pouvez m'appeler Seridia.
russian: Ты будешь звать меня Серидия.
bulgarian: You will call me Seridia.

english: Y-your Majesty...
french: V-Votre Majesté...
russian: В-ваше величество...
bulgarian: Y-your Majesty...

english: I scoured them searching for clues about the Witch Queen...
french: Je les ai fouillées tant et plus pour trouver des informations concernant la Reine-sorcière...
russian: Я много раз обыскивала их в поисках знаний о королеве-ведьме...
bulgarian: I scoured them searching for clues about the Witch Queen...

english: And lo, she has appeared.
french: Et voilà qu'elle est apparue.
russian: И вот — она перед тобой!
bulgarian: And lo, she has appeared.

english: Thanks to [Ari], I would say. <he>He has</he><she>She has</she><they>They have</they><it>It has</it><none>[Ari] has</none> been full of surprises, to say the least.
french: Je dirais que c'est grâce à [Ari]. <he>Il</he><she>Elle</she><they>Iel</they> réserve de nombreuses surprises, c'est le moins qu'on puisse dire.
russian:
Должна заметить, что мне

помогли

помоглапомогпомогло [Ari]. Порой

они совершают

она совершаетон совершаетоно совершает невероятные вещи.
bulgarian: Thanks to [Ari], I would say. <he>He has</he><she>She has</she><they>They have</they><it>It has</it><none>[Ari] has</none> been full of surprises, to say the least.

english: You seem familiar with these ruins, my disciple.
french: Vous semblez bien connaître ces ruines, chère disciple.
russian: Моя послушница, ты, как я вижу, знакома с этими руинами.
bulgarian: You seem familiar with these ruins, my disciple.

english: To think, she lived in Mistria's backyard all along!
french: Quand je pense qu'elle vivait à quelques pas de Mistria !
russian: Подумать только: всё это время он был на задворках Мистрии!
bulgarian: To think, she lived in Mistria's backyard all along!

english: Well, I would call this more of a summer home...
french: Eh bien, je dirais qu'il s'agissait plutôt de ma résidence secondaire...
russian: Ну, я бы, скорее, назвала это летней резиденцией...
bulgarian: Well, I would call this more of a summer home...

english: So the mystery stands...
french: Alors, le mystère demeure...
russian: Так значит, эта загадка ещё не разгадана...
bulgarian: So the mystery stands...

english: The location of the Witch Queen's palace was a mystery for the ages...
french: L'emplacement du palais de la Reine-Sorcière est resté un mystère durant des siècles...
russian: Местоположение дворца королевы-ведьмы веками оставалось загадкой...
bulgarian: The location of the Witch Queen's palace was a mystery for the ages...

english: It stands to reason. I have resumed my research and experimentation of magic...
french: C'est logique. J'ai repris mes recherches et mes expériences sur la magie...
russian: Это вполне объяснимо. Я возобновила свои исследования и эксперименты в области магии...
bulgarian: It stands to reason. I have resumed my research and experimentation of magic...

english: It pleases me to make the leylines sing again.
french: J'aime faire à nouveau résonner ces lignes telluriques...
russian: Приятно, что магические жилы снова запели.
bulgarian: It pleases me to make the leylines sing again.

english: Ever since your return, the leyline that runs through these ruins has been very active.
french: Depuis votre retour, les lignes telluriques qui parcourent ces ruines sont très actives.
russian: С тех пор, как ты вернулась, магические жилы в этих руинах необыкновенно активизировались.
bulgarian: Ever since your return, the leyline that runs through these ruins has been very active.

english: You know... I can't say I've given it much thought. I'm more of a dog person.
french: Mmm... Je n'y ai jamais vraiment réfléchi. En réalité, je préfère les chiens.
russian: Знаешь... Не думаю, что я об этом задумывалась. Я больше собак люблю.
bulgarian: You know... I can't say I've given it much thought. I'm more of a dog person.

english: What do you think, Juniper? Do you have a favorite fish?
french: Dis-moi, Juniper, quel est ton poisson préféré ?
russian: Как думаешь, Джунипер, есть у тебя любимая рыба?
bulgarian: What do you think, Juniper? Do you have a favorite fish?

english: That's very deep, Terithia.
french: C'est très profond, Terithia.
russian: Это было глубоко, Теризия.
bulgarian: That's very deep, Terithia.

english: If you think about it, fish are always in the Bathhouse... of life.
french: Quand on y pense, les poissons nagent dans le grand bain... de la vie.
russian: Если задуматься, рыбы всегда плавают в купальне... купальне жизни.
bulgarian: If you think about it, fish are always in the Bathhouse... of life.

english: KYA HA HA!
french: HÉ HÉ HÉ !
russian: КЯ-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: KYA HA HA!

english: Now, you try it.
french: Vas-y, essaie.
russian: А теперь ты попробуй.
bulgarian: Now, you try it.

english: Okay, here I go. Kya... kya...
french: OK, je me lance. Hé... hé...
russian: Ладно, сейчас. Кя... Кя....
bulgarian: Okay, here I go. Kya... kya...

english: OH HO HO!
french: OH HO HO !
russian: О-ХО-ХО!
bulgarian: OH HO HO!

english: It's like this.
french: Je te montre...
russian: Вот так!
bulgarian: It's like this.

english: Sure! I can show you how to make a nice seaweed extract. But we'll need to add a big fish to get the ambiance just right.
french: Oui ! Je pourrai même te montrer comment faire des extraits d'algues. Et il faudrait aussi ajouter un gros poisson pour compléter l'ambiance.
russian: Давай! Я тебе покажу, как делать экстракт из водорослей. Надо будет ещё добавить рыбы покрупнее, чтобы атмосфера была что надо!
bulgarian: Sure! I can show you how to make a nice seaweed extract. But we'll need to add a big fish to get the ambiance just right.

english: KYA HA HA!
french: HÉ HÉ HÉ !
russian: КЯ-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: KYA HA HA!

english: You want me to add seawater to the baths? So it smells like the ocean?
french: Tu veux que j'ajoute de l'eau de mer dans les bains ? Pour que ça sente les embruns ?
russian: Хочешь, я добавлю в ванну морской воды? Будет пахнуть морем.
bulgarian: You want me to add seawater to the baths? So it smells like the ocean?

english: Juniper, we're outside my clinic.
french: Juniper, on est devant ma clinique.
russian: Джунипер, мы на пороге моей клиники.
bulgarian: Juniper, we're outside my clinic.

english: Are you following me?
french: Tu ne serais pas en train de me suivre ?
russian: Ты за мной следишь?
bulgarian: Are you following me?

english: Don't mind Juniper, that's just her way of being friendly.
french: Ne t'occupe pas de Juniper. C'est sa manière à elle d'être sympa.
russian: Не бойся Джунипер, это она так проявляет расположение.
bulgarian: Don't mind Juniper, that's just her way of being friendly.

english: It's NOT.
french: Mais non.
russian: А вот и нет!
bulgarian: It's NOT.

english: [Ari]! You wouldn't believe what some of the locals are drinking tonight, it's really quite embarrassing.
french: [Ari] ! Si tu voyais ce que certains boivent ce soir, c'en est presque gênant.
russian: [Ari]! Ты не представляешь, что за дрянь тут сегодня наливают. Даже стыдно рассказывать.
bulgarian: [Ari]! You wouldn't believe what some of the locals are drinking tonight, it's really quite embarrassing.

english: I know it was you and Ryis, Landen. You tell me every time we're here.
french: C'était Ryis et toi, Landen. Tu me le dis à chaque fois qu'on vient ici.
russian: Я знаю, что это были вы с Ризом, Ланден. Ты мне это каждый раз говоришь.
bulgarian: I know it was you and Ryis, Landen. You tell me every time we're here.

english: You know it!
french: Ah oui, c'est vrai !
russian: Ещё бы!
bulgarian: You know it!

english: Whoever got this bathhouse fixed up for Juniper did a great job.
french: Je ne sais pas qui a rénové les bains de Juniper, mais c'est du bon boulot !
russian: Те, кто делал Джунипер эту купальню, поработали на славу!
bulgarian: Whoever got this bathhouse fixed up for Juniper did a great job.

english: Ugh. I hope Vera's at the next Saturday Market.
french: Argh. J'espère que Vera sera là au marché, samedi.
russian: Гх. Надеюсь, Вера приедет на Субботний базар.
bulgarian: Ugh. I hope Vera's at the next Saturday Market.

english: Hoho, don't shoot the messenger March, but your roots are showing.
french: Ho ho, ne le prends pas mal, March, mais on voit tes racines.
russian: Хо-хо, не стреляй в гонца, Март, но скажу тебе: у тебя корни отросли.
bulgarian: Hoho, don't shoot the messenger March, but your roots are showing.

english: A second career? Tempting, but then I'd have to retire all over again!
french: Une deuxième carrière ? C'est tentant, mais il faudrait que je parte à nouveau en retraite après !
russian: Вторая работа? Заманчиво, но тогда придётся второй раз уходить на пенсию!
bulgarian: A second career? Tempting, but then I'd have to retire all over again!

english: Have you ever thought about being a blacksmith, Landen? You've got the attention to detail.
french: Tu n'as jamais pensé à devenir forgeron, Landen ? Tu as l'œil pour les détails.
russian: Вы когда-нибудь думали стать кузнецом, Ланден? Со внимательностью у вас всё в порядке.
bulgarian: Have you ever thought about being a blacksmith, Landen? You've got the attention to detail.

english: Landen, you've described literally everything at our shop.
french: Landen, ta description correspond à presque tout ce qu'on a dans l'atelier.
russian: Ланден, ваше описание подходит ко всем нашим товарам.
bulgarian: Landen, you've described literally everything at our shop.

english: Hey March, I'm looking for one of those... uh... things. The metal things. With the... the bits. You know!
french: Salut, March. Je cherche un... euh... un truc en métal. Qui fait... comme ça et comme ça. Tu vois, quoi !
russian: Слушай, Март, мне нужна эта... такая штука. Металлическая. Она ещё как бы... с ручкой. В общем, ты понял!
bulgarian: Hey March, I'm looking for one of those... uh... things. The metal things. With the... the bits. You know!

english: I'd be the best carpenter in Mistria, if I wasn't so busy being the blacksmith.
french: Et moi, je serais le meilleur menuisier de Mistria si je n'étais pas occupé à la forge.
russian: А я был бы лучшим столяром в Мистрии, если бы только не был занят кузницей.
bulgarian: I'd be the best carpenter in Mistria, if I wasn't so busy being the blacksmith.

english: Don't worry, [Ari]. This is how you know March and Uncle Landen are friends.
french: Détends-toi, [Ari]. C'est la preuve que March et oncle Landen s'entendent bien.
russian: Не переживай, [Ari]. Это Ланден и Март просто так дружат.
bulgarian: Don't worry, [Ari]. This is how you know March and Uncle Landen are friends.

english: I'm just saying, March... I'd make a pretty good blacksmith. Might even teach you a thing or two!
french: Tu sais quoi, March...? Je ferais sûrement un bon forgeron. Je pourrais même t'apprendre deux ou trois choses !
russian: Просто замечу, Март... Я мог бы быть неплохим кузнецом. Может, даже тебя научил бы паре вещей!
bulgarian: I'm just saying, March... I'd make a pretty good blacksmith. Might even teach you a thing or two!

english: What do you prefer for your nails, Ringwald Commons or Foundry Company's Box Nails?
french: Pour les clous, tu préfères ceux des Usines Ringwald ou ceux de la Compagnie du métal ?
russian: Какие гвозди ты предпочитаешь: рингвальдские обычные или тарные от «Плавильщиков»?
bulgarian: What do you prefer for your nails, Ringwald Commons or Foundry Company's Box Nails?

english: I uh, haven't really thought about it.
french: Euh, je n'y ai pas trop réfléchi.
russian:
Я... не

думали

думаладумалдумало об этом.
bulgarian: I uh, haven't really thought about it.

english: Ringwald Commons, of course.
french: Sans hésitations, ceux des Usines Ringwald.
russian: Рингвальдские обычные, конечно!
bulgarian: Ringwald Commons, of course.

english: Well now's the time! I can give you a quick lecture to get you up to speed-
french: Eh bien, tu vois ! Je vais t'expliquer rapidement pourquoi...
russian: Так, пора тебя обучить! Сейчас будет небольшой разъясняющий урок...
bulgarian: Well now's the time! I can give you a quick lecture to get you up to speed-

english: Let's just agree to disagree.
french: Non, on va en rester là.
russian: Давайте каждый останется при своём.
bulgarian: Let's just agree to disagree.

english: I told you two! Even [Ari] agrees with me!
french: Je vous l'avais dit ! Même [Ari] est d'accord avec moi !
russian:
Я же вам говорил! Даже [Ari]

согласны

согласнасогласенсогласно.
bulgarian: I told you two! Even [Ari] agrees with me!

english: When you do enough ornamental work, then you'll see the beauty of the box nail.
french: Quand vous fabriquerez des objets de décoration, vous comprendrez l'intérêt du clou à boîtes.
russian: Если бы вы выделывали орнаменты, как я, вы бы поняли всю прелесть тарного гвоздя!
bulgarian: When you do enough ornamental work, then you'll see the beauty of the box nail.

english: Well look who we have here! Maybe you can help sway our little debate, [Ari].
french: Ah, mais qui voilà ? Tu vas peut-être pouvoir nous départager, [Ari].
russian: Смотрите, кто пришёл! [Ari], может, ты нас рассудишь.
bulgarian: Well look who we have here! Maybe you can help sway our little debate, [Ari].

english: Naturally.
french: Évidemment.
russian: Естественно.
bulgarian: Naturally.

english: He says that, [Ari], but he was agonizing over the measurements.
french: Il fait son intéressant, [Ari], mais il en a bavé avec les mesures.
russian: Это он сейчас так говорит, [Ari], но с примеркой он попотел как следует.
bulgarian: He says that, [Ari], but he was agonizing over the measurements.

english: Look at that! These brackets you made are a perfect fit, March.
french: Mazette ! Les équerres que tu as fabriquées s'emboîtent parfaitement., March.
russian: Смотрите-ка! Твои скобы идеально вписываются, Март!
bulgarian: Look at that! These brackets you made are a perfect fit, March.

english: Oh of course, Landen! Always happy to help.
french: Bien sûr, Landen ! Si je peux t'aider...
russian: Конечно, Ланден! Я только рада помочь.
bulgarian: Oh of course, Landen! Always happy to help.

english: I was wondering if you could go over the woodshop's ledger, Nora! I think I mostly got it right, but your expertise is always appreciated.
french: Est-ce que tu pourrais vérifier la comptabilité de la menuiserie, Nora ? Je crois que je n'ai pas fait de bêtise, mais c'est toujours mieux qu'une spécialiste jette un coup d'œil.
russian: Нора, хотел спросить, ты не могла бы проверить нашу бухгалтерию? По-моему, у меня всё в порядке, но твоё экспертное мнение не помешает.
bulgarian: I was wondering if you could go over the woodshop's ledger, Nora! I think I mostly got it right, but your expertise is always appreciated.

english: Thanks, Landen! We'll just keep the light stuff on it for now.
french: Merci, Landen ! On ne stockera que des choses légères dessus en attendant.
russian: Спасибо, Ланден! Мы пока не будем ставить туда ничего тяжёлого.
bulgarian: Thanks, Landen! We'll just keep the light stuff on it for now.

english: I can ask Ryis to come by and take a look at your shelf! It shouldn't wiggle like that.
french: Je peux demander à Ryis de passer voir ton présentoir ! Il ne devrait pas bouger normalement.
russian: Я могу попросить Риза зайти и осмотреть твой шкаф. Он не должен так шататься.
bulgarian: I can ask Ryis to come by and take a look at your shelf! It shouldn't wiggle like that.

english: Well now! Yes and no, I'd say.
french: Eh bien... Oui et non, je dirais.
russian: А как же! Я бы сказал: и да и нет.
bulgarian: Well now! Yes and no, I'd say.

english: The details change, but folks always need things built!
french: Les techniques évoluent, mais les gens ont toujours besoin de meubles !
russian: Меняются мелочи, но мебель людям нужна всегда!
bulgarian: The details change, but folks always need things built!

english: Uncle Landen, has a lot about the job changed since you were my age?
french: Oncle Landen, le métier a beaucoup changé depuis l'époque où tu avais mon âge ?
russian: Дядя Ланден, сильно наше ремесло изменилось с твоей молодости?
bulgarian: Uncle Landen, has a lot about the job changed since you were my age?

english: Sure do! Don't work so hard that you don't leave time for stuff like romance!
french: Bien sûr ! Ne travaille pas au point d'en oublier les rencontres !
russian: Конечно! Работай в меру, чтобы осталось время для всяких штук вроде романтики.
bulgarian: Sure do! Don't work so hard that you don't leave time for stuff like romance!

english: Uncle, I was asking about the job!
french: Oncle Landen, je te parle du travail !
russian: Дядя, я же про работу спрашиваю!
bulgarian: Uncle, I was asking about the job!

english: Got any advice about the job for me, Uncle Landen?
french: Sur le plan du travail, tu as des conseils à me donner, oncle Landen ?
russian: Можешь дать совет по работе, дядя Ланден?
bulgarian: Got any advice about the job for me, Uncle Landen?

english: Oho, well now! How's that sister of mine doing? She didn't happen to send more of her famous cookies, did she?
french: Ho ho ! Et comment va ma sœur ? Elle n'aurait pas envoyé ses biscuits faits maison par hasard ?
russian: Ого, вот как! Как поживает моя сестричка? Она, случайно, не прислала своего знаменитого печенья?
bulgarian: Oho, well now! How's that sister of mine doing? She didn't happen to send more of her famous cookies, did she?

english: Got a letter from my mom, Uncle Landen! She says hey.
french: J'ai reçu une lettre de maman, oncle Landen ! Elle te passe le bonjour.
russian: Я получил письмо от мамы, дядя Ланден! Она передаёт привет.
bulgarian: Got a letter from my mom, Uncle Landen! She says hey.

english: Nice. I'll drop by the market and chat with her some time.
french: Super. Je passerai la voir au marché.
russian: Отлично. Я как-нибудь зайду на базар и побеседую с ней.
bulgarian: Nice. I'll drop by the market and chat with her some time.

english: Did I tell you? Merri from the Saturday Market sent an inquiry. She had some questions on refinishing furniture.
french: Est-ce que je te l'ai dit ? Merri du marché du samedi m'a contacté. Elle a quelques questions sur la restauration de meubles.
russian: Я не рассказывал? Мэрри с Субботнего базара прислала запрос. Хочет уточнить кое-что насчёт отделки мебели.
bulgarian: Did I tell you? Merri from the Saturday Market sent an inquiry. She had some questions on refinishing furniture.

english: Well, I'll be! Your eye's gotten real good, kiddo.
french: Oui, tu as raison ! Bien vu, Ryis.
russian: Ничего себе! Глаз у тебя уже намётан, парень.
bulgarian: Well, I'll be! Your eye's gotten real good, kiddo.

english: I don't know, Uncle Landen... the lumber we've got on hand is too soft for a project like this.
french: Je ne sais pas, oncle Landen... Ce bois me paraît trop tendre pour ce genre de meuble.
russian: Не знаю, дядя Ланден... Древесина, которая у нас есть, для такой работы слишком мягкая.
bulgarian: I don't know, Uncle Landen... the lumber we've got on hand is too soft for a project like this.

english: Oh! I thought we'd have to start all over. Thanks, Uncle Landen!
french: Oh ! Je croyais que j'allais devoir tout recommencer. Merci, oncle Landen !
russian: Ох! Я уж думал, придётся с нуля переделывать. Спасибо, дядя Ланден!
bulgarian: Oh! I thought we'd have to start all over. Thanks, Uncle Landen!

english: Now don't fret, nephew of mine. All you need is an extra anchor point, hereabouts.
french: Pas de panique, Ryis. Il faudrait juste ajouter un point d'attache ici.
russian: Ну не кисни, дорогой племянник. Надо просто добавить ещё крепление, примерно вот тут.
bulgarian: Now don't fret, nephew of mine. All you need is an extra anchor point, hereabouts.

english: You young folk have done a bang-up job fixing it up after the earthquake!
french: Vous avez fait un boulot impressionnant pour tout remettre en état après le tremblement de terre, les jeunes !
russian: Вы, молодёжь, резво справляетесь с восстановлением после землетрясения!
bulgarian: You young folk have done a bang-up job fixing it up after the earthquake!

english: Great work to the lot of you! That includes you, [Ari]!
french: Je vous tire mon chapeau ! Et à toi aussi, [Ari] !
russian: Отличная работа, ребята! Я это и про тебя, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Great work to the lot of you! That includes you, [Ari]!

english: So how do you feel about the condition of the town these days, Uncle Landen?
french: Alors, que penses-tu de la ville ces temps-ci, oncle Landen ?
russian: Что думаешь насчёт состояния нашего города, дядя Ланден?
bulgarian: So how do you feel about the condition of the town these days, Uncle Landen?

english: What a question! Why, I suppose I never kept track.
french: Tiens, bonne question ! Je n'ai jamais vraiment compté.
russian: Ну и вопрос! По-моему, я никогда не считала.
bulgarian: What a question! Why, I suppose I never kept track.

english: Should I start counting now?
french: Tu crois que je devrais commencer ?
russian: Думаешь, стоит начать?
bulgarian: Should I start counting now?

english: How many fish do you think you've caught in your life?
french: À ton avis, tu as pêché combien de poissons dans ta vie ?
russian: Как ты думаешь, сколько рыб ты поймала за свою жизнь?
bulgarian: How many fish do you think you've caught in your life?

english: Oh, hush up and give me another bite!
french: Oh, veux-tu bien arrêter et me donner une autre bouchée ?
russian: Ой, помолчи, дай откусить ещё кусочек!
bulgarian: Oh, hush up and give me another bite!

english: KYA HA HA!
french: HÉ HÉ HÉ !
russian: КЯ-ХА-ХА!
bulgarian: KYA HA HA!

english: So when you said I should try the special, you meant you wanna eat off my plate!
french: Quand tu m'as dit de prendre le plat du jour, c'était pour piquer dans mon assiette !
russian: Я понял! Когда ты говорила попробовать блюдо дня, ты просто хотела поесть за мой счёт!
bulgarian: So when you said I should try the special, you meant you wanna eat off my plate!

english: I sure don't! There's all kinds of fish that only come out in the winter!
french: Un peu, mon neveu ! Certaines espèces ne sont là qu'en hiver !
russian: Всегда! А зимой есть множество рыб, которые больше никогда не показываются!
bulgarian: I sure don't! There's all kinds of fish that only come out in the winter!

english: You don't stop fishing? Even in the winter?
french: Tu pêches toute l'année, même en hiver ?
russian: Ты всегда рыбачишь? Даже зимой?
bulgarian: You don't stop fishing? Even in the winter?

english: Ryis says the same thing. Just say the word and we'll add one to the Clinic!
french: Ryis est du même avis. Si tu veux, on peut en faire un pour la clinique !
russian: Риз говорит так же. Только скажи — мы тебе и в клинике крыльцо сделаем!
bulgarian: Ryis says the same thing. Just say the word and we'll add one to the Clinic!

english: I must say, you've got a good thing going with this porch. It's quite nice to look out at the trees like this.
french: J'avoue que ce porche me plaît beaucoup. C'est agréable de regarder les arbres d'ici.
russian: Должна сказать, у вас в доме отличное крыльцо. С него такой приятный вид на деревья.
bulgarian: I must say, you've got a good thing going with this porch. It's quite nice to look out at the trees like this.

english: And my father patched you up?
french: Et c'est mon père qui t'a soigné ?
russian: И мой отец вас залатал?
bulgarian: And my father patched you up?

english: And I patched up the cart! Ha ha ha!
french: Et moi, je m'occupais du chariot ! Ha ha ha !
russian: А я залатал телегу! Ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: And I patched up the cart! Ha ha ha!

english: And then I went over the cliff, cart and all! Took quite a tumble.
french: Et là, je suis tombé de la falaise avec mon chariot ! C'était une sacrée chute.
russian: И тут я полетел под гору вместе с телегой! Ещё и перевернулся пару раз.
bulgarian: And then I went over the cliff, cart and all! Took quite a tumble.

english: Insect!
french: Des insectes !
russian: Насекомых!
bulgarian: Insect!

english: Don't talk back to your Queen!
french: On en répond pas à sa reine !
russian: Не перечить королеве!
bulgarian: Don't talk back to your Queen!

english: Arise, Sir Luc. I dub thee, my Royal Bug Guy.
french: Sire Luc, je te nomme Expert royal des bestioles.
russian: Встань, сэр Люк. Я нарекаю тебя своим Королевским ловцом жуков.
bulgarian: Arise, Sir Luc. I dub thee, my Royal Bug Guy.

english: Inspecting the swingset to make sure it's safe.
french: On inspecte la balançoire pour être sûrs qu'elle est sans danger.
russian: Проверяем качели на безопасность.
bulgarian: Inspecting the swingset to make sure it's safe.

english: We're on official Dragonguard business, [Ari].
french: On est en mission pour la Garde des dragons, [Ari].
russian: [Ari], у нас тут серьёзное задание Драконьей стражи.
bulgarian: We're on official Dragonguard business, [Ari].
